A verifier that cannot decide leaves the check `Unchecked` with its reason: the turn's budget spent, a brief over the suite's cap (never truncated), a refused or failed call, a reply that is neither verdict. `read_verdict` reads `AGREE` or `OBJECT` as the first word past markdown emphasis, else exactly one of them in capitals; an `AGREE` that writes `OBJECT` in the same breath is no verdict -- an objection is never read away. `Rounds` is the bound: a pass (or an unchecked check) proceeds, the first objection goes back for one revision, the second is surfaced, and asking again throws -- `kMaxRounds` 2, no third round to reach. `validate_artifact` runs an artifact through it (the producer's one revision, re-checked or not; a revision identical to the artifact objected to is the producer standing by it, surfaced without the same question asked twice); `ToolArgChecks` keeps the rounds per tool across a turn's steps. The briefs -- the artifact and the criterion, nothing else -- are `tool_args_brief` (the call, the user's latest message, what the tool does, what is grounds to object), `extraction_brief` (the fixed rubric: a required field empty or unsupported, a name, number, count, date or link differing from the source's, a field the source contradicts; paraphrase is not an error) over `required_fields` read from the schema, and `answer_brief`. `bind_verifier` is the member call: `MemberCalls::call` on the verifier role under the suite's `consult_caps:`, labelled `validate`, spending the same per-turn count consults do.
- [x] **The config unit** (`contracts/config`): a suite's `validate:` -- `verifier` (a role that can answer, `utility` by default, `kDefaultVerifier`), `tool_args` and `extraction` (`on`/`off`), `answers` (`request`, the default, or `always`), each optional and written only when set; `validate_policy` fills the defaults. The loader refuses the root or an embedder as the verifier, a verifier with no member in the suite (named or the default), a seam that is not on or off, an unknown `answers` word or key. The starter config documents it.
- [x] **The tool-argument seam** (`agentloop/loop`): between selection and execution, where a turn has a member-call budget and the active suite turns `tool_args` on, a call of a gated tool (`writes` or `outbound`) is checked before the gate ever sees it. Structure first: the arguments a JSON object, held to the tool's own parameter schema (`validate_against`; a schema that cannot judge is skipped), and to the tool's own `precheck` -- new on `agent::Tool`, set on `edit_file` and `delete_file`, the path an existing file inside the root -- which only validation runs; dispatch never does. Round one's objection is the call's result -- `Not run: before delete_file ran, utility (l3b) checked it and objected -- …` -- and it does not run; the model's next call of that tool is the revision, checked again, and runs after a pass or, still objected to, with the dispute said first (`validate: delete_file {"path":…} runs as the model revised it, over utility (l3b)'s objection -- …`); the same call made again runs over the objection without asking twice. A call that runs goes through the permission gate exactly as any call does.
- [x] **The extraction seam** (`knowledge/clerk`, `operations/knowledge_core`): `run_capture` takes a verifier; a draft that passed its structure (the schema, then the record's own validation) is checked against the source as the clerk wrote it, before any override (the user's own word); an objection goes back to the clerk once (`revision_message`: the source, its record, the objection), the revision is re-checked, and one still objected to is kept as the clerk wrote it with the dispute in `Draft::validation` -- never silently overridden either way. `draft_capture` opens a member-call turn of its own when the active suite turns `extraction` on, so `knowledge capture` (and `--dry-run`), chat's `/capture` and `POST /v1/admin/knowledge/capture` share it; `CaptureResult::validation` reaches the CLI's report (lines on stderr; `validation` in `--json`), chat's `/capture` lines, and both admin envelopes.
- [x] **The answer seam**: `check_answer` asks the verifier once with the question and the answer; on an objection the producer answers it once (`answer_objection`: a side request over a copy of the conversation, the transcript untouched), and the two positions are said. **`/check`** in chat runs it on the last answer in a member-call turn of its own, under the suite's verifier -- the `validate:` block's, else the utility member, so it works under any suite with that member -- and says why when it cannot (no suite, no member, no answer yet). **`validate: {answers: always}`** runs it in the loop after every answer (a structured answer is held by its schema and a side run is never checked).
- [x] **The surfaces**: `chat` (terminal and machine mode) and `complete` (both paths) now hand the loop their `MemberCalls` on every run, tools or not, so the seams reach wherever a turn has a member-call budget; with no suite, no block, or a seam off, nothing changes. A pass is the side call's line in the thinking block (`validate — asking utility (l3b): Check a tool call before it runs: …`); an objection, a dispute and a check that could not be made are kept lines (`Reporter::on_notice`) -- in machine mode `notice` events, no new event type.
- [x] **The writers and the doctor**: `config add-suite`/`set-suite` take `--verifier ROLE` (`""` for the default) and `--validate SEAM=VALUE`, repeatable for real (`TakeAll`; `SEAM=` resets a seam, `off` clears the block), each change spliced in place by `set_suite_validate` through the one editor; `config get suites.<name>.validate`; the verifier held local and unmetered by asking its provider (`validate_suite_validation`, run wherever 27f's consult rule runs -- the verbs, the admin twins, the member route); the admin twin `PUT /v1/admin/suites/{id}/validate` and `validate` in the suite's shape and in `POST`/`PUT` (82 routes, 74 admin); `check`'s suite row names the seams (`· validate: tool_args, answers always (verifier utility)`) and fails a billed verifier.
- [x] **Tests**: `validate_test` (the verdict table; cheap first by call count; every degradation said; `Rounds` throwing past its last round; `validate_artifact`'s and `ToolArgChecks`' rounds by count; the briefs and the surfaced lines golden; the policy; the verifier as a member call on the consult budget; through the loop, `answers: always`), `tool_args_validation_test` (AC1 on the real filesystem tools, the gate compared request for request with a control run; structure catching a missing path and a schema breach with no model; the model insisting; a verifier that objects to everything outlasted; validation off byte-identical; a read-only tool unchecked; the budget spent by a consult), `clerk_test` (AC2 by count; the planted link revised and agreed; a clerk standing by it; a revision failing its structure; the clerk's record checked, not the overrides), `config_test`, `config_edit_test`, `operations/suites_test`, `config_cmd_test` (`--validate` twice in one command), `admin_suites_test` (CLI ↔ HTTP byte-identity), `admin_knowledge_test`, `check_test`, `chat_test` (`/check`, its refusals, `answers: always` in machine mode and on `complete`), `serve_test`; and on the real binary `cli.suites_lifecycle` gains validation.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Which tool calls are checked *(2026-10-05)* | Gated tools only -- `writes` or `outbound` | The spec's examples (`delete_file`, `run_command`) act; a read costs nothing and its result is its own check, and a verifier call per read would spend the turn's budget on nothing. |
| What a revision of a tool call is *(2026-10-05)* | The model's next call of the same tool in the turn; settled after round two, so a later call is a new artifact | The revision arrives as a later step; the counter has to live in the loop (`ToolArgChecks`), and per tool is the unit the model revises. |
| Validation and the gate *(2026-10-05)* | Validation first; round one's objection never reaches the gate; a call that runs is gated exactly as before, a dispute said before any prompt | "Gates execution, not permission": the person asked sees the dispute, and an objected call never costs a prompt. Held by comparing the gate's requests with a control run. |
| The structural floor for tool calls *(2026-10-05)* | A JSON object, the tool's own schema, and an optional `agent::Tool::precheck` (`edit_file`, `delete_file`: the file exists) | The spec's "schema parses, path-existence"; a precheck the tool declares keeps tool knowledge in the tool, and dispatch never running it keeps validation off byte-identical. |
| The answer seam's rounds *(2026-10-05)* | The verifier once; on an objection the producer answers once, unverified, and both are shown | The acceptance criterion pins `/check` at one verifier call; an answer is already the user's to read, so the producer's reply stands beside the objection and the user decides. Tool calls and records are re-checked in round two, because there a passing revision should proceed quietly. |
| A record still disputed *(2026-10-05)* | Kept as the clerk wrote it, the dispute beside it; the capture proceeds | The spec's rule for tool calls ("runs after a clean pass or the round limit with the dispute shown") carried over: refusing to store would make the verifier an override, which "never a silent override" rules out both ways. |
| What the extraction verifier checks *(2026-10-05)* | The clerk's record before the user's overrides | An override is the user already knowing the answer; the producer's work is what is under check. |
| Which extraction sites *(2026-10-05)* | Capture -- the CLI, chat's `/capture`, the admin twin -- through the one core; not `refine` or graph extraction | `refine` is the user's own instruction-driven revision; graph extraction is a bulk per-chunk build, the "harness-internal" class the spec puts out of scope. |
| `/check` without a block *(2026-10-05)* | Works under any suite with a member for the verifier role (utility by default) | `/check` is the user's explicit request each time; the block's seams are what is opt-in. Without a suite or that member it says so and asks nobody. |
| `/check` in machine mode *(2026-10-05)* | Not built: a driver gets `answers: always` | Machine mode has no slash commands (`/capture` has no twin either); a driver message for it would be a protocol change of its own. |
| Where the seams reach *(2026-10-05)* | Wherever a turn has a member-call budget: `chat` and `complete`, which now hand it to every run; not `serve`, `analyze`, side runs, or a schema-held answer | 27f's surfaces; a standing answer check needs no tool; "a model is never asked what a grammar already answered". |
| A verifier billed per call *(2026-10-05)* | Refused as a consultable member is -- at config time by its provider's word, at use by `local_only`, and by `check` | A check runs on Apogee's initiative, which never spends. |
| Presentation *(2026-10-05)* | A pass is its side-call line; objections, disputes and unchecked checks are notices (`notice` events in machine mode) | The spec's "existing surfaces": no new event type, and a dispute kept on screen after the thinking block collapses. |
| The extraction rubric *(2026-10-05)* | Revised once on real weights: paraphrase is not an error, and `AGREE` when nothing breaks the rules | The first wording ("matches the source exactly") was read as verbatim by Llama 3.1 8B, which then objected to wording; the pass is recorded below. |
| The verdict reader *(2026-10-05)* | First word, then one capital verdict alone; ambiguous is unread, said, never guessed | A misread `AGREE` is a silent pass; an unread reply degrades to structure with a note. |

**Guardrails, mutation-tested.** 44 mutants, each rebuilt in a copy of the tree (no llama.cpp) and run against its tests -- the wiring ones also against `suites_e2e.sh` -- every one caught; those touched by the late refactors were run again on the final code. One, `SEAM=off` read as on, was caught by the e2e alone, and is now caught by a unit test as well:
- **Cheap first:** a structural failure ignored; the verifier asked before structure; `tool_args` checked with the seam off; answers checked whatever the block says; a record that failed its own validation sent to the verifier; `delete_file`'s precheck answering nothing; the schema check passing anything.
- **The rounds:** a third round, by comparison and by constant; the rounds asked again once over; a producer standing by its artifact, and a model repeating its call, asked again; a surfaced call's round kept open; a tool call's revision nobody could check said as a clean pass, the first objection dropped; a capture's revision never re-checked.
- **The budget:** the spent budget ignored; a spent budget passing silently; a brief over the cap sent anyway.
- **The gate and the reach:** an objected call run as well; a read-only tool checked; a side run validated; a schema-held answer checked.
- **The answer seam:** a pass said as a notice; the revision re-checked; the revision written into history; the producer's revision sent as a turn of the conversation rather than a side request.
- **The extraction seam:** the record checked after the user's overrides; an agreed revision not kept; the seam never opened in the capture core; nested required fields never walked.
- **Config and surfaces:** a verifier with no member loading; any `answers` word loading; the root as verifier; the editor dropping `answers`; a billed verifier written; the verifier left out of the consult rules (the member route); `check` passing a billed verifier; the twin ignoring `verifier`; `--validate` refusing a second occurrence; `SEAM=off` read as on; `chat` and `complete` handing over member calls only with tools; `/check` opening no turn; `/check` writing into the conversation.

**Verified** -- the full suite (`make test`: 100% but the pre-existing pdftotext skip), `format-check`, clang-tidy on every touched file (no finding in a gating class; the new code's own findings fixed -- a recursive schema walk made iterative, a range loop, a flag parser split below the complexity bound, optional accesses made explicit, statics made `constexpr` -- and the rest the touched files' existing style findings and Catch2's test-case complexity), and `cli.suites_lifecycle` on the real binary in a scratch `APOGEE_HOME`: a billed verifier refused at config time with the file unchanged; `--validate` twice in one command; `chat --suite checked --tools --allow delete_file` in a workspace with two notes, the root deleting the wrong one first -- the file survives, the objection is said and is the session's first tool result, and the revision runs and deletes the right one; the same in machine mode (the objection a `notice`, the check a `tool_status`, every event of a known type); `/check` saying both positions with the session holding only the question and the answer; and `knowledge capture --dry-run` (JSON and words) disputing a clerk's planted wrong link after one check, the record kept.

**Real weights** -- the planted-flaw check, one family at a time in a scratch `APOGEE_HOME` whose verifier (`utility`, pinned to an 8K window) points read-only at the owner's GGUF; the producers are scripted mock clerks, one per case, each returning its record and standing by it when asked to revise -- so a caught flaw is surfaced after exactly one verifier call. One `apogee serve --all-backends` per family, the verifier loaded once, each case a draft through `POST /v1/admin/knowledge/capture`. Six planted cases, one field wrong each -- a PR number transposed, a count (four screens for three), a status (`shipped` for an option the conversation dropped), an attribution naming someone absent, a retention period (30 days for 90), a reason the source contradicts -- and two clean controls.

| Family (verifier) | Planted flaw objected to, surfaced in one round | The objection names the fault | Clean controls passed | 8 captures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meta (Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M) | 6 of 6 | 3 of 6 -- the status, attribution and retention cases objected to the intent's wording instead | 0 of 2 | 12 s |
| Qwen (Qwen3-VL-8B Q4_K_M) | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 (the attribution case among complaints about other fields) | 1 of 2 | 13 s |
| Google (Gemma 4 12B Q4_K_M) | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 1 of 2 | 17 s |
| OpenAI (gpt-oss-20b F16) | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 (the status case attributed to the decision field) | 1 of 2 | 18 s |

Every verifier reply was a readable verdict (none unread), each capture 1-4 s with the verifier loaded. The control three families objected to is the same one: a record whose `status: shipped` the source supports only by "Agreed" -- the rubric names the fields but not their meanings, so `shipped` is read literally. A first pass with the rubric's earlier wording is recorded for honesty: Meta objected to all eight, naming the fault in 4 of 6, before the paraphrase rule was added (the other families ran once, on the final wording). The measure is what the spike's default stands on: every family catches a planted fault, and a clean record draws an objection often enough that validation stays opt-in per seam.

**Not verified.** The tool-argument and answer seams on real weights (the guardrail asks for the extraction check; both are held on scripted members at the wire and on the real binary over mocks); the thinking-block line under a pseudo-terminal (the e2e runs piped); a cloud verifier's refusal through its real provider (a mock whose script says it bills); `/check` in machine mode (not built, above); validation under `serve`'s chat routes (not a surface, above).

**Left for the owner.** The extraction rubric could carry each field's meaning from the schema's descriptions (`shipped` meaning chosen or done) -- the one false objection three families shared; measured, not changed, so the brief stays fixed until the owner weighs its cost in tokens. And the 27f findings still stand: repeatable `expected(1)` flags elsewhere (`--context-size`, `--allow`, …) refuse a second occurrence; `BackendConfig::system_prompt` is parsed and never applied.

### 2026-10-06 — `symphonies` (backlog item 27q): named, staged multi-model prompt processes

**Why.** A suite (27d) says *which* models work together; nothing said *how*. The vision's second half (the user, 2026-10-04) is a **symphony**: an input goes in, each member plays a role in a staged prompt process, an output comes out -- declarative, shipped as starters and user-addable, playable from the command line before the interactive surface (27s) or the Orchestrator (27t) exist. Feasibility was mapped onto shipped shapes, not re-spiked: agents are the lifecycle precedent, training pipelines the staged-definition one, and 27f's member call the stage mechanic -- so this item is mostly composition, and its one new invariant is that a stage is the same bounded, brief-only call a consult and a validation make.

**What was built**

- [x] **The definition** (`contracts/config`): `SymphonySpec` -- a name, a description, an input contract (`SymphonyInput`: what the input is, and whether it carries an `image`) and ordered `SymphonyStage`s, each a `name`, a suite **role** (`symphony_role_names()`: every role but `embedding`), a `prompt` template read exactly as written (never `${ENV}`-expanded), an optional `schema` (a JSON Schema as JSON text), `image` (the stage is sent the input's image) and its own `brief_tokens`/`answer_tokens`. One parser reads a `symphonies:` config entry and a spec file alike (`parse_symphony_spec`, the `training.pipelines` precedent): at least one stage; names unique, never `input`, never a YAML keyword; an unknown key refused by name at every level (a `promt:` would otherwise play nothing); and **a backend refused at parse, by name** -- a `backend:` or `model:` key, or a role that is a configured backend's name (`'l3b' is a backend -- a stage names the role it plays …, and the suite decides which backend plays it`), so one definition serves every suite and machine. A commented example joins the starter config.
- [x] **The editor** (`contracts/config_edit`): `append_symphony` and `delete_symphony`, and `render_symphony_spec` for the same text as a spec file -- each writing a definition so the one parser reads back exactly what was written: a single line plain only when safe, several a literal block (clip or strip; an indentation indicator when the first line opens with a space), anything a block cannot carry exactly -- a carriage return, two final newlines, a line of blanks -- double-quoted with escapes. An entry's extent is its own (`symphony_extent`): a line indented under it is its whatever it starts with, so a prompt's `# Heading` is block content on a replace, a delete and an append after it, never a comment that belongs to the next entry -- found by its test, where the generic extent inserted a second entry inside the first one's prompt.
- [x] **The guarded Business module `symphony/`** (`cmake/modules.cmake`: links `agentloop`, `contracts`; `harness.layering`: may include `agentloop/`, `harness/`, `contracts/`, `platform/` and itself, never a backend or a surface). `definition` -- the sources and their order (the starters first, a config entry of the name in a starter's place, then the config's entries, then the user's spec files under the data directory's `symphonies/`, each name once; a starter is its seeded file when present, the user's once it exists, else its compiled-in text); `find_definition` by name or by path; the template grammar (`{{input}}` and an earlier stage's `{{name}}`, nothing else touched, no escape); and `validate`, every reason a definition cannot be played before any model is asked anything -- a malformed template, a variable naming no stage or a later one or itself, a schema that is not a valid draft-07 JSON Schema, an input nobody reads, an input image no stage is given. `runner` -- the stage walk: each stage one `MemberCalls::call` on the caller's open turn, through 27f's `call_member`, on its role resolved by the one chain under the active suite, its brief the rendered template and nothing else; a schema stage's answer held by 26f's grammar on a local member and checked on every member (`validate_against`), threaded on as written; a refusal, a failed member or a schema miss stopping the walk -- `stage 2/2 verify (chat): 'root' gave no answer` -- with no output, never an earlier answer handed back as the symphony's. `view` -- the documents every surface renders.
- [x] **The member call grew, not forked** (`agentloop/member_call`): a `MemberCall` carries a stage's `schema` (asked of the provider through `transient.response_schema`, never written into the brief) and its `images` (parts that open the message ahead of the brief's text, as 26e's describe request orders them), and a call with an image to a member that cannot read one is refused unsent. The consult tool and validation pass neither and are byte-identical on the wire.
- [x] **The starters** (`assets/symphonies/`, compiled in by `scripts/generate_symphony_assets.py` as `contracts/assets_symphonies.cpp`, byte-identical by test, in `bundled_files()` so the one seeding path writes them under the new `symphonies/` layout row): `summarize-verify` (utility summarizes, chat checks and corrects -- output threading), `extract-facts` (one extraction stage held to a schema -- a grammar-held stage), `describe-answer` (vision describes the `--image` with the question in view, chat answers from the description -- a vision stage).
- [x] **`apogee symphonies list|show|create|edit|delete|play`** (`cli/symphonies_cmd`, in the registry; `SYMPHONY` the new name kind, completing the catalog's names and paths; the verbs from the tree). `list` tells `shipped`, `config`, `config (overrides shipped)` and `file` apart with each role chain; `show` prints the input contract and every stage's role, caps, prompt and schema; both take `--output-format json`. `create` takes `--stage NAME:ROLE:PROMPT` (repeatable), `--from` any definition, or writes a one-stage skeleton; `edit` opens a rendering in `$EDITOR` and writes it back through the same scaffold; `delete` removes an entry. **`play <name|path>`** -- the input from `--input` or piped stdin, `--image`, `--suite` for this run -- refuses what the definition cannot take before anything is built, then plays: each stage on M1's busy line while it runs and kept above it once done (`stage 1/2 summarize — asking utility (l3b): … · 1.2 s · 98 tokens`), the kept lines alone on a pipe, nothing under `-q` or JSON; the output on stdout, or one `symphony.play` document. A refusal exits 1, a member's failure or a schema miss 2, Ctrl-C 130.
- [x] **One writer, two surfaces** (`scaffold/symphony`): `create_symphony` renders the definition as its entry, reads it back through the parser with the config's backends named, validates it, and only then writes -- the function `create`, `edit`, `POST` and `PUT` all call. **The admin slice** (`httpserver/admin_symphonies`, five routes, 93 in all, 85 admin): `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/admin/symphonies[/{id}]` the twins of create, edit and delete, byte-identical to the CLI's; `GET /v1/admin/symphonies[/{id}]` the reads, byte for byte what `list`/`show --output-format json` print. `play` has no route -- it runs the host's models on a user's act, CLI-only as training control is (a parity carve-out).
- [x] **Tests**: `contracts/symphony_spec_test` (the parser's every rule and refusal; an eighteen-row round-trip table through the entry and the spec file; the entry's bytes and delete its inverse; the extent; the starters byte for byte), `symphony/definition_test`, `symphony/runner_test` (the wire per stage, threading, the suite deciding placement, every stop named, the schema stage, the vision starter's image to one stage only, the budget, cancellation), `symphony/view_test`, `scaffold/symphony_test`, `cli/symphonies_test`, `httpserver/admin_symphonies_test` (CLI ↔ HTTP byte identity for create, `--from`, edit's twin and delete; the reads byte for byte), `agentloop/member_call_test` (the schema and the image on the wire, the image refusal), the parity table, the route count, the seed count, and on the real binary `cli.symphonies_lifecycle` (`symphonies_e2e.sh`); `cli.install_parity` now requires every install path to seed the starters byte for byte the repository's.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How a stage calls *(2026-10-06)* | `MemberCalls::call` on a turn the play opens (or a caller's), over `call_member` -- the one path, with its gate, narration and cancellation | A second call site, even a thin one, is how the three consumers would come to differ; through `MemberCalls` a play is counted as consults and validation are, which is the seam 27r's aggregate budget and 27t's shared turn need. |
| A play's budget *(2026-10-06)* | One call per stage (`PlayOptions::per_turn` 0); a caller with its own budget passes it | The suite's consult caps bound the *model's* initiative; a user's play of five stages must not be refused at four. |
| Spend *(2026-10-06)* | `play` may reach a billed member (`local_only` off); `PlayOptions::local_only` is the switch a model-initiated play (27t) sets | The spec's "the user's initiative spends"; the model's never does. |
| The member call's shape *(2026-10-06)* | Grown by two fields -- a schema beside the brief, images ahead of it -- with the image refusal in the core | A stage's grammar and picture are part of its brief's delivery; carrying them in the one core keeps consult and validation untouched on the wire and the refusal in one place. |
| A schema stage that misses *(2026-10-06)* | Stops the walk named; no corrective retry | 26f's grammar holds a local member's answer by construction; a retry would be a second generation the definition never asked for, and a member that misses is said, not hidden behind a second try. |
| How a schema is written *(2026-10-06)* | Inline, as JSON text | A definition stays one self-contained unit -- config entry, spec file or starter -- and the text rides the request as written, so a grammar writes the properties in the author's order (26f). |
| Templates *(2026-10-06)* | `{{input}}` and an earlier stage's `{{name}}`; nothing else between braces, no escape | Deterministic and table-tested; a prompt with a stray `{{` is refused at validation rather than played with a hole in it. |
| Where validation lives *(2026-10-06)* | The parse rules (roles, backends, names, keys, caps, a schema that is a JSON object) in the one parser, so a bad entry fails the load like a bad suite; template and schema validity in `symphony::validate`, run by create, edit, play, show and list | The spec's split (`definition.h` validates templates and schemas); the load stays cheap and the business rules stay in Business. |
| Unknown keys *(2026-10-06)* | Refused by name | A typo silently ignored plays the wrong process; 27r adds `play:` beside `role:` where it is refused today. |
| Which roles *(2026-10-06)* | Every suite role but `embedding` | An embedder answers no prompt. |
| What plays by a starter's name *(2026-10-06)* | Its seeded file under `symphonies/` when present, else the compiled-in text; a config entry of the name wins over both | The kits' and agents' precedent: a seeded file is the user's once it exists. A later Apogee that changes a starter leaves an unedited seeded copy in place -- noted for the owner below. |
| Spec files under `symphonies/` *(2026-10-06)* | Play by their name, listed `file`; read-only to Apogee (`delete` refuses them; `edit` makes an entry that stands in) | "Registered by name beside user definitions"; spec files are inputs, the training precedent. |
| `edit` *(2026-10-06)* | `$EDITOR` on the definition rendered as a spec file, read back and written through the scaffold with force; an unchanged file writes nothing; a rename refused | `PUT` is create with force (the agents' twin); writing the edit the same way keeps the twins byte-identical. The cost: a comment *inside* an edited entry does not survive the re-render (the rest of the file's do). `platform::run_foreground`'s one documented exception now names `symphonies edit` beside `agents edit`. |
| Editing a starter *(2026-10-06)* | Makes a config entry of its name that stands in for it, said; `delete` brings the starter back | One rule for the CLI and `PUT`; the starter itself stays the shipped text (or the user's own edit of its seeded file). |
| The admin plane *(2026-10-06)* | Create, edit, delete twinned; list and show served; play a carve-out | ADR 0002's twin rule for writes; the 27j read convention; playing is the host's models on a user's act, CLI-only as training control is. |
| Media *(2026-10-06)* | One image (`--image`, read as `complete --image` reads one), to the stages marked for it | The spec's vision-role starter; audio and video wait for a starter that needs them. |
| A stage's default caps *(2026-10-06)* | 4,096 brief and 1,024 answer tokens; the member's window the ceiling | A play's brief carries its whole input; a consult's 1,024 would refuse an ordinary passage. |
| `--suite` on `play` *(2026-10-06)* | Yes, as `task run` has it; else `models.default_suite` | "The same symphony plays on any suite" is the point of roles; 27d's one-shot rule predates a one-shot whose meaning is the suite. |
| Mutation testing *(2026-10-06)* | In a copy of the tree under the scratch directory, built without llama.cpp | The run's rules keep git read-only, so no worktree. |

**Guardrails, mutation-tested.** 33 mutants, each rebuilt in a copy of the tree (no llama.cpp) and run against its tests -- 32 caught on the first pass, the one survivor caught once its test was strengthened:
- **The call core:** the schema left off the request; the images dropped; the image refusal removed.
- **The walk:** the brief sent as the raw template; an answer not threaded on; the schema stage unchecked; a failed stage played past; the first stage's answer returned as the output; the image sent to every stage; the play's budget the consult default of four; a play held to local members; an input the definition reads not required.
- **The definition:** a later stage's answer allowed; an invalid JSON Schema let through; an unclosed `{{` accepted (caught by the suite's timeout -- the walk never ends); a config entry not standing in for a starter; a seeded starter's file ignored for the compiled-in text.
- **The parser and the editor:** a role that is a backend not named so; a `backend:` key not named so; `embedding` a stage role; a prompt `${ENV}`-expanded; a block always clipped; an append inserted inside the last entry's prompt; and the survivor, a comment at an entry's own indent ending the entry -- no test had a hand-written comment between an entry's lines, caught once one did (the delete and the replace each took the whole entry).
- **The surfaces:** the scaffold unvalidated, or not told the config's backends; the view without its problems; `play` saying nothing, ignoring `--suite`, narrating under JSON; the admin read indented; `PUT` without force; the starters left out of the seed.

**Verified** -- the full suite (`make test`: 100% but the pre-existing pdftotext skip), `format-check`, clang-tidy on every touched file (no finding in a gating class; the new code's own findings fixed -- `validate` and `play` split below the complexity bound, designated initializers, no temporaries in the entry renderer -- the rest the touched files' existing style findings and Catch2's test-case complexity), GCC's library (`gcc-check.py`), and `cli.symphonies_lifecycle` on the real binary in a scratch `APOGEE_HOME`.

**Real weights** -- a scratch `APOGEE_HOME` whose backends point read-only at the owner's GGUFs, one suite per family with `chat`, `utility` and `extraction` all on that family's model, so each play loads it once; nothing else running. One spec file, three stages: `find` (utility) reads meeting minutes holding a planted vault code, `KESTREL-4816`, among distractors and replies with the code alone; `tell` (chat) is given **only stage one's answer** -- never the minutes -- and writes the night guard a sentence; `record` (extraction) records the code and the recipient to a schema (`code`, `for`, nothing else). One `apogee symphonies play … --output-format json` per family.

| Family (model) | Stage one found the code | Stage two carried it (from stage one alone) | Stage three schema-valid, code exact | Play |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meta (Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M) | `KESTREL-4816` | "The night guard, please enter the vault code: KESTREL-4816." | yes (`for`: "The night guard") | 2.1 s |
| Qwen (Qwen3-VL-8B Q4_K_M) | `KESTREL-4816` | "The vault code is KESTREL-4816." | yes (`for`: "unknown recipient") | 3.2 s |
| Google (Gemma 4 12B Q4_K_M) | `KESTREL-4816` | "The vault code is KESTREL-4816." | yes (`for`: "Not specified") | 3.5 s |
| OpenAI (gpt-oss-20b F16) | `KESTREL-4816` | "The vault code is KESTREL-4816." | yes (`for`: "(No recipient specified)") | 4.3 s |

Every family threaded the planted fact through all three stages, and every `record` answer held to its schema (each family's chat format has a grammar for one -- 26f measured all four). Three of four sentences named no recipient, so their records said so rather than inventing one. gpt-oss reported 31 tokens for its eight-character first answer: the harmony format's low-effort reasoning, counted, under reasoning off.

**Not verified.** The vision starter on real weights (its stage is held by a seeing fake on the wire; no family run loaded a projector); `edit` with a person's editor at a terminal (the e2e drives a scripted `$EDITOR`), and the busy line on a terminal (the e2e runs piped; M1's own checks hold the line); a cloud member as a stage; an MLX member; the admin routes over a live `serve` (in process only); Windows (the e2e is POSIX).

**Left for the owner.** A starter changed by a later Apogee leaves an unedited seeded copy under `symphonies/` in place -- seeding is skip-if-present, and starters have no retired-digest refresh as the drivers do -- so the old starter keeps playing until the file is deleted and `check --fix` seeds the new one. And `symphonies edit` re-renders the entry, so a comment written *inside* an entry does not survive an edit (the twin's byte identity chose that).

### 2026-10-06 — `symphony-chaining` (backlog item 27r): composition without a second concept

**Why.** The user's vision (2026-10-04): symphonies chained, the output of one passed into the input of the next. The design that keeps the model small: **a chain is itself a symphony.** Beside a role stage, a stage may `play:` another symphony by name, its output threading onward as a role stage's answer does -- so a chain is defined, listed, created, edited, served and played with the machinery 27q built, and nesting falls out instead of being built. What this item adds is composition's rules and their enforcement: loops refused at definition time naming the loop, a depth cap, one budget across the whole walk, and every failure and narration line saying its position.

**What was built**

- [x] **The `play:` stage kind** (`contracts/config`): `SymphonyStage::play` (a symphony's name) and `input` (a template in the prompt's grammar -- what the played symphony is given as its `{{input}}`; left out, the previous stage's answer, the symphony's own input for the first stage, so stages that each play a symphony chain without a word), `plays()`. A play stage takes `image: true` (the play's image passed on) and nothing a role stage's call carries -- a `role` beside it (`a stage plays a role or a symphony, never both`), a `prompt`, a `schema` or caps are each refused by name, as is an empty `input:` and a role stage's `input:`; a stage with neither is told both ways out. `kSymphonyStageKeys` gains `play` and `input` where 27q left them refused.
- [x] **One static walk** (`contracts/symphony_walk.h/.cpp`, new): `walk_symphony(spec, lookup, max_depth, complete)` refuses a loop -- the symphony's own name, mutual, transitive, one below the root; names case-folded; checked before the depth, so a self-play at the cap is named a loop -- and a nesting past the cap, each with its path (`a → b, stage 2 (two): plays 'a', which is already playing -- a loop, a → b → a; a symphony may not reach itself, directly or through another`; `... plays 'l5', which nests 5 deep -- l1 → l2 → l3 → l4 → l5, and the cap is 4 (symphony_caps.depth)`), and, for a complete lookup, a played name nothing defines. A sound walk reports its depth, one play's member calls (each played symphony counted as often as it is played) and what it reached; a subtree walked clean is remembered and asked again only for its depth. **One walk, four askers, each with its own lookup**: the parser (a definition knowing only itself -- `play:` of its own name refused at parse), the loader (the `symphonies:` entries walked against each other: a loop or a nesting past the cap fails the load like a bad suite; a name no entry defines -- a starter, a spec file -- late-bound, a leaf one level down), and in Business the catalog (every source) at create, edit, show, list and play.
- [x] **`symphony_caps:`** (`SymphonyCaps`, hand-edited like `memory:`): `depth` (the cap, `kSymphonyDepth` 4 unless set), `stage_calls` and `answer_tokens` (one whole play's budget), each a positive number, an unknown key refused by name. The starter config documents a chain and the block, commented (both copies byte-matched).
- [x] **The definition** (`symphony/definition`): `stage_template` (the template a stage renders -- a role stage's prompt, a play stage's input or its default), which validation reads for every stage, so a play stage's input naming a later stage is refused as a prompt's would be; `Catalog` gains `max_depth`, `find` and `lookup`; `walk(spec, catalog)`; and `validate(spec, catalog)` -- the definition's own problems, then the walk's, then each symphony it reaches that cannot be played itself (`'broken', which it plays, cannot be played: stage 1 (a): ...`) and each image a played symphony needs and is not passed, or is passed and does not take. `Found` carries the catalog its definition's plays resolve against, a file named by its path included. `role_chain` says a play stage `play:<name>`.
- [x] **The walk recurses** (`symphony/runner`): `play(spec, catalog, input, calls, options)` -- a play stage renders its template into the played symphony's input, passes the image when marked, and walks that symphony through the same `Walk` on the same `MemberCalls` turn, so its stages are the same `MemberCalls::call`s an inline stage makes, request for request (pinned against the same symphony played alone); its output is the stage's answer. `refusal(spec, catalog, input)` checks the whole walk before the first call -- a late-bound spec file that loops or nests too deep is refused with nothing sent. **One budget**: `PlayOptions::per_turn` counts every call the walk makes on the one turn (0: the walk's own count -- `calls.used()` plus every stage of every symphony reached -- so a play is never refused for its size, 27q's rule carried to the whole walk), checked before each call; `answer_tokens` counts each answer as its provider reports it, else as its text estimates, checked before each call and after each answer; a spent budget stops the walk at its position with its spend (`twice → pair, stage 2/2 second (utility): the play's budget is spent -- 3 of 3 member calls made, 3 answer tokens; the play stops here, with no answer`), the answers discarded (`budget_spent`, `calls`, `tokens`). **Positions**: `stage_position` labels every narration line and every failure in a walk that plays another with the path from the root (`digest → summarize-verify, stage 1/2 summarize`, `outer, stage 2/3 then`); one that plays none reads exactly as 27q's. `failed_stage` names the root's stage the walk stopped in. `StageResult` gains `play` and the played symphony's `stages`. The overloads without a catalog play what 27q played.
- [x] **The surfaces**: `create --play NAME:SYMPHONY[:INPUT]` (repeatable, interleaved with `--stage` in the order written); `list` saying `play:<name>`; `show` printing what each play stage is given and one play's cost (`one play: 5 member calls, one after another, 2 symphonies deep (the cap is 4)`); `play` resolving plays against the found catalog and passing `symphony_caps` as the budget (a spent one exits 1, named, nothing on stdout). The admin twins read a stage's `play` and `input`; the reads judge `problems` against the catalog; a play stage's view is `{name, play, input?, image}`; a chain's play document nests each played symphony's stages inside the stage that played it. The editor writes `play:` and `input:`, and every field a stage holds -- so a stage holding both kinds (a hand-built `POST` body) reads back refused, never as one of them.
- [x] **Tests**: `contracts/symphony_walk_test` (new, 7 cases), `contracts/symphony_spec_test` (+5: the play stage's keys and refusals, its own name at parse, the load's walk, `symphony_caps:`, a play stage's entry bytes; the eighteen-row round-trip table now carries a play stage whose input is each text), `symphony/definition_test` (+3), `symphony/runner_test` (+10), `symphony/view_test` (+2), `scaffold/symphony_test` (+1), `cli/symphonies_test` (+2), `httpserver/admin_symphonies_test` (+1, the chain's CLI ↔ HTTP byte identity), `backends/mock_test` (`{{last_user:json}}`, new in the mock so a schema answer can carry the brief it was sent), and on the real binary `cli.symphonies_lifecycle` extended.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How a play stage is written *(2026-10-06)* | `play: <name>` and an optional `input:` template; left out, the previous stage's answer (the symphony's input for the first) | "The output of one passed into the input of the next" is the vision's own sentence, so the plain chain needs no words; `input:` composes anything else in the grammar a prompt already has. A role stage's `input:` and a play stage's `prompt:` are refused by name, so neither kind is half-read as the other. |
| What a play stage carries *(2026-10-06)* | Its name, `play`, `input`, `image` -- no role, schema or caps | The played symphony's stages make the calls and hold their own schemas and caps; `image: true` passes the play's image on, and a played symphony that needs one and is not passed it (or is passed one it does not take) is refused at validation. |
| Where the walk lives *(2026-10-06)* | `contracts/symphony_walk`, the Data floor beside the parser, called with a lookup by the parser, the loader and Business's catalog | The spec puts the walk in `definition`, and also has the config load refuse cycles -- which the Data floor must do without reaching up. One walk with four lookups keeps "a definition that reaches itself is refused" one rule; `definition` asks it over the catalog. |
| What the load walks *(2026-10-06)* | The `symphonies:` entries against each other; a name no entry defines is late-bound | The loader cannot read spec files or know which seeded starter a user edited; those are walked by the catalog at create, show, list and play start, before any call. |
| The depth cap's home *(2026-10-06)* | `symphony_caps.depth`, top level, hand-edited as `memory:` is; 4 unless set; a symphony that plays none is 1 deep | "Config-adjustable as 27f's caps are", but a definition's validity cannot depend on the active suite, which can change per play (`--suite`); 27f's caps are per suite because the root's initiative is. |
| The budget's defaults *(2026-10-06)* | `stage_calls` unset is the walk's own count; `answer_tokens` unset is none | 27q's decision that a user's play is never refused for its size, carried to the whole walk. The aggregation is what binds: a cap -- the config's, or a caller's turn (27t) -- holds every symphony the walk reaches together, through the one turn's count. |
| When the budget is checked *(2026-10-06)* | Before each call (calls and tokens), and after each answer (tokens); not refused up front from the static count | The spec puts the cap in the walk and has the walk stop where the aggregate crosses it; tokens can only be known as spent, and one rule for both is easier to hold. An answer that crosses the token cap is discarded with the rest. |
| Unreported tokens *(2026-10-06)* | Counted as their text estimates | A member whose provider reports nothing must not play past an answer-token cap for free. |
| Positions *(2026-10-06)* | `outer → inner, stage 2/3 verify` -- the path from the root -- on every line and failure of a walk that plays another; 27q's labels unchanged for one that plays none | 26n's labels extended without moving a single-symphony golden; inside a chain even the root's own stages carry its name (`outer, stage 3/3 final`), so a reader never has to infer whose stage is running. |
| A played name nothing defines *(2026-10-06)* | Refused at create and edit, listed `cannot be played`; deleting a played entry is not refused | The validation rule 27q gave templates; and spec files are late-bound, so a chain may name one that is not there yet only by hand. |
| A loop is judged by name *(2026-10-06)* | A path back to the root's name is a loop whatever the catalog holds under that name | The conservative reading, and what lets the scaffold validate a new or replacing entry against the catalog as it stands: any route back to the candidate is caught on the path. |
| `create` *(2026-10-06)* | `--play NAME:SYMPHONY[:INPUT]`, interleaved with `--stage` in the order written (the command's parse order) | `POST` can express a chain, so its CLI twin must, byte for byte. |
| Mixed stages from a body *(2026-10-06)* | The renderer writes every field a stage holds | A body with both `role` and `play` would otherwise have been rendered as one kind and accepted; written whole, the parser refuses it. |
| No chain starter *(2026-10-06)* | The three starters unchanged; the starter config's commented example shows a chain | A chain needs no new mechanism to ship, and a fourth starter would change the seeded set every install path is held to. |
| Mutation testing *(2026-10-06)* | In a copy of the tree under the scratch directory, built without llama.cpp | The run's rules keep git read-only, so no worktree. |

**Guardrails, mutation-tested.** 49 mutants, each rebuilt in a copy of the tree (no llama.cpp) and run against its tests -- 46 caught on the first pass, two caught once a test was written for them, one found equivalent and removed:
- **The walk:** the loop check removed; names compared case-sensitively; the depth one off; a remembered subtree trusted at any depth; an unknown name accepted by a complete lookup, and a late-bound one refused; calls not multiplied; the height not added.
- **The parser and the load:** a definition's own name not refused at parse; the load's walk removed, and run at the default depth; a role, a prompt beside a play, an input on a role stage accepted; `symphony_caps.depth` and `stage_calls` ignored.
- **The editor:** `play:` or `input:` not written; an empty `role:` written on a play stage.
- **The definition:** a play stage's default input always `{{input}}`; the catalog's walk skipped; a reached symphony's problems ignored; the image boundary unchecked; the config's depth ignored; a path's lookup without the catalog.
- **The runner:** the refusal without the catalog; the budget per symphony (27q's stage count); the call pre-check gone; the token checks gone, after and -- the first survivor, caught once a budget spent exactly to the token was tested -- before; unreported tokens free; the image never passed; the played symphony given the outer input; the play stage's answer its input; labels without positions, and positions on a single symphony; `failed_stage` the inner stage's; a blank rendered input played -- the second survivor, reachable only by a definition built in code (the parser refuses a blank `input:`), caught once tested.
- **The surfaces:** the scaffold validating without the catalog; `play` ignoring `symphony_caps`; `--play` after every `--stage`; `play` without the catalog; the admin body's `play` or `input` ignored; the view's problems without the catalog, its `input` dropped, its play document flat; the mock's `{{last_user:json}}`.
- **Equivalent:** the scaffold's catalog built with the candidate written in -- every path back to the candidate's name is already a loop by name, so the copy changed nothing and was removed.

**Verified** -- the full suite (`make test`: 100% but the pre-existing pdftotext skip), `format-check`, clang-tidy on every touched file (the new code's own findings fixed -- the walk's and the runner's bounded recursion annotated in the tree's `NOLINTNEXTLINE(misc-no-recursion)` form, checked optional access in the command -- the rest the touched files' existing classes and Catch2's test-case complexity), GCC's library (`gcc-check.py`), and `cli.symphonies_lifecycle` on the real binary in a scratch `APOGEE_HOME`: a chain of the two starters created with `--play`, played under a suite whose extraction member answers with the brief it was sent -- that brief extract-facts' template holding summarize-verify's output, each of the three lines naming its position, the document nesting -- a hand-written loop failing the load with its path, spec files four deep played and five refused at play start with no member asked, and `symphony_caps.stage_calls: 3` stopping a two-play chain at its fourth call, exit 1, nothing on stdout.

**Real weights** -- a scratch `APOGEE_HOME` whose backends point read-only at the owner's GGUFs, one suite per family with `chat`, `utility` and `extraction` all on its model; one config entry, `digest`: `summary` plays `summarize-verify`, `facts` plays `extract-facts` (two shipped starters, the second given the first's output). The input: 27q's meeting minutes with the planted vault code `KESTREL-4816`. One `apogee symphonies play digest --suite <family> --output-format json` per family.

| Family (model) | summarize-verify's output (stage one) | extract-facts' record (from stage one alone) | Play |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meta (Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M) | a three-sentence summary carrying `KESTREL-4816` (the attendees dropped) | schema-valid; `"The new vault code is KESTREL-4816."` among five facts; `people` empty -- the summary named none | 8 s |
| Qwen (Qwen3-VL-8B Q4_K_M) | a verdict -- "The summary is accurate ... No corrections or additions are needed." | schema-valid and empty: the verdict states no fact | 4 s |
| Google (Gemma 4 12B Q4_K_M) | a verdict -- "The summary is accurate and includes all key details ..." | schema-valid; four facts about the summary's accuracy | 11 s |
| OpenAI (gpt-oss-20b F16) | the minutes restated, `KESTREL-4816` kept | schema-valid; `"The new vault code is \"KESTREL-4816\"."` among eight facts | 17 s |

Every family threaded stage one's output into stage two exactly: each record is a reading of the summary it was given, not of the minutes -- Llama's lists no people because its summary dropped them, Gemma's records the verdict it was handed. The code reached the record on two of four. On Qwen and Gemma the shipped `summarize-verify`'s verify stage answers with a verdict instead of the corrected summary its prompt asks for, and does so played alone too (rerun on each: the same kind of answer) -- a property of 27q's starter prompt on those families, not of the chain.

**Not verified.** Windows (the e2e is POSIX); the busy line drawing a chain's positions on a terminal (the e2e runs piped; the kept lines are the same strings); a cloud or MLX member inside a chain; the admin routes over a live `serve` (in process only); a chain played inside a turn with consults already spent (no such caller yet -- 27t's; the runner test holds the shared count through `per_turn`).

**Left for the owner.** The `summarize-verify` starter's verify stage, on Qwen3-VL 8B and Gemma 4 12B, replies with a verdict ("the summary is accurate") rather than the final summary, alone or chained -- its prompt ("Reply with the final summary only") is not held by those families; a change to a shipped starter is the owner's call (and an unedited seeded copy stays in place, per 27q's note). The two readings this item chose and recorded above, each a one-place change if vetoed: a play stage's default input is the previous stage's answer, and the budget's defaults leave a play bounded by its own walk until `symphony_caps` says otherwise.

### 2026-10-06 — `execute-mode` (backlog item 27s): a session opened with a suite

**Why.** The user's vision (2026-10-04): "a new mode that is similar to chat called `execute` where instead of starting up a window with a model, you start it up with a suite." 27d made a suite a named unit, 27e priced and held it, 27q and 27r made symphonies playable from the command line -- but a person could not sit in one session with a suite and play its symphonies between ordinary questions. This item is that session: chat's sibling whose unit is the suite, built as a superset of chat for the suite case rather than a second conversation model, so the Orchestrator (27t) lands later as an upgrade -- the root gains symphony tools -- instead of a second loop. Its constraint is the item's whole design: **reuse, never fork**.

**What was built**

- [x] **The session core** (`cli/chat_session.h/.cpp`). Chat's whole session -- the callback that was `ChatCommand::bind`'s body, some thirteen hundred lines: the flags, the suite chosen, priced and held, the providers built once, resume, recall, the tools and their gate, the permission presets, the busy line, the REPL with its one command table and completion, machine mode, the per-turn save, the title, capture -- moved out of `chat.cpp` whole and parameterized by `SessionMode`. `SessionFlags`/`bind_session_flags` declare chat's flags in chat's order; `run_session(context, flags, machine, mode)` runs a session; `parse_slash` moved with it. `chat.cpp` is now a thin face -- bind the flags, run the session as `SessionMode::Chat` -- and chat is the first consumer of its own generalization. **What the mode changes, and nothing else:** the command a refusal is said under (`session_command`: `apogee chat:` / `apogee execute:`); a suite insisted on (below); the banner's symphony count (`session_banner`); the table's execute rows; and in machine mode a `user` line holding `/play`.
- [x] **`apogee execute`** (`cli/execute.h/.cpp`, in the registry beside `chat`): `ExecuteCommand` -- chat's flags, chat's session, as `SessionMode::Execute`; its `--suite` help names no `off`. Bare input converses with the suite's root model exactly as `chat --suite` does: the same `run_chat_turn`, and on mocks byte-identical stdout, stderr and saved conversation.
- [x] **Suite-first.** An execute session's suite is `--suite`, else a resumed session's, else `models.default_suite`. With none it refuses -- before anything is built when no session is resumed, after the session is read when one is -- naming the way to one (`execute_suite_refusal`): the configured suites and `apogee config set-default-suite <name>`, or with none configured `apogee config add-suite <name> --chat <backend> [--utility <backend> ...]`. `--suite off` and `/suite off` are refused (`'apogee chat --suite off' is a session without`); a saved `""` -- a chat that turned its suite off -- resumes under the default rather than off. Then admission, the session hold and `--warm`/`--force` fire exactly as for `chat --suite` (27e): the same lines, from the same code.
- [x] **`/play <symphony> [input]`** (`cli/chat_play.h/.cpp`). `parse_play_argument` reads the first word as the symphony (a name, or a spec file's path, as `find_definition` takes) and the rest of the line, as typed, as its input; `prepare_play` finds the definition among every source and asks `symphony::refusal` before anything is sent -- an unknown name, a symphony that cannot be played, a missing input (`-- /play <symphony> [input]`), one that takes an image (`/play` gives text alone; `'apogee symphonies play <name> --image <file>' plays it with one`). `run_play_turn` plays through 27q/27r's one walk on a turn of the **session's own `MemberCalls`**, the whole walk under `symphony_caps` (`stage_calls`, `answer_tokens`), `local_only` off (the user's initiative spends, as `symphonies play`), `PlayOptions::conversation` the session's backend (so a helper role the suite leaves out falls back as the one chain says); each stage is narrated through `Reporter::on_side_call` -- the terminal's thinking block, machine mode's `tool_status` -- and the output said as the answer (`on_answer_start/token/end`, so the terminal renders its Markdown). **A play is session history**: the line as typed and the output are appended as one ordinary exchange, `turns` counted, recall marked, the session saved at once -- so the next bare question reads it as any earlier answer, and resume, compaction and recall treat it as one. A play that stops is cleared from the status and said, and leaves the session as it was. The REPL wraps it as a turn (the typeahead guard, the spacing, the title asked after it).
- [x] **`/symphonies`**: `symphonies list`'s table, now one function (`symphony_list_lines`, exported from `cli/symphonies_cmd`, the command printing exactly the bytes it did), indented under the prompt, a spec file that cannot be read said.
- [x] **One table, two sessions** (`cli/chat_completer`). Each row carries `SessionRows` (`Every`, `ChatOnly`, `ExecuteOnly`; `offered_in`); `chat_commands(mode)`, `find_chat_command(verb, mode)` and `chat_help_lines(width, mode)` read the rows a session offers, and `ChatCompletionSources` carries the `mode` and the live `symphonies`. Chat's rows and their order are unchanged (its `/suite [name|off]` now `ChatOnly`); execute's own come after the suites': `/suite [name]` (`ArgumentValues::NamedSuites`, no `off`), `/symphonies`, `/play <symphony> [input]` (`ArgumentValues::Symphonies`, the names read live from the session's catalog, the input free text); the new verbs follow `Exit`, under the `-Werror=switch` dispatch. `chat_commands()` returns references into the one table (it was a span), so chat's table tests read unchanged and compare rows by address. In chat, `/play` and `/symphonies` are unknown commands, as they were.
- [x] **Machine mode, through the existing protocol.** In an execute session a `user` line that `parse_slash` reads as a command the table's execute rows offer as `/play` is played: a `tool_status` as each stage starts (`stage 1/2 summarize — asking utility (l3b): …`, a chain's with its position), `answer_start`, the output as `answer_delta`, `answer_end`, and the turn's `result`; one that cannot run ends in an `error` (the reason on stderr too) with nothing kept. Every other line is a prompt, as in chat. **No new event type, and no new input type**: `cli.machine_schema_conformance` reads the same 17 emitted and 3 accepted types. `machine-mode.md` documents the `/play` line and the `execute` command.
- [x] **The banner** names the suite and what the session can play: `l8b  ·  suite meta  ·  3 symphonies  ·  chat <id>  ·  /help for commands` (on a terminal, as chat's is).
- [x] **Completion**: `execute` and its flags from the parser (`__complete execute --`, `--suite` the suites, `--resume` the chats), `execute -s`, `--system` and `--allow-host` on the reviewed free-text list beside chat's; in the session `/play <TAB>` the symphonies, described, and execute's `/suite` without `off`.
- [x] **Tests.** `cli/chat_session_test` (the chat golden, below); `cli/execute_test` (27 cases: the refusals, the default suite, resumed suites, bare input byte-identical to `chat --suite`, `/play` threading stage one into stage two and kept as one exchange, another suite's members, a play-heavy session resumed whole, every refusal and a schema miss with nothing kept, the conversation fallback, `symphony_caps`, recall, `/symphonies` byte for byte `symphonies list`, `/suite`, chat without `/play`, machine mode's events and its `error`, `run_play_turn`'s narration and immediate save, the root sent the play as history on the next turn, the argument, the banner, the table both ways, execute's `/help` golden, `/play`'s completion, every offered symphony played, and the whole surface held to `fixtures/cli/execute_session.golden`); on the real binary `cli.execute_lifecycle` (`execute_e2e.sh`) and an `execute` case in `cli.chat_typeahead_and_crash_safety` (the banner, Tab completing a symphony, the stages in the thinking block collapsing to `Worked for`, the output rendered). Outside chat's battery three tests follow the change: `attachment_guard_test`'s scans read chat's `--image` where it now lives (`chat_session.cpp`) and hold `execute.cpp` and `chat_play.cpp` to the same rules, `lifecycle_test`'s `kFreeText` gains execute's three free-text flags, and `parity_test` classifies `execute` read-only, as `chat` is.

**The chat-unchanged guardrail.** Before a line of the core was moved, `chat_session_test` was written and its golden generated by `chat.cpp` as it stood: `apogee chat` in process through every path the core owns -- a piped REPL with every slash command (`/play` and `/symphonies` among them, unknown), resumed; a suite named, switched, turned off, refused, warmed and resumed; the config's default suite and `--suite off`; machine mode with an attach, an unknown line and a `/play` line that is a prompt; ten launch refusals; `chat --help`; four `__complete chat` lines -- the exit code, stdout and stderr of each, only chat ids and the temporary home normalized (`fixtures/cli/chat_session.golden`, 23 runs in 389 lines). It passes unchanged after the cut, as does every existing chat test (`[chat]`, 140 cases, untouched). And on the real binary: a 23-run battery (piped and machine mode, tools with presets, verbose, every refusal, help and completion) run against the binary built from the commit before and the one after differed in two lines only -- `execute` in `apogee --help` and in `__complete ""`.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the core lives *(2026-10-06)* | `cli/chat_session.h/.cpp`, chat's callback moved whole and parameterized by `SessionMode`; `chat.cpp` and `execute.cpp` thin faces | The spec's "one session/REPL machinery parameterized by mode"; 27h's `run_chat_turn` is the precedent for sharing chat's machinery by moving it. A core in a file of its own keeps chat from looking like the owner of what both commands are. |
| What the mode may change *(2026-10-06)* | The refusal's command name, the suite requirement, the banner's count, the table's rows, machine mode's `/play` line -- nothing else | Every other difference would be a fork by another name; "a fix in chat's core is a fix in execute by construction". |
| Proving chat unchanged *(2026-10-06)* | A golden of chat's whole surface written by the code before the cut, plus a before/after battery on the real binary | The spec's byte-equivalence run; the 27d precedent (`roles_no_suite.golden`, written by the resolver before the rung). Chat's own tests stay untouched. |
| Which suite execute runs under *(2026-10-06)* | `--suite`, else the resumed session's, else the default; none refused naming `set-default-suite` or `add-suite`; `off` refused at launch and by `/suite`; a saved `""` takes the default | "Never silently degrades into plain chat, because the mode's promise is the suite" -- extended to an explicit `off`, the conservative reading: an execute session always has a suite, and `chat` is the session without one. |
| When the refusal fires *(2026-10-06)* | Before anything is built when no session is resumed; after the session is read when one is | The common case costs nothing; a resumed session's suite is only known once it is read. |
| `/play`'s table rows *(2026-10-06)* | `SessionRows` per row in the one table; `chat_commands(mode)` returns references; execute's own `/suite [name]` row; the new verbs after `Exit` | One table (ADR 0007's one resolver per surface) serving two sessions without a second list; chat's rows, order and `/help` bytes unchanged; chat's table tests compile and pass unchanged. |
| `/play` in chat *(2026-10-06)* | Not offered: an unknown command, as before | Chat's surface byte-identical, and playing is execute's promise; a chat user has `symphonies play`. |
| What a play keeps *(2026-10-06)* | The line as typed and the output, one exchange; `turns` counted, recall marked, saved at once; a play that stops keeps nothing | "Plays are session history" -- resumable, compactable, recallable; the typed line is the honest record of what was asked; a failed chat turn keeps nothing either. |
| How a play is said *(2026-10-06)* | Each stage a side call (`on_side_call`), the output an answer (`on_answer_*`) | The spec's "stage narration as the side-call lines are"; the same calls give the terminal its thinking block and rendered answer and machine mode its existing events. |
| Machine mode's `/play` *(2026-10-06)* | A `user` line the table reads as `/play`, found through the table's execute rows; a failure an `error` event, no `result` | "Rides machine mode through the existing protocol": no new input type (the conformance check counts accepted types too); the task run's precedent for a turn that does not finish. |
| A play's options *(2026-10-06)* | `local_only` off; `per_turn`/`answer_tokens` from `symphony_caps`; `conversation` the session's backend; the catalog read at each `/play` from the session's config and the spec files | As `symphonies play` plays one; the conversation fallback is the one chain's; a spec file dropped mid-session plays without a restart. |
| Images *(2026-10-06)* | `/play` gives text alone; a symphony that takes an image is refused naming `symphonies play --image` | The spec's shape is `/play <symphony> [input]`; a flag inside free text would need a parse and a completion of its own. Left for the owner below. |
| The banner's count *(2026-10-06)* | Every definition the catalog holds (what `/symphonies` lists), on a terminal only | One number the user can check against `/symphonies`; chat's banner rule. |
| Session format *(2026-10-06)* | No new field: an execute session is a chat session | One format both commands open (`chat --resume` of an execute session works, and the reverse); the mode is a property of the run, not of the record. |
| `serve` *(2026-10-06)* | Not a surface: `execute` read-only in the parity table | The spec: `serve` is an API, not a session surface; a GUI drives execute over machine mode. |
| SPEC *(2026-10-06)* | Unchanged | Core surfaces item 3, added with the set, describes what was built. |
| Mutation testing *(2026-10-06)* | In the scratch copy of the tree built without llama.cpp | The run's rules keep git read-only, so no worktree. |

**Guardrails, mutation-tested.** 41 mutants, each rebuilt in a copy of the tree (no llama.cpp) and run against the chat, execute, completion, symphonies, attachment-guard and parity suites -- the wiring ones also against `execute_e2e.sh` or the PTY `execute` case -- 40 caught, one found equivalent and the code it guarded removed:
- **Suite-first:** `--suite off` accepted; the refusal for a resumed session with no suite removed; a session turned off resumed off in execute; `/suite off` allowed; every refusal said as `apogee chat:`; execute run as chat.
- **The one table, in the session:** the REPL dispatching through execute's rows in chat (caught by chat's golden) and through chat's in execute; `/help` printing execute's rows in chat (the golden); completion's mode never set and the symphonies never handed to it -- both caught by the PTY case alone, Tab completing nothing after `/play su`.
- **The table itself:** execute's rows offered in chat (chat's own table test); chat's in execute; `find_chat_command` ignoring the mode (the golden); `/help` unfiltered (chat's own test); suggestions ignoring the mode; execute's `/suite` offering `off`; `/play` offered no symphonies; the names and descriptions swapped.
- **Machine mode:** a `/play` line not recognised; its failure's `error` not emitted; its `result` not emitted; the table's gate read as execute's in chat (the golden).
- **The banner:** no count; a count in chat's; a count of nothing (the PTY case).
- **The play:** the line, the output, the answer, the turn count, the immediate save, recall's mark, the conversation fallback, `symphony_caps`, the input, the refusal and its way out each dropped; a play that stopped kept as an exchange; the input cut at its first word; `symphony_list_lines` drifting from `symphonies list`.
- **Equivalent:** the machine-mode branch's own `mode == Execute` test made always true -- the table's lookup already offers `/play` to execute alone, so nothing changed. The redundant test was removed, leaving the table the one gate, and the gate itself then mutated to execute's rows in chat: caught by chat's golden.

**Verified** -- the full suite (`make test`: 100% of 2849 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before), `format-check`, clang-tidy on every touched file (no finding in a gating class; `chat_session.cpp`'s findings are `chat.cpp`'s before the cut, each class the same, and `chat_play.cpp`'s one fixed), GCC's library (`gcc-check.py`: every first-party file), `cli.execute_lifecycle` and the PTY `execute` case on the real binary, and the before/after battery above.

**Real weights** -- a scratch `APOGEE_HOME` per family whose one backend points read-only at the owner's GGUF and answers every role of a one-member suite (so each session loads its model once), recall off (`--no-recall`). One piped `apogee execute --suite <s>` per family: `/play summarize-verify` over meeting minutes holding a planted vault code, `KESTREL-4816`, then a bare question -- "What is the new vault code, and who is to be told?".

| Family (model) | The play (`summarize-verify`'s output) | The bare question, after it | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meta (Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M) | a three-sentence summary carrying `KESTREL-4816` and the night guard | `KESTREL-4816`, only the night guard | 4 s |
| Qwen (Qwen3-VL-8B Q4_K_M) | a summary carrying the code and the night guard | `KESTREL-4816`, effective tonight, only the night guard | 5 s |
| Google (Gemma 4 12B Q4_K_M) | a verdict on the summary ("accurately captures the new vault code…"), as 27r recorded of this starter on Gemma | `KESTREL-4816`, only the night guard | 11 s |
| OpenAI (gpt-oss-20b F16) | a summary carrying the code (`KESTREL‑4816`, a non-breaking hyphen) | `KESTREL-4816`, only the night guard | 8 s |

Every session saved the play and the question as two exchanges, the suite named; each admission line stated its footprint (`suite meta needs 7893 MiB of this machine's 110100 MiB: l8b 6869 + 1024 margin -- fits`). The bare question could read the code from the play's line as typed as well as from its output -- what this run measures is the session, not recall from the summary alone.

**Not verified.** Windows (the e2e and the PTY check are POSIX); machine mode on real weights (held on mocks in process and on the real binary); a cloud or MLX member in a play; Ctrl-C during a play (it ends the process as during a chat turn -- the session saved after the last finished exchange -- not exercised); a chain or `--warm` under execute on real weights (each is chat's or `symphonies play`'s own code, covered there).

**Left for the owner.** `/play` cannot give a symphony an image (`describe-answer` is refused with `symphonies play --image` named); a `--image` after the name, with its completion, would be a small item. The root `README.md` still names three surfaces (complete, chat, serve) -- unchanged here since v0.1.4 is unreleased; the release's docs pass is where it gains `execute`. `SlashOutcome`, an enum nothing uses, moved with `parse_slash` as it was.

### 2026-10-06 — `orchestrator` (backlog item 27t): symphonies as tools

**Why.** The vision's keystone (the user, 2026-10-04): in an execute session, a model "has access to the available symphonies, and can orchestrate what symphonies to play based upon the context." Everything it composes had shipped -- 27q's definitions and runner, 27r's chains and aggregate budget, 27s's session, 27f's bounded member call and per-turn budget, 27g's validation spending from it, 26g's selection, 26n's narration, 26p's registry-composed note -- so the architecture is registration and policy only: **each symphony's definition projects an ordinary tool**, and with orchestration on the root's toolset gains them. The ordinary agent loop is the orchestration engine; the root model of the execute session is the Orchestrator, a framing in its note rather than a second process. The honest risk was never plumbing but small-model judgment, so it ships **opt-in**, with a measured pick rate as the evidence a default-on decision would cite.

**What was built**

- [x] **The projection** (`symphony/tools.h/.cpp`, new, in the guarded Business module -- which now links `agent` for the registry and `harness` for the one role chain, `harness.layering`'s allow-list gaining `agent/`): a definition projects `play_<name>` -- its own description, then what playing it is (`Plays the summarize-verify symphony: 2 member calls on your suite's models, one after another (utility → chat). It sees only the input you give it -- not this conversation, not any file -- so put the whole text it needs there.`) -- with one argument, `input`, a string described as the definition's input contract describes it (`The text the symphony works on` when it says nothing). Ungated: a symphony's stages call no tools (27q), so a play reads, writes and reaches nothing the gate would be asked about. Not projected, with the reason: a symphony that cannot be played (its own problems or its walk's), one that takes an image (a tool call carries text alone, as `/play` does), and one whose tool name would pass 64 characters.
- [x] **The offer** (`orchestra_offer`, `register_play_tools`): under the active suite, each projectable symphony whose **every reached member** -- its role stages and those of every symphony it plays, each resolved through the one chain with the conversation as its fallback (`reached_members`) -- is configured, built in this session, and local and unmetered by its provider's word, and whose whole play fits a turn's budget (`consult_caps.per_turn`) and a play's (`symphony_caps.stage_calls`). The rest are withheld, each with why (`its summarize stage (utility) is 'paid', billed per call -- a play the model starts runs on its initiative, which never spends`). A registry holding a play gains **the Orchestrator framing** in its environment note, composed from the registry asking as 26p's policy is, so a copy narrowed to none says nothing of it: *You are the orchestrator of a suite of models. Each play_ tool plays a symphony: a staged process in which your suite's models work through an input in turn. When a request is the work a symphony is for, play it rather than doing that work yourself -- give it the whole text it needs as its input, since it sees nothing else -- then answer the user from its output. Anything else, answer yourself, without a tool.* (under 512 bytes).
- [x] **A play the model starts** (`make_play_tool`): the input checked (required, not blank -- an error the model can correct); then the budget, before anything is sent -- the turn's member calls are the suite's `consult_caps.per_turn`, which consults and validation already spend (27f, 27g), and a play whose static count cannot fit what is left, or `symphony_caps.stage_calls`, is refused before its first call (`Not played: this turn's member-call budget has 0 of 4 calls left -- plays, consults and checks share it -- and a play of extract-facts makes 1. Answer without it.`) -- every stage is called unless one fails, so the static count is exactly what a play that finishes spends, and the refusal never turns away one that could have finished. Then 27q/27r's one walk on the turn's own `MemberCalls`, with `PlayOptions::local_only` on (a billed member is refused at the stage whatever the offer said), `per_turn` the turn's budget, `answer_tokens` the play's, the conversation's backend the helper fallback. The output comes back as an ordinary tool result in consult's shape, `summarize-verify answered:` and the output; a refusal or a spent budget is a result the model reads (`Not played: …`), a member's failure an error result.
- [x] **Narrated, always**: `[tool] play_summarize-verify` from dispatch as for any tool, then the **labeled line** -- a 26n side call, `play — the model chose summarize-verify: 2 member calls, utility → chat`, closed with its time and, when every stage said, its tokens -- and each stage's own line beneath it. A play refused or stopped is a kept line (`orchestrate: extract-facts not played -- …`, `orchestrate: digest stopped -- …`) through a notice sink the turn now carries (`MemberCalls::begin_turn`'s third argument, which the loop sets to `Reporter::on_notice`; `MemberCalls::narration()` hands a consumer the turn's side-call sink). Machine mode: the same lines as `tool_status` events and the notices as `notice` events -- `cli.machine_schema_conformance` reads the same 17 emitted and 3 accepted types.
- [x] **One budget family**: validation's budget-spent line now says so -- `the turn's member-call budget is spent (4 of 4, plays, consults and checks together)`.
