- [x] **Kept on offer under 26g**: every registered `play_` tool is in the selection core (`agentloop::is_core_tool`, keyed on `kPlayToolPrefix`, declared beside consult's name so selection never reaches up into `symphony/`).
- [x] **The session** (`cli/chat_session`): `apogee execute --orchestrate`, an execute-only flag -- chat's flags, help, golden and surface unchanged -- and a suite's own `orchestrate: true` both turn orchestration on (`symphony::orchestrating`); the play tools join after any toolset pin, as consult does, and need no `--tools` -- orchestration is its own consent -- while consult and the native toolsets still do. Re-offered when `/suite` or `/model` moves the suite or the conversation. Each withheld symphony is said once as a warning, one withheld for its definition (an image) only under `--verbose`, and none offered says `orchestrate: no symphony can be offered as a tool -- the model answers without plays`; the banner reads `3 symphonies  ·  orchestrating 2` (or `orchestrating none`). Off, absent: no `play_` tool is registered, and `chat` never orchestrates.
- [x] **The config unit** (`contracts/config`): a suite's `orchestrate:` switch (`true`/`on`, read as a `validate:` seam is; a word that is not one refused by name), off when absent. The editor writes `orchestrate: true` last in the entry and only when on; `set_suite_orchestrate` sets it in place or removes the key. The starter config documents it beside `validate:`.
- [x] **The model's initiative never spends, at config time** (`operations::validate_suite_orchestrate`, run by `validate_suite` wherever 27f's consult rule runs, `operations` now linking `symphony`): with `orchestrate` on, every member a symphony the suite would offer reaches -- resolved under the suite with its chat role as the conversation, each backend asked once -- must be local and unmetered by its provider's word; unknown is metered, and no catalog to read is unknown. `config add-suite`/`set-suite --orchestrate on|off` (`--orchestrate maybe` refused), the member flags on an orchestrating suite, and the admin twins refuse in one sentence naming the symphony, the stage, the role and the backend: `orchestrate: 'summarize-verify' reaches utility ('paid') through its summarize stage (utility), and 'paid' is billed per call -- a play the model starts runs on its initiative, which never spends: only a suite whose symphonies reach local, unmetered members can orchestrate`. `config get suites.<name>.orchestrate` says `on` or `off`; `check`'s suite row ends `· orchestrates` and fails a hand-edited suite, or one a later symphony made unsafe, with `apogee config set-suite <name> --orchestrate off` as the fix.
- [x] **The admin twin**: `orchestrate` in the suite's shape and in `POST`/`PUT /v1/admin/suites`, and a new `PUT /v1/admin/suites/{id}/orchestrate` (`{"orchestrate": true | false}`), byte-identical to the CLI; the member route holds an orchestrating suite to the rule. 94 routes, 86 of them admin.
- [x] **Tests**: `symphony/tools_test` (new, 13 cases: the projection golden and a chain's; the offer -- every reason a symphony is withheld, by its words; the framing golden and its composition; through the loop, a play's wire, its tool result and its narration; the budget shared with a consult and an `answers: always` check, by call count; a chain stopped by the play's answer-token budget; a billed member refused at play time past the offer; a member's failure; the arguments; the members reached), `agentloop/tool_selection_test` (plays in the core), `contracts/config_test` and `config_edit_test` (the switch, round trips, in-place surgery), `operations/suites_test` (the rule, each backend asked once, the vision starter never asked about), `cli/config_cmd_test`, `cli/check_test`, `httpserver/admin_suites_test` (CLI ↔ HTTP byte identity, the member route), `serve_test` (the route count), `cli/execute_test` (+5, and the banner case extended: no play tool without orchestration and none in chat, the flag and the suite's switch, `/suite` moving the offer, consult still needing `--tools`, the framing on the wire, every symphony withheld and said, the root's play run and kept as an ordinary tool call, a driver's events all of known types, the banner) and `execute_session.golden` (`--orchestrate` in execute's help and completion); on the real binary `cli.execute_lifecycle` (`execute_e2e.sh`) gains the Orchestrator, and `cli.chat_typeahead_and_crash_safety` an `orchestrate` case under a pseudo-terminal (the banner, the labeled line and the stages in the thinking block, each stage closing with its time, the answer rendered).

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The tool's name *(2026-10-06)* | `play_<symphony>`; a name past 64 characters withheld and said | Collision-free with every native and MCP tool, a valid tool name on every vendor whatever the symphony is called (a symphony name may start with a digit or a dash), and the mark selection keeps on offer and the narration reads naturally (`[tool] play_summarize-verify`). |
| The projection *(2026-10-06)* | The definition's description, then the play's cost and roles and that it sees only its input; one `input` string described by the input contract | "Its own description, its input contract as the schema"; the brief-only property is what a model must know to write a usable input, as consult's description says it. |
| Symphonies that take an image *(2026-10-06)* | Not projected; said under `--verbose` only | A tool call carries text alone (`/play`'s own rule, 27s); the withholding is a property of the definition, so a warning on every session start would be noise. |
| 26g ranking *(2026-10-06)* | Every registered play tool is in the selection core, never ranked | 27f's evidence: a call ranked out of the offer is one a local model's grammar cannot even parse. Orchestration is the user's opt-in to the model choosing among the symphonies; the cost, each definition on every step, is the catalog's size, which the user writes. |
| Where orchestration runs *(2026-10-06)* | `execute` alone -- the flag is execute's, and a suite's `orchestrate: true` does nothing in `chat` | The spec's "in an execute session"; 27s's mode may change only what execute is, and chat's whole surface stays byte-identical (its golden passes unchanged). |
| Consent *(2026-10-06)* | Orchestration registers its tools without `--tools`; consult and the native tools still need it | The acceptance command is `apogee execute --suite research --orchestrate`; turning orchestration on is the consent to the model starting a play, and nothing else widens. |
| Off *(2026-10-06)* | Absent; no `--no-orchestrate` | The flag turns orchestration on for a session; a suite's switch is turned off through the editor, and `chat` is the session without plays. Left for the owner. |
| The config-time rule's scope *(2026-10-06)* | The symphonies the suite would offer -- playable, text input, a valid name -- each member resolved under the suite, the conversation its chat role; each backend asked once; no catalog, or a provider that cannot be asked, is metered | "Reachable from any registered symphony": a vision member that only the image starter reaches is never played on the model's initiative, so refusing for it would refuse nothing that could spend. |
| A symphony added after `orchestrate: true` *(2026-10-06)* | Not refused at `symphonies create`; withheld at session start (said), refused at its stage (`local_only`), and failed by `check` | A definition is suite-independent -- the same symphony plays on any suite -- and three later layers hold the spend rule. |
| What the offer withholds *(2026-10-06)* | A member not configured, not built, or billed; a play bigger than a turn's budget or `symphony_caps.stage_calls` | Consult's precedent: a member that cannot answer here is not offered, and the surface says why; a symphony that could never finish within the caps is not one the model can choose. |
| The budget *(2026-10-06)* | The suite's `consult_caps.per_turn`, the count consults and checks already spend; a play's static count checked before its first call; `symphony_caps` as for `/play` | "One family, shared accounting"; refusing up front never turns away a play that could finish (every stage is called unless one fails), and saves the members' time; the walk's own check stays the backstop. 27r's "never refused up front" was about a user's play, whose size the user chose. |
| How a play is said *(2026-10-06)* | A labeled side call opened before the walk and closed with its time and tokens (tokens only when every stage reported), the stages beneath; refusals and stops as notices; no kept line for a play that finished | 26n's shape, so machine mode needs nothing new; a kept warning-tagged line after every play would be noise -- the thinking block shows each stage's cost, and `--verbose` keeps the whole transcript. The labeled line's own closing scrolls out of the default block's two-row tail (noted below). |
| The tool result's wording *(2026-10-06)* | `<symphony> answered:` and the output -- consult's shape | Measured on real weights: with `summarize-verify played; its output:` and then `summarize-verify's output:`, Llama 3.1 8B answered every turn by describing the call (`The function play_summarize-verify is called …`) instead of relaying the result -- the pathology 26g recorded; with consult's shape it relayed the output on every turn. |
| The framing *(2026-10-06)* | One paragraph, composed from the registry asking, its wording revised once with the result's | The 26p mechanism; the first wording's "its output comes back as the result" was echoed back verbatim by Llama's description of its own call. |
| The admin twin *(2026-10-06)* | A new route, `PUT /v1/admin/suites/{id}/orchestrate`, and `orchestrate` in the suite's body and shape | ADR 0002: `set-suite --orchestrate` edits one key in place; the consult and validate routes are other flags' twins. |
| Real-weights design *(2026-10-06)* | One `execute --orchestrate --no-recall` session per family in machine mode, its model loaded once, the ten requests one after another; the pick is the first play a turn makes | The run's rule -- one family at a time, model loaded once -- means a session's later requests see its earlier turns; the order interleaves the symphonies and the controls, and the effect is noted below. |
| Mutation testing *(2026-10-06)* | In the scratch copy of the tree built without llama.cpp | The run's rules keep git read-only, so no worktree. |

**Guardrails, mutation-tested.** 56 mutants, each rebuilt in a copy of the tree (no llama.cpp) and run against the orchestration, symphony, execute, chat, consult, validation, selection, config, editor, operations, check and admin-suites suites -- 55 caught on the first pass, the one survivor caught once its test was written:
- **A play the model starts:** `local_only` off; the turn's budget not checked before the first call, nor `symphony_caps.stage_calls`; the play's answer-token cap dropped; a refusal or a stop unsaid; a refusal returned as an error, and a member's failure as none; the labeled line unsaid; its tokens summed when a stage reported none; a blank input played; the output dropped from the result.
- **The projection and the offer:** the argument renamed; the input contract's description, and the definition's own, dropped; a symphony that takes an image projected; one that cannot be played projected -- the survivor, since no test offered a definition that cannot be played, caught once one did; a name past 64 characters projected; a billed, an unbuilt and an unconfigured member offered; a play bigger than the turn's budget or than `symphony_caps.stage_calls` offered; the symphonies a chain plays never reached; the reach ignoring the conversation; an offer made with no suite; the framing always, and never; the suite's switch ignored.
- **The loop and selection:** plays ranked like any other tool; the loop, and `MemberCalls`, dropping the turn's notices.
- **The config unit:** `orchestrate:` unparsed, unwritten, and written when off.
- **The config-time rule:** skipped; asking about nothing; asking about the symphonies never offered; unknown passing; no catalog passing; the members resolved without the suite active.
- **The session:** the flag ignored; orchestration in `chat`; the flag bound in `chat` (caught by chat's golden); plays offered only with `--tools`; consult registered without it; `/suite` not moving the offer; withheld symphonies unsaid; none offered unsaid; the banner's count gone.
- **The verbs, the doctor and the twins:** `--orchestrate` ignored; `set-suite` not writing it; `check` not ruling; the twin's body key ignored; the member route not ruling; the twin never writing.

**Verified** -- the full suite (`make test`: 100% of 2875 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before), `format-check`, clang-tidy on every touched file (no finding in a gating class; the new code's own findings fixed -- a play tool's state held behind one shared pointer so its closure moves without throwing, the recursive token sum annotated in the tree's `NOLINTNEXTLINE(misc-no-recursion)` form, a raw string, designated initializers, `check`'s row built with `+=` -- the rest the touched files' existing classes (the route table's aggregate rows, which the new row follows) and Catch2's test-case complexity), GCC's library (`gcc-check.py`: all 535 first-party files), `cli.execute_lifecycle` and the PTY `orchestrate` case on the real binary.

**Real weights** -- the planted-task pick-rate check, the dated evidence any default-on decision must cite. A scratch `APOGEE_HOME` whose backends point read-only at the owner's GGUFs, one suite per family with `chat`, `utility` and `extraction` all on its model (so the root plays the starters on itself and the model loads once), recall off. One `apogee execute --suite <family> --orchestrate --no-recall --output-format stream-json` per family, nothing else running: ten requests, each a natural ask that never names a tool, a symphony or a play -- four that only `summarize-verify` answers (minutes, an article, an email thread, lab notes, each asking for a short summary that is accurate), four that only `extract-facts` answers (an incident report, a press release, a news brief, a paragraph, each asking for the topic, people, places, dates and facts as a structured record), and two controls that need none (the capital of Australia; the days in a leap year), interleaved S E C E S S E C S E. The vision starter is not offered (it takes an image), so the choice is among two plays and none. The pick is the first play a turn makes; what the play produced is measured separately.

| Family (model) | Symphony requests: the right play (of 8) | Controls answered without a play (of 2) | Picked right (of 10) | Wrong symphony | Session |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google (Gemma 4 12B Q4_K_M) | 8 | 2 | **10** | 0 | 241 s |
| OpenAI (gpt-oss-20b F16) | 7 | 2 | **9** | 0 | 108 s |
| Meta (Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M) | 8 | 0 | **8** | 0 | 75 s |
| Qwen (Qwen3-VL-8B Q4_K_M) | 3 | 2 | **5** | 0 | 62 s |

No family ever played the wrong symphony: every miss was a choice not to play -- gpt-oss summarized one email thread itself; Qwen played the first two requests and the lab notes, and after the first control answered the next four symphony requests and the last itself (the session's history is shared by its requests, so Qwen may have taken its own direct answer to the control as the pattern) -- or a play where none was needed: Llama played `extract-facts` on both controls, then answered the control itself ("The capital of Australia is Canberra."). Every play ran to its output (no notice in any session), and every answer to a symphony request that followed a play relayed what the play produced -- a summary, the record as a list or as its JSON. Two earlier Llama passes are recorded for honesty: with the first result wording (`… played; its output:`) and framing, and with the second (`…'s output:`), its picks were the same 8 of 10 but every answer described the call it had made rather than relaying the output; the wording then moved to consult's shape (above) and the other three families ran once, on the final wording. On Llama the `summarize-verify` starter's verify stage answered the first request with a verdict ("The summary is accurate and can be relied on."), which the root relayed -- 27r's note on that starter, seen here on a third family. The measure is what keeps orchestration opt-in: two families pick reliably, one over-plays and one under-plays.

**Not verified.** Windows (the e2e and the PTY check are POSIX); orchestration with `--tools` beside it on real weights (26g's selection is on past sixteen tools, held to keep every play on offer by a unit test, not measured on a model); a fresh-context pick rate (each request in a session of its own would load each model ten times); a cloud root, or a cloud or MLX member reached by a symphony through a real provider (the refusal is exercised with mocks whose script says they bill); the admin route over a live `serve` (in process only); the terminal's thinking block on real weights (the PTY case runs on mocks; the real-weights sessions ran in machine mode).

**Left for the owner.** The pick rates above are the evidence a default-on decision must cite; Qwen3-VL-8B's under-playing after its first control and Llama 3.1 8B's playing on controls are the two behaviours a default would have to answer. Llama 3.1 8B cut its first play's input at an apostrophe (`… because the payment provider` -- the minutes' "provider's"): the call's argument ended there as the model wrote it, a template or model behaviour outside this item. The labeled line's closing time and tokens scroll out of the default thinking block's two-row tail once its stages are drawn (each stage line keeps its own; `--verbose` keeps all of them). There is no session-level off switch for a suite's `orchestrate: true` (`--no-orchestrate`). The `summarize-verify` starter's verdict-instead-of-summary (27r) stands.
