## Milestone AD — Autonomous tasks

**Goal.** A goal that takes several model turns took a person at the keyboard between them. `apogee task run "<goal>"` removes the person: the application plans, drives successive turns of the one shared agent loop, checks each round against acceptance the user stated up front, composes the corrective follow-up when a check fails, and stops on done or on budget. The context-only spike (2026-09-25) completed exactly this cycle as an outer loop over the shipped binary, and found the two reasons it belongs *in* the binary with state of its own: an external driver sees only result text and cannot verify tool work it did not do, and the task's state -- plan, rounds, which checks had passed -- lived only in the driving process, so a restart lost the task though the chat survived. Track 27's tasks items open here: 27h the runner and its ledger, 27i the declared autonomy policy, 27j the surfaces.

### 2026-10-05 — `task-runner-core` (backlog item 27h): the task runner and its ledger

**What was built**

- [x] **`apogee task run "<goal>" [--require TEXT]... [--require-file PATH]... [--rounds N]`** (`cli/task_cmd.h/.cpp`), with `-m`, `--suite`, `--tools`, `--no-recall`, `--force`, `-v`, `--no-color`, `--raw` as `chat` has them. The lock first; then the session assembled as `chat` assembles one -- the suite chosen, validated and priced (`--force` over budget), the providers built, `SessionHold`, the chat role resolved, recall -- and a new chat saved up front naming its task (`session.task`), titled from the goal. The **plan is an ordinary first turn**, not a mode: the model is told the goal, the acceptance and that no one is present, and asked for a numbered plan only; its answer is recorded in the ledger and quoted into every round (up to 8,000 characters; the ledger keeps it whole), so the whole task reads in its transcript afterwards. Then **rounds**, each one ordinary chat turn of the task's session; after each the task is checked -- each `--require` text in the round's answer, exactly; each `--require-file`, made absolute where the task started, existing and not empty; and the model's own last `TASK STATUS: DONE` / `TASK STATUS: NOT DONE` line, read through Markdown, anything else unreported and never taken for done -- and the next round is composed from what failed: `Round 2 of 8. The task is not done -- after round 1:` then a `passed:`/`FAILED:` line per check with its detail, the self-report's, the plan again, and the status instruction. The task is `done` when every check passes in the same round **and** the model reports it done. Progress on the status line through the existing Reporter: the spinner reads `Round 2 of 8…`, and `[task] planning`, `[task] round 2 of 8 -- correcting: 1 check failing, not reported done`, `[task] round 2: 1 of 1 check passed, reported done` and each denial stay; the answers stream as a chat's do; the outcome line names the status, the reason and the conversation, with `task status`/`task resume` named when it is not done.
- [x] **Bounded by construction** (`tasks/task.h/.cpp`): `rounds_budget` is a field in 1..32 (`--rounds`, `CLI::Range`; the ledger clamps it on read), 8 by default, with no value meaning unbounded; the plan is one more turn outside it, and every turn is the loop's own (`max_iterations` and the half-turn rollback untouched). The stop set, each a status: **`done`**; **`exhausted`** -- the budget used, the reason naming every unpassed check and the self-report (`the round budget (8) is spent and the task is not done -- not passed: the answer contains "42" (not in the answer); not reported done by the model`); **`stalled`** -- the breaker: two consecutive rounds with no check passing that had never passed and no tool call run whose fingerprint (the SHA-256 of its name and arguments) had never run, the reason naming the same; **`failed`** -- a turn's provider error, or a question nobody was present to answer; **`halted`** and **`cancelled`** by request. Tokens are recorded per round, unenforced.
- [x] **The record and its transitions are functions of the ledger** (`tasks/task`): `plan_message`, `round_message` (the first round carries the plan out; every later one names what the round before it failed), `conclude_round` (each check evaluated, the self-report read, progress against every earlier round, then the next status), `shortfall`, `live` (planning, running, halted) and `finished` (done, exhausted), the JSON. Nothing that decides what happens next lives anywhere else -- which is what lets a task resumed in another process continue exactly where the last stopped, sending a round run again exactly what it was sent the first time.
- [x] **The ledger, rewritten on every transition** (`tasks/ledger`, the pipeline manifest's pattern): `tasks/<id>/task.json` through `write_file_atomically` at each of `created`, `started`/`resumed`, `plan_started`, `plan_recorded`, `round_started`, `round_ended`, `finished` -- each entry with its time, the status after it, the round and a detail -- so a `kill -9` at any moment leaves the last transition and never a torn file. The ledger references the session by id and never copies the transcript (the plan, by the spec's word, is the one answer it records). `task-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` ids, suffixed past one that exists; `list_tasks` newest first, an unreadable ledger named and skipped.
- [x] **One task at a time, under the cycle's lock, now shared** (`platform/pid_lock.h/.cpp`): `PidLock` -- the training cycle's exclusive-create PID file moved into the platform seam, with a label line (the task's id) beside the process id, a `holder` read, and an opt-in takeover of a lock whose process is gone (once, and only while the file still says what was read; a file naming no process never). `training::CycleLock` now wraps it with its own rule unchanged -- a crashed cycle's lock refused, naming the file -- pinned by a new test; `tasks::TaskLock` (`tasks/task.lock`) takes a dead holder's over, since `task resume` is the documented way back from a kill, and refuses a live one by name: `task task-… is running (process 4153) -- one task runs at a time. 'apogee task status task-…' shows it; 'apogee task halt' or 'apogee task cancel' stops it`.
- [x] **Nobody present** (`tasks/unattended.h/.cpp`): the gate is `make_permission_checker(config, nullptr)` with **no confirm function**, so an `ask`-level tool denies exactly as on any pipe and the denial is the tool's result the model reads, the turn going on; `TurnRecorder::gate` wraps the checker only to record each refusal (`Deny`, and `Ask`) with its tool and target, the decision returned unchanged, and `TurnRecorder::observe` wraps each registered tool's run to record the calls that actually ran -- the round's activity. `ask_user` is offered where a chat offers it (with tools) and `fail_on_question` throws `UnansweredQuestion` from it: the loop rolls the half-turn back as for any aborted question, and the task fails naming the question (`round 1: the model asked a question and no one is present to answer it: Which city?`). Widening either is 27i's, by declared policy; nothing here grants anything.
- [x] **The outer loop** (`tasks/runner.h/.cpp`): `run_task` over a `TurnFn` closure -- the runner decides whether to open another turn, never how one runs. A `RequestWatcher` thread polls the task's `request` file every 200 ms: a `cancel` -- or the command's Ctrl-C token -- is passed to the turn's cancellation token at once, so the in-flight turn ends through the loop's own cancellation; a `halt` is read when the round ends. On resume a round left unfinished is run again **under its own number and with its own message**, unless the session shows its turn did finish (killed between the session's save and the ledger's write): then the answer is taken from the session (`answer_in_session`, the last user message reading exactly the round's message and the answer closing its turn) and the round marked `adopted` -- never asked twice. Resuming a stalled task clears the breaker's count, as `cycle resume` clears the cycle's; a request left standing by a process that ended before reading it is cleared when a run starts; `resume_refusal` refuses done and exhausted.
- [x] **A task's turns are chat turns** (`cli/chat_turn.h/.cpp`): `run_chat_turn` -- measure, compact or warn, append, retrieve and recall, run the loop, persist -- moved out of `chat.cpp` whole, so the REPL, machine mode and a task's rounds call the one function. It now returns a `ChatTurnResult` (completed, cancelled, the provider's error, the loop's result; the REPL ignores it) and takes the turn's cancellation token (by default one that never fires, as before). A turn cut short in a task -- cancelled, failed, a question -- leaves the session as the last finished turn left it, the same state a kill leaves, so the round run again on resume is said once.
- [x] **The other verbs**: `task status [TASK]` (the running task, else the newest: the status -- `running (now, process N)` or `running (interrupted -- its process is gone; 'apogee task resume …' continues it)` -- goal, conversation, folder, tools, rounds used of the budget, the reason, each check's state as the newest round left it, the self-report, the plan, every turn with its checks, tools run and denied and tokens, every denial with its target); `task list [--all]` (newest 50, each with its status and rounds used); `task resume [TASK]` (refused once finished, and anywhere but the folder the task was started in; continues under the session's backend and suite); `task halt|cancel [TASK]` (a request left for the running task, or -- for a task no process runs -- the status written under the lock). Exit codes a scheduler can read: done 0, cancelled 130, a provider failure 2, anything else short of done 1.
- [x] **The session linkage** (`logger/session`): `Session::task`, written only when set, so every other chat saves exactly as before. **`chats delete` refuses a live task's conversation** (planning, running, halted): `chat … is the conversation of task …, which is halted -- 'apogee task cancel …' stops it first`.
- [x] **The `tasks/` layout row** (`contracts/layout.h`, private, user data; `tasks_dir()`), in the same change as the code that uses it -- `check --fix` and both installers seed it, `reset --keep tasks` keeps it. The starter config's recall note names `task` beside `chat` (both copies, byte-matched).
- [x] **The module**: `tasks` in the Business row of `cmake/modules.cmake`, linking `agent agentloop contracts logger platform` and nothing else; guarded in `harness.layering` (no `backends/`, and an allow-list of `agentloop/`, `agent/`, `harness/`, `logger/`, `contracts/`, `platform/` and itself); the Business card and ADR 0008's table with it; `cli` links it. `platform::utc_time` for the ledger's timestamps and ids (the `gmtime_r`/`gmtime_s` `#ifdef` kept in the seam). Completion: a `TASK` name kind (`kTaskValue`) on every verb's task argument, listing the ledgers' ids. The parity table classifies `task run|resume|halt|cancel` as carve-outs (task control is CLI-only) and `task status|list` as reads.
- [x] **58 new test cases** -- `platform/pid_lock_test` (6), `tasks/task_test` (16, the transitions table-tested), `tasks/ledger_test` (7), `tasks/unattended_test` (6, through the real loop and gate), `tasks/runner_test` (15, the outer loop over a scripted turn saving a real session), `cli/task_test` (7, the real command tree), `training/cycle_test` (1, the crashed cycle's lock) -- and on the real binary **`cli.task_lifecycle`** (`task_e2e.sh`).

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | **`source/business/tasks/`** (a Business module, its row, guarded) and the command in `cli/task_cmd.h/.cpp`; tests under `tests/business/tasks/` *(2026-10-05)* | The spec predates the four layers; `commands/` became `cli/`, and a domain core with a closure seam is Business, like `training/`. |
| How a turn reaches the runner | **A closure** -- one `run_chat_turn` of the task's session, which the composition root hands in *(2026-10-05)* | The spec says generation arrives "through the loop's existing seams", and a task is an ordinary chat session: everything a chat turn does (the suite, retrieval, recall, compaction, the per-turn save, consult and validation) lives in Presentation, so calling `agentloop::run` from Business would have been a second, poorer turn. The training precedent: generation arrives as a closure. |
| `--require` | **Text the round's answer must contain, exactly** (case counts; empty refused) *(2026-10-05)* | The spec names the flag, not its reading. A deterministic check of the round's own answer is the literal one; a judge-model check is the later item, under the never-fail contract. |
| `--require-file` | **Absolute where the task started; exists, is a regular file, and is not empty** *(2026-10-05)* | "Never a claimed success": an empty file is no work done, and an absolute path is checked the same wherever status is read. |
| The self-report | **The last `TASK STATUS: DONE` / `NOT DONE` line**, read through Markdown, case aside; anything else unreported, never done *(2026-10-05)* | A marker in the transcript keeps every answer readable prose (a response schema would have turned the conversation into JSON), and unreported is the conservative reading. |
| Done | **Every check passing in the same round and the self-report `done`**; checks evaluated per round, not remembered *(2026-10-05)* | Done must describe the state the task ended in. A text check that passed three rounds ago says nothing about the final answer. |
| The plan and the budget | **The plan is one turn outside the budget**; the budget counts rounds after it; `--rounds` 1..32 *(2026-10-05)* | The plan is not checked, so it is not a round; the confirmed default is "8 rounds". A flag lets a scheduler or a test choose, and a ceiling keeps it bounded. |
| Progress, for the breaker | **A check passing that had never passed in an earlier round, or a call that ran whose fingerprint never ran before**; a denied call is not activity *(2026-10-05)* | A high-water mark cannot be gamed by a check flip-flopping, a model repeating one call each round is not progressing, and a model knocking on a denied door is the futility the breaker exists to stop -- the budget still bounds the rest. |
| Budget and breaker at once | **Exhausted** *(2026-10-05)* | Exhausted is final; stalled would invite a resume with nothing left to run. |
| What resumes | Halted, cancelled, stalled (its count cleared, as `cycle resume`), failed, and a task killed mid-turn; **never done or exhausted** *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed default allows cancelled; a failed turn may be a provider that is back. Exhausted is the budget's end, by construction. |
| Live, for `chats delete` | **Planning, running or halted**; `task cancel` is the way out *(2026-10-05)* | Those are the states that will write the session again. A wider "anything resumable" would have left a stopped task's chat undeletable with no way out. |
| Halt and cancel | **Halt at the round's end; cancel now, through the turn's cancellation token** -- asked across processes by a request file the runner polls every 200 ms *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed default ("the lock holder finishes its in-flight turn via the loop's cancellation") and the cycle's halt. A file is portable and the filesystem stays the truth; a signal would need a Windows twin and could not carry a halt. |
| A turn cut short | **The session restored to before the turn** *(2026-10-05)* | A kill leaves exactly that; restoring a cancel, a failure or a question to the same state is what lets the round run again on resume and be said once. A chat's own cancel is unchanged. |
| A turn that finished before a restart | **Adopted from the session**, found by its exact message after the round's recorded turn count *(2026-10-05)* | Asking again would say the turn twice -- the guardrail's "no duplicated turns". |
| The lock | **The cycle's, moved to `platform/pid_lock` and shared**; the task's takes over a dead holder's lock, the cycle's still refuses *(2026-10-05)* | "Do not copy code that could be shared." A killed task must resume without the user deleting a file; the cycle's recorded rule is its own and stays. |
| A model's question | **`ask_user` offered (with tools, as chat) and its use fails the task naming the question** *(2026-10-05)* | 27i's declared answer needs a question to answer, and 27i's acceptance has the task "fail naming the question" without it; never advertising it would have made fail-on-question vacuous. The model is told up front that asking ends the task. |
| A terminal present | **Still no prompt** -- a task's gate has no confirm function however it is started *(2026-10-05)* | Deny-by-default survives autonomy; 27i owns any widening, its attended-prompt guardrail included. |
| The session's title | **From the goal** (`task: <goal>`), no title model call *(2026-10-05)* | Cosmetic, and a call saved per task; every turn is still the chat's own. |
| Resume's folder | **Only where the task was started**, refused elsewhere naming the folder *(2026-10-05)* | A chat's tools work in the launch folder (25a); a task resumed elsewhere would write in one place and check in another. Refusing is safer than changing directory. |
| Recall | **As a chat's**: turns recall unless `--no-recall` or `memory.recall: false`, the session summarised at a clean end (not after a cancel) *(2026-10-05)* | A task is an ordinary chat session; the starter config's note says so. |
| `task list` | **Newest 50, `--all` for every one** *(2026-10-05)* | 27j's confirmed default, taken where the list is first built so its JSON twin reads the same. |
| Machine mode and the admin plane | **Not built** -- 27j's; control stays CLI-only (carve-outs in the parity table) *(2026-10-05)* | ADR 0002's skipped modes, named: 27j adds the events, the JSON reads and the served reads over this ledger. |

**Verified on the real binary.** `cli.task_lifecycle` in a scratch `APOGEE_HOME`, recall off and scripted mocks, nothing typed after the command: goal → plan → an incomplete round → the corrective round naming `FAILED: the answer contains "42" -- not in the answer` → done, exit 0, and the ledger's transitions asserted whole (`created started plan_started plan_recorded round_started@1 round_ended@1 round_started@2 round_ended@2:done finished:done`); the conversation three turns, each said once; `task status` with the plan, `2 of 8 used`, each check `[x]` and the conversation, `task list` with each outcome; `write_file` from an unattended task denied with stdin a FIFO held open for a minute (a prompt would hang; the run took well under the bound) -- the denial the tool's result the next turn quoted, `round 1: write_file on report.txt` in the ledger and `status`, no file written, and the one-round budget ending it `exhausted` naming the file check, exit 1; the breaker `stalled` naming the check, exit 1; a second `task run` beside a live one refused naming its id and process; that task `kill -9`ed mid-round 2, `status` saying it was interrupted, resumed to done with round 2 started again and three distinct user turns; `task cancel` ending a running turn (exit 130, the cut-short turn gone from the conversation, the reason `cancelled by 'apogee task cancel' during round 1`) and the chat then deletable; `task halt` stopping a task when round 1 ended, `chats delete` refusing its conversation by name, `task resume` finishing it; `__complete task status ""` offering the ids; `check` green. By hand in a sandbox: a denied task whose config was then given `permissions: write_file: allow` resumed and wrote its file to done. The full suite through `make test` (llama.cpp on): 100% of 2509 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before; `make format-check` clean; `clang-tidy` over every file this item touched reports no error (the ownership gate); the warnings left in the new files are kinds the tree already carries -- cognitive complexity on the command's composition root, unchecked optional access and designated-initializer suggestions in the tests, and an exception-escape note on the recorder's wrapped tools.

**Guardrails, each mutation-tested.** 42 mutants, each applied in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared checkout), rebuilt and run against its tests -- **42 caught**. Two of those tests were written for the run before it began: the runner test reading the ledger as each turn begins (a round's start left unwritten was otherwise caught only by the e2e's kill test, which polls the ledger for it), and the cycle test refusing a crashed cycle's lock (nothing held the cycle's own rule once its lock became the shared one that can take over). The mutations: done without the self-report, and on the self-report alone; the budget a round late; the breaker at three; the breaker winning over the budget; a check passing again counted as progress, and a repeated tool call; progress never resetting the count; the first self-report winning; one read by prefix; an empty file, an empty require text and a folder passing; a correction naming no failure; the plan never quoted, and never recorded; a halted task not live; an exhausted task resumable; a finished turn never adopted; an interrupted round run as a new one; a cancel request ignored mid-turn; a halt ignored; a round's start not written; a stalled task's count kept on resume; a stale request left to stop the next run; a question not named; an `Ask` not recorded as a denial; a call that ran not recorded; a question answered with nothing; a live holder's lock taken over, and a killed task's never; the cycle taking a crashed cycle's lock; `chats delete` refusing nothing; a task's gate confirming; a turn cut short left in the session (the e2e's cancel); a task resumed in another folder; a task short of done exiting 0; the gate not watched; a backend included by `tasks/` (`harness.layering`); the chat not linked to its task, and the linkage never saved; a finished task stopped anyway.

**Real weights.** Not run: the guardrails ask for a scripted mock, and nothing here changes how a model is called -- each round is the chat's own turn.

**Not verified.** Windows (the e2e is POSIX; the lock, the request file and the watcher are portable mechanisms -- an exclusive create, `process_running`, a polled file -- but none was run there); a task under a pseudo-terminal (the e2e runs piped, so the spinner's `Round N of M…` label was seen only in code); compaction mid-task on a real window, MCP tools, `consult` and validation inside a task (each is the chat turn's own and covered there, not re-run through `task`); a `task cancel` landing in the instant a task's lock changes hands (a request is for a running process, and a run clears any it finds standing).

**Left for the owner.** Two readings the spec left open and this item chose, each in the table above and each a one-place change if vetoed: `--require` as exact text in the answer (a shell-command check -- a test suite passing -- would be a new flag, not a new reading of this one), and a halted task counted live for `chats delete`.

**Fixed 2026-10-06 (found at 27t's boundary).** `task list`'s newest-first order could put an older task first. A new task's id was minted from one clock reading and its `created_at` stamped from another, later one -- after agent resolution, tool setup and the session's first save -- so under load a task minted at second 51 with a suffix (`task-…-115959-2`-shaped) could carry `created_at` second 52 and, on the tie, outrank a genuinely newer `…-120000` by the old longer-id-first rule. The task e2e's newest-task lookup then returned the wrong task, intermittently (2 of 9 runs under load: "the breaker did not trip", "the background task never started"). Now one `system_clock::now()` names a new task and dates it (`tasks::timestamp`), and the list breaks a same-second tie by the id's own time, then its numeric suffix (`-10` after `-9`), so ledgers written before the fix sort right too. Two ledger cases pin it; the e2e then passed 20 repetitions in a row.

### 2026-10-05 — `task-autonomy-policy` (backlog item 27i): authority handed over before the run

**Why.** 27h shipped safe and therefore narrow: an unattended task failed on a question and every `ask`-level tool denied, which made whole classes of useful tasks impossible on purpose -- a task that must write files, run a build or make a judgment call needs the user's authority granted **before** the run, since nobody is present during it. The hazard is the rubber stamp: an orchestrator that answers "yes" to every prompt re-creates exactly the hole the permission gate closes. So the authority is *declared up front, scoped to the task, and recorded per use* -- never answered live by the machine on the user's behalf.

**What was built**

- [x] **Per-task grants**, `task run --allow <tool>` (repeatable): a tool that writes, named one at a time -- there is no `--allow-all`, and its absence is permanent -- resolved from `ask` to `allow` for the task's life. **The gate's semantics do not change**: a grant is chat's own `session` answer given at launch, composed through chat's own `seed_approvals` and `make_permission_checker` (26o) -- no second checker, so the order stays the gate's (the config's no, then its yes, then the grant, then `ask`), a denial is still a tool result the model reads, and `ask` with nobody present still denies everywhere else.
- [x] **The ceiling** (`tasks/policy`, `grant_refusal`): a grant must name a tool the task has that writes (an outbound tool is asked about per website, a read-only one never asks), that the agent's tool policy keeps (Milestone X's filter -- `apply_tool_policy`, applied by the composition root and handed to the ceiling as its result, never re-derived), and that the config's `permissions:` does not deny. Anything wider is refused at `task run` naming the rule -- `--allow write_file: the config says permissions.write_file: deny -- a task's grant is never wider than the config`; `--allow write_file: the agent 'security-review' runs with tools: read-only, which leaves out write_file -- a task's grant is never wider than its agent's policy` -- with **no task made**: the tools and the gate are now composed before the session and the ledger are first written. A resume is held to the config and the agent as they are now (`task … cannot resume: …`).
- [x] **The question policy**, `--on-question fail|answer:"<text>"`: `fail`, the default (grants or no), ends the task on a question nobody answers, naming it; `answer:` is **one declared answer** served to every question the run asks -- the text after the colon as it is, one pair of matching quotes dropped, an empty answer refused. The plan turn says which rule holds; with neither grants nor an answer its message is 27h's, byte for byte.
- [x] **`--agent <name>`**: the task runs under that agent's policy -- its tool policy over the registry, its MCP servers and none else (none at all for `tools: none`), its `questions` switch (an agent that asks no questions is never offered `ask_user`, and a declared answer for one is refused). `--allow`, `--on-question answer:` and `--agent` each need `--tools`, refused without it, as chat's `--allow` is.
- [x] **Every use recorded** (`tasks/task`, `tasks/unattended`): `TurnRecorder::watch` wraps the gate's two halves, every decision returned unchanged -- a call let through recorded on its round as a `Permit` with its target and its authority (`config` when the config's own levels allow it too, `grant` when the task's grants name it, `person` for the person at the terminal), a refusal as a `Denial` with its reason (`config`, `nobody`, `person`), and `ask_user` wrapped to record each `Answered` question by `declared` or `person`. The ledger keeps the policy (`policy`: grants, the question policy and the declared answer, the agent) and each round's `allowed`, `denied` and `answered`; a ledger written by 27h reads as handed nothing. The run says each grant's use (`[task] write_file on report.txt -- allowed by this task's grant`), each refusal with its reason, and each question a declared answer answered -- the question, never the answer. **`task status`** shows the agent, the grants, the question policy with the declared answer, then `allowed:`, `denied:` and `answered:` across the rounds.
- [x] **The human path, kept.** An attended `task run` -- stdin and stderr a terminal -- still prompts for anything not granted, through chat's own `terminal_confirm_fn` over the same remembered answers (`session` and `always` as in a chat), and puts a question with no declared answer to the person (`terminal_ask_fn`); with nobody there the prompt is null, `ask` denies and a question fails the task, exactly as 27h. Policy adds to the human path, never replaces it -- which supersedes 27h's "a terminal present: still no prompt".
- [x] **Secrets hygiene**: a declared answer is stored in the ledger like any other field, so `--help` says plainly that it is kept and shown, never a credential; and **the leak sweep covers ledgers** -- a distinctive declared answer is found in the ledger, `task status` and the conversation the model read, and nowhere else (the run's own lines, `task list`, `chats list`, the event bus, the operational log).
- [x] **Repeatable for real.** `task run --allow`, and 27h's `--require` and `--require-file`, are `TakeAll` -- and so, the same flag family, are `chat` and `complete`'s `--allow`, `--deny` and `--allow-host`: each refused a second use (`--allow: At Most 1 required but received 2`), found by 27f and left for the owner then. Completion offers `--on-question`'s forms, `fail` and `answer:` -- `__complete` now reads a `{...}` set whole, since `answer:` holds a colon.
- [x] **22 new test cases**: `tasks/policy_test` (5: the question policy's forms, the grants, **the ceiling's 64-row table** -- every tool kind under every agent policy at every config level, granted -- every grant held, the JSON), `tasks/unattended_test` (+4: each authority, the attended yes and no, a declared answer to every question, the person's answer), `tasks/task_test` (+2), `tasks/runner_test` (+2: the records said and kept, an interrupted attempt's kept), `cli/task_test` (+7: a granted write, a declared answer and its absence, a dozen refusals each naming its rule, the agent's questions switch, a resume refused, the repeatable flags, and **the composition table** -- 96 rows of agent policy × config level × grant × nobody / a yes / a no at the terminal through `compose_task_gate` and the real gate), `cli/leak_test` (+1), `cli/chat_test` (+1), and completion assertions; on the real binary `cli.task_lifecycle` grew the policy and `cli.chat_typeahead_and_crash_safety` a `task-attended` case under a pseudo-terminal.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | **`tasks/policy.h/.cpp`** in `source/business/tasks/` (the guarded module, no new link), the flags in `cli/task_cmd`, `tests/business/tasks/policy_test.cpp`; the composition the command runs in `cli/task_cmd`'s exported `compose_task_gate`, its table in `tests/presentation/cli/task_test.cpp` *(2026-10-05)* | The spec predates the layers. The ceiling is domain logic over plain data (Business); the checker it feeds is chat's, in Presentation, so the table that proves the two together lives where both are visible. |
| How grants reach the gate | **Chat's own composition** -- the grants seeded as the `session` answer by `seed_approvals`, the checker `make_permission_checker(config, approvals)` *(2026-10-05)* | The spec's rule -- the existing shapes are reused, not duplicated: one composition of the config with the session's answers (26o), never a second. It also keeps the gate's order -- a config `deny` beats a grant even if the ceiling were bypassed. |
| The ceiling's inputs | **The task's registry before and after the agent's filter**, built by the composition root; the ceiling reads which tools the filter left out *(2026-10-05)* | Milestone X's filter exists once (`apply_tool_policy`); re-deriving "read-only drops `writes`" in `tasks/` would be its second copy. |
| What a grant may name | **A tool that writes** -- an outbound tool refused (asked about per website; a task reaches only `tools.allowed_hosts`), a read-only one refused (nothing to grant), a grant of a tool the config already allows standing *(2026-10-05)* | The gate asks per tool only for `writes` tools; a host grant would be a different item. A grant equal to the config is not wider than it. |
| A refused grant | **Refused before anything is written** -- the tools composed ahead of the session and the ledger, an order change from 27h (tools now before the banner, as chat's) *(2026-10-05)* | "Refused at `task run`" should leave no task behind to resume or delete. |
| Resume | **Held to the config and the agent as they are now**, refused naming the rule; no policy flags on `resume` *(2026-10-05)* | A grant the config has since denied must not be exercised because it was once allowed; the checker would deny it anyway (config first), but saying so up front is honest. A task's policy is the task's, fixed at its start. |
| An attended run | **Prompts for anything not granted** (chat's terminal prompt over the same answers) and **puts an undeclared question to the person**; a declared answer and a grant still serve first; with nobody present, 27h's behaviour unchanged *(2026-10-05)* | The guardrail: policy adds to the human path, never replaces it. This reverses 27h's "a terminal present: still no prompt", which named 27i as its owner. A failure saying "no one is present" while someone is would be false; `fail` therefore means "a question nobody answers ends the task". |
| What is recorded | **Every gated call let through, with its authority** (the config's too), every refusal with its reason, every answered question -- not only the grants' uses *(2026-10-05)* | "The audit trail is the price of autonomy": a ledger that lists grant uses but not the config's allows reads as if nothing else ran. The run says only what the task's own authority did. |
| A round run again | **Keeps what its interrupted attempt let through and answered**, appending the new attempt's; its denials and activity are the attempt's own, as 27h *(2026-10-05)* | The attempt's turn was rolled back out of the conversation; its effects -- a file written under a grant -- were not, and the audit trail is of what happened. Found by the mutation run: the first version cleared them, and nothing could tell. |
| The declared answer's reach | **The ledger and `task status`** (the spec's), and the conversation as the tool result the model read; the run's lines name the question only *(2026-10-05)* | The leak sweep's "only where it belongs"; 27j's served view says one existed, never what. |
| `--agent` | **The agent's policy** -- tool policy, MCP servers, `questions` -- **not its persona, schema or model** *(2026-10-05)* | The spec's words are "an agent's policy". A task's turns are chat turns whose answers carry the `TASK STATUS:` line; an agent's schema would turn them into JSON (27h's reason against a response schema). `-m` chooses the model. |
| An agent that asks nothing | **`ask_user` not offered; `--on-question answer:` refused** naming its `questions: false` *(2026-10-05)* | Its policy holds in a task as in `analyze`; a declared answer that could never be used is a typo, said. |
| Flags without `--tools` | **`--allow`, `--on-question answer:` and `--agent` refused** *(2026-10-05)* | Each is meaningless without tools (no gated call, no `ask_user`); chat refuses `--allow` the same way. |
| `--on-question`'s reading | `fail`, or `answer:` + the text as it is, **one pair of matching quotes dropped**; an empty answer refused; `fail` case-sensitive *(2026-10-05)* | The spec writes `answer:"blue"`, which a shell hands over as `answer:blue`; quoting the whole word keeps the quotes, and they are not the answer. |
| The ledger's schema | **Additive fields, version 1 kept** *(2026-10-05)* | A 27h ledger reads as handed nothing. A 27h binary resuming a 27i ledger drops the policy and runs narrower, never wider. |
| The repeatable flags | **`TakeAll`** on `task run`'s `--allow`, `--require`, `--require-file` and on `chat`/`complete`'s `--allow`, `--deny`, `--allow-host` *(2026-10-05)* | 27f's fix for `--consult-cap`, applied to the `--allow` family and to the command this item touches. |
| Completion of `answer:` | **`__complete` reads a `{...}` set whole** *(2026-10-05)* | Splitting the type name at every colon broke the set at `answer:`; the change is a parser fix, the protocol unchanged. |

**Verified on the real binary.** In a scratch `APOGEE_HOME`, scripted mocks, recall off: `cli.task_lifecycle` now runs a write granted with `--allow` to done with nothing prompting (stdin `/dev/null`), the file written, `[task] write_file on granted.txt -- allowed by this task's grant` said, the ledger's `policy.grants` and the round's `allowed` (`{"by": "grant", "target": "granted.txt", "tool": "write_file"}`) asserted, and `task status` showing both; `--on-question 'answer:"blue"'` finishing a question-asking task to done with `{"answer": "blue", "by": "declared", "question": "Which colour?"}` in the ledger and shown -- and without it, the same task failing `round 1: the model asked a question and no one is present to answer it: Which colour?`; a grant the config denies and one `security-review` leaves out each refused naming the rule, no task made; two `--require`s taken whole; 27h's denial now recorded `by: nobody`. Under a pseudo-terminal (`task-attended`): `task run --tools --allow write_file` wrote with no prompt, asked exactly once -- for `run_command` -- took the person's `n`, put the question to the person and took `blue`, ended done, and the ledger held the grant's use, `{"by": "person", "target": "echo hi", "tool": "run_command"}` and the person's answer. By hand: `task status` of a mixed task (a grant used, a denial, a declared answer) reads as the sections above; `__complete task run --on-question ""` offers `fail` and `answer:`. The full suite through `make test` (llama.cpp on): 100% of 2531 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before; `make format-check` clean; `clang-tidy` over every file this item touched reports no error (the ownership gate) -- the warnings left in its new code are kinds the tree already carries: cognitive complexity on the command's composition root and the runner's turn, the recorder's wrapped tools' exception-escape note, and designated-initializer and optional-access suggestions in the tests.

**Guardrails, each mutation-tested.** 46 mutants against the final code, each applied in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared checkout), rebuilt and run against the unit suites -- and the e2e or the pseudo-terminal check where the mutant reaches the binary -- **46 caught**. A first run against an earlier form left one alive: a round run again clearing what its interrupted attempt had let through, which nothing could see; its answer is the decision above (keep them) and the runner test that holds it. The mutations: the ceiling ignoring a config deny, the agent's filter, a tool that does not write, an outbound tool, or an unknown name; refusing a grant of a tool the config allows; holding only the first grant; an empty answer accepted, and its quotes kept; duplicate grants kept; the policy never written, or read back unnormalized; a denial's reason lost from the ledger; the grants sentence in every plan; a grant winning over the config's allow; an outbound allow counted as a grant; nobody's `ask`, the person's no, and the person altogether, unrecorded; one answer for the first question only; a declared answer unrecorded, said by the run, unused, or missing from `status`; the round's permits or answers dropped, and an interrupted attempt's forgotten; the ceiling skipped; the agent's policy not applied; grants not seeded; the standing checker the granted one; nobody's prompt even attended (the pseudo-terminal check too); everything allowed -- the blanket grant; the person never asked a question (caught by the pseudo-terminal check alone); an agent's questions switch ignored; `--allow` taken without `--tools`; a resume not held to today's config, or run under an agent the config no longer has; a denial's reason dropped from `status`; the answer listed by `task list`; each repeatable flag back to one use (`task run --allow` and `--require`, `chat --allow`, `complete --deny` and `--allow-host`); and a completion set split at its colon.

**Real weights.** Not run, and none was asked for: nothing here changes how a model is called -- grants and answers act at the gate and the question seam, each round still the chat's own turn.

**Not verified.** Windows (the e2e and the pseudo-terminal check are POSIX; the composition is portable code). A turn killed with `kill -9`: the ledger is written at transitions, so that turn's permits and answers -- like 27h's tools and denials -- never reach it, though its effects remain; a cancel, a failure or a question keeps them. A `task cancel` arriving while an attended prompt waits for its answer (the prompt reads a line, as chat's does; the cancel lands when it is answered). `always` answered at an attended task's prompt (chat's path, written through the one editor and covered there). An MCP tool granted by name (the ceiling treats it as any tool that writes; no MCP server ran under a task here).

**Left for the owner.** The remaining `expected(1)` vector flags refuse a second use -- `config add-suite`/`set-suite`'s `--context-size`, `--unpin` and `--remove` (a different flag family from the `--allow` one this item fixed). Two readings this item chose, each in the table and each a one-place change if vetoed: an attended run prompting (and putting questions to the person) rather than behaving exactly as an unattended one; and `--agent` bringing the agent's policy without its persona.

### 2026-10-05 — `task-surfaces` (backlog item 27j): one ledger, three views

**Why.** 27h shipped a CLI command narrating to a terminal, and 27i the authority it runs on. Parity is the product, so a task had to be *watchable and readable* from every surface there is: a front-end driving the binary over machine mode needs the task's lifecycle to render live progress (a task is exactly the long-running thing a GUI wants a progress panel for), a host or a script needs `task status`/`task list` as documents rather than prose, and a server deployment needs its tasks visible over the admin plane -- reads served, control CLI-only, the training track's split. One runner, one ledger, and every surface a rendering of it: nothing computes task state a second way.

**What was built**

- [x] **The one view** (`tasks/view.h/.cpp`, Business -- the training precedent: the domain owns its served shapes, as `training::manifest_to_json` does). `make_task_view(task, holder)` decides, once, every fact `task status` shows: the ledger's status, and from the task lock's holder `process` (the process running it -- only while it plans or runs, and only that task's live holder) and `interrupted` (planning or running with no process left); the goal, the conversation, the folder, tools, the policy (`PolicyView`: agent, grants, `on_question`; none without tools, as the human view shows none), the rounds used of the budget, the times, the reason, each check as the newest completed round left it (`CheckView`: kind, value, description, ran, passed, detail), the newest completed round's self-report, the plan, and a `TurnView` per turn -- outcome (`in_flight` while it runs), adopted, checks passed, self-report, tools that ran, every call let through and refused with its authority, every question answered and by whom, tokens, times. `make_task_list` the listing (the newest `kListLimit`, 50, unless all, and the total -- the constant moved here from the command so the admin list mirrors it from one place). **View types, by construction:** `QuestionView` is the question and who answered it, `PolicyView` says `on_question: answer` -- neither has a slot for what a declared answer said, so a served view or an event a host logs cannot carry it, rather than merely not doing so; nor does anything in it name a path into the private layout (the ledger's, the session's file). `to_json` renders each; `tasks::transition_to_json` is factored out of the ledger's own JSON so an event carries a transition exactly as the ledger writes it.
- [x] **The human reads render the view** (`cli/task_cmd`): `task status` prints the view -- the declared answer beside it read from the ledger, the one fact only this rendering shows (27i's decision kept), each answered question paired with its own answer in the view's order -- and `task list` the listing; both byte-identical to before. With **`--output-format json`** each prints the view's one document on one line and nothing else on stdout (`machine/json_reporter`'s `ReadFormat` and `write_document`, the convention 28h's reads will extend: `text` or `json`; `stream-json`, or any other word, refused naming the two).
- [x] **The admin plane's reads** (`httpserver/admin_tasks.h/.cpp`): `GET /v1/admin/tasks[?all=true]` and `GET /v1/admin/tasks/{id}`, gated like every admin route, off the ledgers the CLI writes through the same view -- **the body byte for byte what `--output-format json` prints**. `400` for an id that is not one, `404` for none, `500` for an unreadable ledger with a message that never names its path (the ledger's own error does), and an unreadable ledger left out of the list as `task list` leaves it out. `task run`, `resume`, `halt` and `cancel` have no route: 76 admin rows, two new.
- [x] **Machine mode's task events** (`machine/json_reporter`, whose include rule in `harness.layering` now admits `tasks/`). `task run|resume --output-format stream-json` drives the task as ever with a `JsonReporter` as each turn's reporter: `session` first, each turn's ordinary events ending in its `result` -- or an `error` (the provider's message, `cancelled`, the question nobody was present to answer) -- and around them the task's lifecycle, **one event per ledger transition**, each carrying that transition as the ledger wrote it (`transition`) and the task's id: `task_started` for `started`/`resumed` (with `resumed`, every earlier transition as `history`, and the task's whole view -- a front-end joining at a resume needs no other source), `task_plan` for `plan_started`/`plan_recorded` (the plan turn, then the plan), `task_round` for `round_started`/`round_ended` (the round's `TurnView`, then each check's state and the rounds used), `task_finished` for `finished` (status, reason, the final view); `created`, written before the run, reaches a driver as `task_started`'s history. And `task_grant` -- the round, tool, target and `by: grant` -- for each call the task's grant let through, after its turn and before its round ends. The person's `[task]` lines, the notices and the outcome go to stderr; the exit code is the task's.
- [x] **Told only once written** (`tasks/runner`): `RunRequest::on_transition` is called for each transition once the ledger on disk holds it, in order -- one the ledger failed to take is never told, and those the task came in with are history, never told again -- and `on_grant` beside the run's own "allowed by this task's grant" line. The stream is the ledger's transition sequence one for one by construction, not by a second list kept in step.
- [x] **Nobody asked in machine mode.** A machine-mode run reads no input, so its gate has no confirm function and its `ask_user` no person, even with a terminal attached: an ungranted `ask` tool denies (`by: nobody`) and a question with no declared answer ends the task, as on any pipe.
- [x] **The parity table** (`httpserver/parity_test`): a fifth classification, **served** -- a read with the admin route that serves it, checked as a twin's route is (registered, flagged admin, `401` unauthenticated) -- for `task status` and `task list`; `task run|resume|halt|cancel` stay the carve-outs 27h placed, and a new case sends every mutating method to every task path a client might guess (`/v1/admin/tasks/{id}/halt`, `…/run`, …) and requires every task route to be a GET.
- [x] **The references, under their pins**: [machine-mode.md](../reference/machine-mode.md) gains "A task's run" (the five events in the JSONL fence and the reference table, the one-for-one rule, the view, a declared answer in no event, nothing asked) and the reads' contract under "Everything else is a CLI command"; [http-api.md](../reference/http-api.md) the two routes and "task control is CLI-only". `cli.machine_schema_conformance` now counts 17 emitted types and `cli.http_api_conformance` 84 routes.
- [x] **24 new test cases** -- `tasks/view_test` (6: the golden document of a task with every kind of record, a declared answer in the ledger and in no view nor any layout path, the lock's say over `process`, nothing run before a round completes, no policy without tools, the listing), `tasks/runner_test` (+1: each transition told once the ledger holds it, in order, `created` never, a resumed task from `resumed` on, each grant's use; and a ledger that cannot be written telling nothing), `machine/machine_mode_test` (+5: each transition kind's event and fields, a resumed `task_started`, `task_grant`, a declared answer in no event, the read format), `cli/task_test` (+7: the machine-mode stream -- its shape, the history and transitions equal to the ledger's, the grant, a driver's reconstruction from the stream equal to the status document; a resumed stream; the JSON reads byte-identical to the admin bodies with **row parity** against the human view; the formats each surface refuses; the process in both renderings; answers paired; the listing's `--all`), `httpserver/admin_tasks_test` (4), `httpserver/parity_test` (+1), the leak sweep extended over every new surface, `serve_test`'s route count; on the real binary `cli.task_lifecycle` grew the machine-mode run and a machine-mode resume, `cli.serve_lifecycle` the served reads, and `cli.chat_typeahead_and_crash_safety` a `task-machine` case under a pseudo-terminal.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | **The view in `tasks/view.h/.cpp`** (Business); the events and the reads' framing in `machine/json_reporter` (its include rule widened to `tasks/`); the routes in `httpserver/admin_tasks.h/.cpp` (`httpserver` and `machine` link `tasks`); the command in `cli/task_cmd`; **`render/json_report` untouched** *(2026-10-05)* | The spec predates the layers. `render/json_report` renders a model's JSON report as Markdown -- it owns no document shape -- while the training track's served shapes live in `training/`, the domain; a view the CLI, machine mode and the server all render has to sit where all three can reach it, and `machine/` naming the event types is what `cli.machine_schema_conformance` reads. |
| The event vocabulary, settled against the ledger | **One event per transition, carrying it**: `started`/`resumed` → `task_started`, `plan_started`/`plan_recorded` → `task_plan`, `round_started`/`round_ended` → `task_round`, `finished` → `task_finished`; `created` in `task_started`'s `history`; `task_grant` per grant used, after its turn *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed five names, each carrying its transition's ledger fields. Emitting `created` as an event of its own would have made a new task open with two `task_started`s; as history, `history` then each event's `transition` *is* the ledger's sequence, which is the guardrail stated as data. |
| When an event is sent | **Only once the ledger on disk holds its transition** -- the runner's `on_transition` after a successful write *(2026-10-05)* | "Every surface renders the ledger": an event for a transition the ledger failed to take would describe a task no reader of the ledger can see. |
| What the events carry beyond the transition | `task_started` and `task_finished` **the task's whole view**; `task_plan`/`task_round` their turn, an ended round each check's state and the rounds used *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed "current ledger state first" for a resume, and an end state a driver can check its reconstruction against -- the e2e and the command test both rebuild the state from the events and compare it with `task status --output-format json`. |
| The JSON document and the served view | **One document**, byte for byte the admin body, **with no declared answer**; the human `task status` alone shows it *(2026-10-05)* | The spec: the served view says an answer existed, never what; and 28h's rule that the JSON a host gets from the command line is the JSON a remote client gets. A host logs what it reads as readily as a remote client does. The view types have no slot for it, so neither can carry it by accident. |
| An answered question in a view | **The question and who answered it** -- the person's answer withheld too, not only the declared one *(2026-10-05)* | The conservative reading: an answer typed at a terminal is no more the served view's than a declared one, and the one type cannot tell the two apart by construction otherwise. |
| `policy` without tools | **`null`** *(2026-10-05)* | The human view shows no policy for a task without tools; a default policy in the document would be a fact the human view does not state. |
| `process` and `interrupted` | **From the task lock's holder, only while the ledger says planning or running** -- the human status words' own rule, now the view's *(2026-10-05)* | One derivation of "is it running now", where the human words and the document both read it. |
| Machine mode and a person at the terminal | **Nobody is asked**: no confirm function, no person's `ask_user`, terminal or not *(2026-10-05)* | Machine mode's stdin is the protocol's, and `task run` reads none; a prompt on the terminal would be an input channel the protocol does not have. Deny-by-default is the conservative side of 27i's "policy adds to the human path": in machine mode the human path is the driver, which grants in advance. Held under a pseudo-terminal (`task-machine`). |
| A turn that does not finish, in machine mode | **An `error` event** -- the provider's message, `cancelled`, or the question nobody answered -- in place of its `result` *(2026-10-05)* | `complete`'s own convention for a cancel; the machine-readable half of what stderr says, with `task_finished` following. |
| The reads' format words | **`text` or `json`** on `task status`/`list`; **`text` or `stream-json`** on `task run`/`resume`; each refuses the other's *(2026-10-05)* | 28h's confirmed flag and its "one document per invocation -- reads, not streams; JSONL stays machine mode's". The parse and the framing live in `machine/` for 28h's reads to reuse. |
| The admin list's `all` | **`?all=true`** (`false` the default), anything else `400` *(2026-10-05)* | The admin plane's existing boolean form (`purge=true`, `anonymize=true`), refusing a typo as `?kind=` does. |
| An unreadable ledger, served | **Left out of the list; `500` for the one, its message naming no path** *(2026-10-05)* | `task list` names the problem on stderr with the ledger's path; a served response never carries a path into the private layout. |
| The parity classification | **A fifth kind, `served`**, for `task status`/`list`, checked as a twin's route is; the four task carve-outs unchanged *(2026-10-05)* | "Reads served, control carved out by name": read-only said nothing about the route that now serves them, and a twin means a mutation. 27h already placed the carve-outs (the brief's "grows by exactly the task control verbs" was satisfied then); this item adds the test that none of them has a route. |
| The human reads | **Rendered from the view**, byte-identical *(2026-10-05)* | "Nothing computes task state a second way": the check states, the self-report, the rounds used and the running/interrupted words were the command's own derivations; now the view's, which the document and the events share. |
| 28g | **Not shipped; nothing done for it** *(2026-10-05)* | Additive either order: the schema artifact will read the same declaration `cli.machine_schema_conformance` reads, the five task types among it. |

**Verified on the real binary.** In a scratch `APOGEE_HOME`, scripted mocks, recall off: `cli.task_lifecycle` runs a task granted a write under `--output-format stream-json` with stdin `/dev/null` -- every stdout line JSON, `session` first, three turns each ended in a `result`, the grant's `task_grant` before its round ended, the person's lines and the outcome on stderr only -- and holds `task_started`'s history followed by every later event's `transition` equal to the ledger's `transitions`, and a driver's reconstruction from the events alone (the transitions' statuses and times, each turn, the plan, the checks, the reason) equal to `task status --output-format json`, which `task_finished` carries too; `task list --output-format json` names the human list's rows in order; and the halted task, resumed under `--output-format stream-json`, opens with `task_started`, `resumed: true` and the whole history before it, the same equalities holding. `cli.serve_lifecycle` runs a task with the CLI and reads it over a real socket: `GET /v1/admin/tasks` and `/v1/admin/tasks/{id}` byte for byte what `task list`/`task status --output-format json` print, `401` without the bearer, and `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` at the task paths and at `…/resume`, `…/halt`, `…/cancel`, `…/run` answering nothing in the `2xx` range. Under a pseudo-terminal (`task-machine`), the same task as `task-attended` in machine mode asks nothing -- `run_command` denied `by: nobody`, the question ending the task `failed`, the process ending by itself. By hand: `__complete task status --output-format ""` offers `text` and `json`, `task run … --output-format ""` `text` and `stream-json`; `task list --output-format json` on an empty home prints `{"data":[],"object":"list","total":0}`. `cli.machine_schema_conformance` (17 emitted types, 3 accepted) and `cli.http_api_conformance` (84 routes) pass in both directions. The full suite through `make test` (llama.cpp on): 100% of 2555 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before; `make format-check` clean; `clang-tidy` over every file this item touched reports no error (the ownership gate) -- the warnings left are kinds the tree already carries (cognitive complexity on the command's composition root and the runner's turn, designated-initializer, const-correctness and optional-access suggestions in the tests).

**Guardrails, each mutation-tested.** 46 mutants against the final code, each applied in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared checkout), rebuilt and run against the unit suites, then the e2e, the conformance and layering checks, and for the two that reach a terminal the pseudo-terminal check -- **46 caught**. The view: `process` for another task's lock or a dead holder, never interrupted, the lock read whatever the status, an answered question carrying its answer, the policy carrying the declared answer, checks from the first round rather than the newest completed, a check's detail dropped, the self-report never read, an in-flight round's outcome empty, the list limit ignored, the total counting only those shown, a policy without tools, the plan counted as a round, every check counted passed. The runner: the history told as the run's, no transition told, one told though the ledger failed, every permit told as a grant, no grant told. The events: a history including its own transition, a resume said as a start, the newest transition in place of the index's, `created` emitted as a start, an ended round without its checks, the plan never sent, `task_finished` without its view, the declared answer on every event, a round event carrying the wrong turn, a grant said as the config's. The reads: `stream-json` accepted on a read, the document pretty-printed (no longer the admin body). The command: a machine-mode turn without its `result`, the outcome on machine mode's stdout, no `session` first, the person prompted and asked at a terminal in machine mode (both caught by the pseudo-terminal check alone), no task events wired, the status document blind to the lock, the list document ignoring `--all`, every answered question shown the first answer. The admin plane: `?all` ignored, a `500` naming the ledger's path, an id never validated, the view blind to the lock, and a task control route added to the mux.

**Real weights.** Not run, and none was asked for: nothing here changes how a model is called -- every surface renders the ledger the runner already writes, and each round is still the chat's own turn.

**Not verified.** Windows (the e2e, the served reads over a socket and the pseudo-terminal check are POSIX; the view, the events and the routes are portable code). A front-end consuming the stream live -- the e2e reads it after the run; the per-event flush is `JsonReporter`'s own, unchanged. A task killed mid-turn under machine mode: the stream simply ends, and the next `task resume --output-format stream-json` opens with the whole history (the resume path is the one verified, after a halt). 28g's schema artifact, not yet shipped, does not yet carry the task events.

**Left for the owner.** Readings this item chose, each in the table and each a one-place change if vetoed: the served view and the JSON document withholding a person's answers as well as the declared one; machine mode prompting nobody even at a terminal; and `created` delivered as `task_started`'s history rather than as an event of its own. The parity table's training reads (`train status`, `train versions`, `train pipeline status`, `train cycle status`) are still classified read-only though `/v1/admin/training/*` serves them -- the new `served` kind could name their routes too; left as they were, since they are not this item's.

## Milestone AE — The code graph

**Goal.** Milestone Y's knowledge graph is built by a model: one structured call per chunk of prose, the right tool for documents and decisions and the wrong one for source code, whose structure is *in* the code. A parser recovers it deterministically, locally and for nothing -- no hallucinated edge, no spend. This milestone adds a second extraction *source* to the one graph layer (Graphify's shape, adopted as a source, never a second graph system): tree-sitter parses a source tree into the same `kg_*` tables, every edge saying whether it was parsed or asserted, and a code-only graph is built, updated, clustered and walked with **no model, no key, no embedder and no network** -- the user's call (2026-09-30), held by tests rather than by care. Track 27's graph items open here: 27k the extractor; 27l navigation, 27m the artifacts and 27n–27p the attachment code graph build on it.

### 2026-10-05 — `code-graph-extraction` (backlog item 27k): tree-sitter into the one graph layer, model-free end to end

**What was built**

- [x] **The pins** (`third_party/tree-sitter/CMakeLists.txt`): the tree-sitter runtime `v0.27.0` and **twelve grammars, each its own pin** -- C `v0.24.2`, C++ `v0.23.4`, Python `v0.25.0`, JavaScript `v0.25.0` (JSX included), TypeScript and TSX `v0.23.2` (one repository, two grammars), Go `v0.25.0`, Rust `v0.24.2`, Java `v0.23.5`, C# `v0.23.5`, Ruby `v0.23.1`, Bash `v0.25.1` -- the broad set from day one (the user's call, 2026-10-03). Each is an archive of the **exact commit** its release tag names (checked against `git ls-remote`), `URL_HASH`-checked, fetched at configure and never found on the system, and compiled here as a plain C11 static library -- the runtime as its one-file amalgamation, a grammar as its `parser.c` and `scanner.c` -- never through upstream's CMake, warnings off, headers `SYSTEM`, read-only, out of the lint and format scope. All MIT; all ABI 14 or 15, within the runtime's 13–15. In every build, the no-llama and unit-test builds included (`add_subdirectory(tree-sitter)` before llama.cpp's early return), since the graph is model-free by design and the suite pins its extraction. Every pin, tag, licence and size in `third_party/README.md`.
- [x] **The one boundary** (`graph/code_parser.h/.cpp`): `CodeParser` holds the parser, each parse's tree, the compiled query and its cursor in `unique_ptr`s with their deleters, and nothing of tree-sitter crosses it -- out come `CodeMatch`/`CodeCapture`, plain names, byte ranges and 1-based lines. The text predicates the C library leaves to its host (`#eq?`, `#not-eq?`, `#any-of?`, `#not-any-of?`) are evaluated here; a `_` capture exists only for a predicate and never reaches the extractor; an ERROR node marks a parse partial while a MISSING one -- a token assumed, no text lost, which the pinned C++ grammar inserts for every `= {}` default argument -- does not. A query that does not compile against its pinned grammar throws naming the language and the offset. It is the only file in the tree that includes `tree_sitter/` (`harness.layering`).
- [x] **The roster as data** (`graph/code_languages.h/.cpp`): per language its `--lang` name and aliases, extensions (a `.h` is C++ when the tree holds C++), the pinned grammar, its separator, how it **qualifies a name** (one global namespace for C, C++ and Ruby with C/C++ internal linkage qualified by its file; the module path for Python; file-scoped for JavaScript, TypeScript and Bash; the declared package or namespace for Java and C#; the package directory for Go; the crate module for Rust), its builtin and wrapper types, and its tree-sitter **query** in one small capture vocabulary the extractor reads the same way for every grammar (TSX adds JSX through `extra_query`, which the TypeScript grammar it shares a query with cannot compile). `code_extractor_id` -- language, grammar pin, `kCodeExtractorVersion` -- is recorded with every file's facts, so a moved pin or an edited query re-parses that language on the next update instead of mixing two extractors' facts.
- [x] **One file's facts** (`graph/code_extract.h/.cpp`): definitions -- modules, classes, functions and declarations -- with their qualified names, nesting and signatures (the header up to the body, whitespace collapsed, clipped at 200 codepoints); imports (module, relative, namespace, symbol); calls and type references as written (generic arguments dropped, `?.` read as `.`, `->` kept); bases; and the declared types of parameters, locals and fields. A C/C++ cast or operator is not a call, a lower-case JSX element is the host's and a component rendered is a call, and a call inside an import (`require('fs')`, `source lib.sh`) is the import. Pure and deterministic over (path, bytes, grammar), and cached as JSON.
- [x] **Resolution, deterministic** (`graph/code_resolve.h/.cpp`): every file's facts in, one graph out. A reference links only when the lookup the language itself would make finds **exactly** that qualified name -- the enclosing scopes outward, a class's bases where a bare name may name a member, an import's binding or the namespace it opened, `this`/`self`, a declared type (through a smart pointer only with `->` in C++, implicitly in Rust and for Python's `Optional`), a field's type for a chain -- and anything else is an edge to an **unresolved `name` node** carrying the text as written (`std::max`, `json.dumps`, `.push_back` for a member call on an unknown receiver), counted per kind, never guessed: two candidates (a module two files' paths end with) are as unresolved as none. Nodes `file`, `module`, `class`, `function`, `name`; relations `defined_in` (to the enclosing class or function, else the file; a file to its innermost module; a member defined outside its class -- C++ out of line, a Go method, a Rust impl's function -- to that class too, by qualification), `imports`, `calls`, `inherits`, `references` (a definition's interface: parameters, returns, fields; a local's type resolves calls but is not an edge); each mention a `file:line` under its source member, each edge its sites. Recursion records no self edge. The result depends on the set of files, never their order.
- [x] **The build, over an injected file list** (`graph/code_build.h/.cpp`): `build_source(store, members, options)` takes `SourceMember`s -- a label, the files relative to their root, and a reader -- and never walks a directory itself, so `graph build --source` and an attachment (27n) hand it the same list and get the same graph. **Incremental by content hash**: a file whose SHA-256 and extractor id match its `kg_state` row is not parsed again -- its cached facts are used -- while the whole tree is re-linked every build (a rename in one file changes what another's call resolves to) and the code layer synced in one transaction, so an update stores exactly what a fresh build would. Everything it cannot use is **skipped and named**, never silently and never a failure: an unsupported language (by extension, or none), one `--lang` leaves out, unreadable, over 2 MiB, binary (a NUL in the first 8 KiB), unparseable; a file parsed around a syntax error is used and named partial. Vendored and build directories -- `third_party`, `third-party`, `thirdparty`, `vendor`, `node_modules`, `bower_components`, `__pycache__`, `site-packages`, `_deps`, `CMakeFiles`, `venv`, `target`, `cmake-build-*` -- are left out whole wherever they sit and counted per directory. A file's state is written as it is parsed, so a cancelled build (checked between files) keeps its work and the next one links it; a build owns its graph's membership, a tree it was not handed forgotten unless `prune_other_members` is off; a damaged cache is a re-parse; a dry run parses and links and stores nothing. No generation closure, no embedder: nothing it includes can reach a model.
- [x] **Schema v6** (`embedstore/graph.cpp`, `graph_code.h/.cpp`): every edge gains **`origin`** and **`confidence`** (additive, the chunk-metadata-column precedent -- an older store's edges read `inferred` with no confidence); every prose writer stamps `inferred` (`upsert_edge`, the record pass's `ensure_edge`); the code layer stamps `extracted` at 1.0, and an inferred edge a parse later states is promoted, never the other way. `kg_state` gains a code file's `content_hash` and cached `facts` beside the prose rows, and every prose plan, staleness check and reconcile now reads and prunes prose rows alone. The code layer's own provenance: `kg_code_mentions` (a definition, declaration or reference at `file:line`, under its member) and `kg_edge_sites` (each place an edge is stated; its weight is their count). `sync_code_graph` converges every code row in one transaction -- a surviving node keeps its id and whatever hangs off it, a changed description clears its vector, a metadata change does not, an edge no site states and a node nothing mentions go -- and leaves the prose layer exactly as it was. A node's salience counts both kinds of mention, in every recount. A **code node's identity is its exact qualified name, case included** (`code_identity`; prose keeps its fold), and `find_nodes` matches it exactly or, when nothing is spelled so, by the fold. `graph_dump` renders the whole graph as canonical text with no ids, vectors or times -- what "an update converges on a fresh build" is held to.
- [x] **The pipeline downstream, model-free**: `graph/communities` with no summariser clusters alone -- every community stored with its membership and no summary (so no pseudo-chunk and nothing to embed), the absence counted in `summaries_absent`, an existing summary never lost, and a later run with a summariser filling exactly the ones still without; `all_edges` and the expansion walk leave `name` nodes out (a name is not structure, and every caller of `.push_back` would otherwise cluster as one theme or crowd the context); dedupe never considers a code node, folds origin-aware (an extracted edge never merges down, and its sites move with it), and `Store::dedupe_scope` says what each layer has to merge. Retrieval-time expansion over a graph holding code renders a code entity with its line -- `pkg.service.make_user (function, pkg/service.py:6): def make_user(name: str) -> User` -- and a parsed relation as `A —[calls·extracted]→ B`, a model's keeping its bare form, under the existing 1,500-codepoint budget.
- [x] **The command line** (`cli/graph.cpp`, `operations/graph_sources.h/.cpp`): a named graph may hold **source trees** -- `sources:` (absolute, `~` and `${VAR}` expanded) and `languages:` on its `graphs:` entry, written by `config add-graph --sources DIR --languages a,b` and by **`graph build --source DIR --graph NAME [--lang L]...`**, which records the tree (and the entry, when new) through the one config editor and builds: the trees parsed first, no provider built for them, then the graph's collections extracted as ever. `graph build NAME` builds a mixed graph; **`graph update NAME`** re-parses only what changed and never makes a model call. The summary says files used by language, parsed and unchanged, forgotten, the excluded directories, partial parses, references resolved and unresolved per kind, the code layer's change, every skipped file grouped by reason (`--show-skipped` names past ten), and a tree that is gone or offers no file (inside a repository, a tree git ignores is read as git reads it: as nothing). After a run `communities` lists the twenty largest and counts the rest -- a code graph clusters into hundreds. `stats` reports **the extracted/inferred split** and the code layer (files per language, `file:line` mentions, unresolved names); `show` lists a code node's definitions and declarations at their lines and each parsed edge's first sites; `communities` clusters with no model when no generation backend resolves, or with `--no-summaries`, the summaries reported absent (the metered-default refusal names `--no-summaries`); `dedupe` reports per layer -- `Code entities: N -- merged by exact qualified name as they were built (M stated at more than one place, one node each); never by resemblance.` and `Prose entities: vector dedupe skipped -- … ; nothing to merge.` The trees are walked with the one attachment walk (`git ls-files` inside a repository, hidden entries out) and labelled by directory name; `validate_named_graph` holds them absolute, distinctly named, never a member collection's name, and only vendored languages. The doctor checks each tree and language.
- [x] **The control plane** (`httpserver/admin_graph*.cpp`): the `graphs:` slice takes `sources` and `languages` (a tree normalized as the CLI records it, so the bytes match); the build route parses a named graph's trees first, the code counts on the job's `code` field, and a graph of trees alone runs as a job **with no generation backend served**; `"update": true` is `graph update`'s twin (the parity table's new row); `POST …/communities` takes `"summaries": false` and clusters with no model -- with summaries and nothing to write them, the `501` stands and names the flag; `POST …/dedupe` carries `code_entities`, `code_identity_merges` and `prose_skipped`; stats carry the origin split and the code layer. All in [http-api.md](../reference/http-api.md).
- [x] **The layering**: two new rules in `harness.layering` -- `graph/code_*` may include only one another, `embedstore/`, `contracts/sha256.h` and `contracts/cancellation.h`, so "zero model calls" is a property of the include graph; and only `graph/code_parser.cpp` may include `tree_sitter/`, a check that requires seeing it there. Each verified against a planted violation.
- [x] **59 new Catch2 cases** (2,615 tests in `make test`, the e2e among them), and on the real binary **`cli.code_graph_lifecycle`** (`code_graph_e2e.sh`). **Every vendored grammar has a golden fixture**: a mini-repo per language under `tests/fixtures/code_graph/<lang>/` whose whole graph -- every node with its description, metadata and `file:line` mentions, every edge with its origin and sites -- must equal `<lang>.golden` byte for byte, each reviewed by hand when it was cut (`APOGEE_CODE_GRAPH_GOLDENS=<dir>` regenerates them outside the tree for review).
