**What they cost**, measured on the development Mac (Apple clang, `RelWithDebInfo`): about **8 s** of CPU to compile the runtime and all twelve grammars one after another -- under 1% of a no-llama build's compile work, and in a parallel build no longer than its slowest object -- plus about 7 MB downloaded at the first configure (122 MB unpacked); about **17.6 MB** of code and parse tables in the executable (the stripped binary 21.4 → 39.1 MB; C# 5.1, C++ 3.3, Ruby 2.0, TSX 1.4, TypeScript 1.3, Bash 1.3, Rust 1.1, C 0.6, Python 0.4, JavaScript 0.4, Java 0.4, Go 0.2, the runtime 0.1), but only **+1.4 MB compressed** (gzip -9: 8.50 → 9.87 MB), the tables compressing about thirteenfold. MinGW-w64 GCC 16 compiles the same C sources warning-free in about 11 s.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | **`graph/code_{languages,parser,extract,resolve,build}`** in the graph module (the spec's `code_extract`/`code_resolve` and a `code_build` beside `build` rather than inside it), **`embedstore/graph_code`** for the storage, **`operations/graph_sources`** for the walk both surfaces share; tests under `tests/{business,data,presentation}/…` *(2026-10-05)* | The spec predates the four layers. The code build shares nothing with the prose build but the store -- no extractor closure, no chunk fingerprint -- so a function of its own keeps the prose loop untouched; the tree walk is a surface concern both the CLI and the admin plane need, which is what `operations/` is for. |
| Where a source tree lives | **On a named graph's entry** (`sources:`, `languages:`); `graph build --source DIR --graph NAME` writes it through the one editor; a collection's own graph takes none (`'notes' is a collection -- a source tree builds into a named graph`) *(2026-10-05)* | A tree belongs to no collection; the named graph is where several members already meet, and the confirmed "a source build and a collection build may share one named graph". The entry is the enablement, as for collections. |
| A tree's label | **Its directory name**; two trees with one name, or a tree named like a member collection, refused *(2026-10-05)* | Every mention, site and state row is recorded under a member label; a short stable name reads well in `show` (`cli: source/…:198`) and an absolute path would churn with a checkout's location. |
| Code identity | **The exact qualified name, case included** (`code_identity`); `find_nodes` exact first, then the fold *(2026-10-05)* | The prose fold would merge Go's `Parse` and `parse` into one node -- an invented link, which the spec forbids. The two layers' types are disjoint, so the keys never meet. Found reviewing the first cut, which folded. |
| A declaration and its definition, two trees' copies | **One node**, every mention kept *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed exact qualified-name identity is the code dedupe; `dedupe` reports how many such merges the build made. |
| What a member call on an unknown receiver names | **`.member`** -- through an import, the name it reached (`json.dumps`) *(2026-10-05)* | A node per variable name (`user.greet`, `u.greet`) would be noise standing for one unknown thing; the member's name is what is known. |
| Containment | `defined_in` the enclosing class or function, else the file; a file `defined_in` its innermost module; a member defined outside its class also `defined_in` that class *(2026-10-05)* | Namespaces and packages span files, so a module contains files; an out-of-line member belongs to its class whatever file holds its body (Go and Rust only ever define methods outside). |
| Locals | **Resolve member calls; not `references` edges** *(2026-10-05)* | A definition's references are its interface -- parameters, returns, fields, bases; a local's type is its implementation and the noisiest kind. |
| Builtins | Each language's own types, and `java.lang`'s, never references *(2026-10-05)* | `String` was a five-way hub on the Java fixture, standing for nothing the tree holds. |
| JSX | **A component rendered is a call**; a lower-case element is the host's and dropped *(2026-10-05)* | A React tree's composition is its call graph; `<div>` is not a reference to anything. |
| The incremental unit | **SHA-256 of the bytes + the extractor id**, per file; facts cached in `kg_state`; the whole tree re-linked and synced every build *(2026-10-05)* | Parsing is the cost, linking is global. A bare `touch` -- bytes unchanged -- re-parses nothing, which is the spec's "only what changed" taken at its word. |
| Writes | **Each parsed file's state its own write; the sync one transaction** *(2026-10-05)* | A cancelled or killed build keeps its parsing work and the next links it; the graph a reader sees is always one sync's whole result. |
| What is left out | **The vendored/build list above, wherever it sits; `build/` not on it**; 2 MiB per file; a NUL in the first 8 KiB is binary *(2026-10-05)* | Inside a repository git already ignores build output; `build` is a real source directory name often enough (Go's `go/build`) that leaving it out would drop code. A generated table or a bundled blob over 2 MiB is not code anyone navigates. |
| Membership | **A build owns its graph's trees**: one removed from `sources:` -- or gone from the disk, named -- is forgotten *(2026-10-05)* | Collections' reconcile converges on the config the same way. |
| Communities with no model | **A null summariser clusters alone**; the CLI does so when no generation backend resolves, or with `--no-summaries`; over HTTP only with `"summaries": false` -- the existing `501` kept otherwise, naming the flag *(2026-10-05)* | Summaries are the paid extra the spec lets a code graph skip, reported absent and never required. The `501` was an existing, mutation-tested contract; a flag is additive where reinterpreting it is not. |
| A metered default for `communities` | **Still refused**, the refusal naming `--no-summaries` *(2026-10-05)* | A prose graph's rule is unchanged; the way out is now said. |
| `graph update` | **Named graphs with trees only**; its twin is `"update": true` on the build route *(2026-10-05)* | A collection's own graph has no trees; a second route for the same build would be two definitions of it. |
| Every existing writer stamps | **`inferred`**, the record pass's `concerns`/`supersedes` edges included *(2026-10-05)* | The spec's rule. The record pass's edges hang on a model's entities. |
| A parsed edge in an injected section | **`A —[calls·extracted]→ B`**; a model's unchanged *(2026-10-05)* | Provenance labelled for the model as for a reader, in 27l's notation, without moving a byte of what prose graphs already inject. |
| The roster's peers | **Rust, Java, C#, Ruby, Bash** beside the spec's named core *(2026-10-05)* | The user's "common peers": the next most used languages with maintained official grammars. Each grammar costs its tables in the binary (below), so the list stops there; another is a pin and a fixture. |

**The acceptance run over this repository.** In a sandboxed `APOGEE_HOME` with **no backend configured**, no key and the network pointed at a closed port, `apogee graph build --source lib/src/cli --graph apogee-code` from the repository root -- so the tree is walked by `git ls-files` and the build output is never seen -- recorded the entry and used **871 files** (C++ 772, Python 58, Bash 21, and the fixtures' C 2, C# 2, Go 2, Java 3, JavaScript 3, Ruby 2, Rust 2, TSX 1, TypeScript 3), left `third_party/` out whole (120 files, the vendored converter among them), named the 113 it could not use by reason (CMake, Markdown, YAML, text and JSON fixtures, the completion scripts, a SQLite fixture), and parsed one around a syntax error (`source/data/backends/sampling.cpp`, named partial). It stored **9,840 nodes** -- 5,633 functions, 1,422 classes, 871 files, 49 modules and 1,865 unresolved names -- and **63,742 edges, every one extracted**: `graph stats` says `Origin: 63742 extracted (parsed from source), 0 inferred (asserted by a model)`, beside 90,109 `file:line` mentions. Of 124,532 references, 44,209 resolved and 80,323 stay names -- calls 33,052 of 95,575 (the rest the standard library's, and member calls on receivers whose type is not declared, `auto` among them), types 8,017 of 21,470, imports 3,001 of 7,333, bases 139 of 154. **3.2 s** for the whole build (2.75 s of CPU) on the development Mac; an `update` with nothing changed **1.6 s** -- parsing nothing, re-linking and syncing the tree; `communities` 450 clusters with no model in 0.5 s, the summaries reported absent; `dedupe` 7,975 code entities, 2,301 of them stated at more than one place (a declaration and its definition), the prose pass skipped and said. `graph show apogee-code apogee::graph::build_source` names its declaration (`code_build.h:149-151`) and definition (`code_build.cpp:201-340`) and its callers across files -- `apogee::commands::build_graph_sources` at `source/presentation/operations/graph_sources.cpp:84`, and the tests' helpers -- each at its line. In a copy of the tree with one file edited, `update` parsed exactly that file (`1 parsed, 870 unchanged`, 1.7 s) and its `graph stats` equalled a fresh build's.

**Verified on the real binary.** `cli.code_graph_lifecycle`, in a scratch `APOGEE_HOME` with zero backends, no key and every proxy at a closed port: `graph build --source` over a copy of the Python fixture tree records the entry, names the Lua file it skipped and leaves `third_party/` out; `stats` reports every edge extracted and none inferred; `show` gives a method's definition at `pkg/models.py:10-11`, its caller in another file (`<- pkg.service.run … at pkg/service.py:12`) and its callee through the base class; an edit is parsed alone by `update` (`1 parsed, 3 unchanged`) and the graph's `stats` equal a fresh build's; the same bytes written again parse nothing; `communities` clusters with `no model; summaries absent (no generation backend is configured)`; `dedupe` says code merged by identity and the prose pass skipped. Then a scripted mock to answer and another that extracts nothing, the graph given a collection beside its tree: the mixed build parses no code again, and `complete --rag notes "make_user"` injects `[Knowledge graph: code]` with `pkg.service.make_user (function, pkg/service.py:6): def make_user(name: str) -> User` and the parsed relations as `·extracted`, the status line counting the graph entities -- **retrieval-time expansion over a code-bearing graph, under the existing budget, labelled with its provenance**. MinGW-w64 GCC 16 cross-compiles the runtime and all twelve grammars, and every new first-party C++ file with `-Wall -Wextra -Wshadow`, without a warning (one, a missing designated initializer, fixed). The full suite through `make test` (llama.cpp on): 100% of 2,615 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before; `make format-check` clean; `clang-tidy` over every file this item touched reports no error (the ownership gate) -- the warnings left in the new files are kinds the tree already carries (cognitive complexity in the resolver, the extractor and the CLI's composition root; designated-initializer suggestions on the roster table; optional-access and const-correctness notes in the tests).

**Guardrails, each mutation-tested.** 73 mutants against the final code, each applied in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared checkout), rebuilt and run against the code graph's suites -- **66 caught outright, 6 caught after their tests were strengthened, 1 equivalent and removed as dead code.** The strengthened six: dedupe considering code nodes survived because the test's two same-vector functions were looked up by exact name, which now finds one -- the test vectorises both through the fold and requires two; an unsummarised community writing an empty pseudo-chunk survived a search for text it could not hold -- the test now asks for the community's chunk itself; a package's `__init__` read as a module of its own survived a fixture whose `__init__` defined nothing -- a resolve test now calls through one; a relative import inside `__init__` survived because a unique suffix match found the module anyway -- a second `util` makes the package-relative lookup the only way; an include matched tree-wide by two files survived with no fixture holding two -- a resolve test now does; and dropping the resolver's sort of its input survived a test over files no lookup could tell apart -- a C# partial class declaring one field in two files with two types now can. The equivalent one: `delete_graph`'s explicit deletes of the code mentions and edge sites, which the schema's `ON DELETE CASCADE` performs -- removed (the Milestone Y precedent). Four more were planted violations for the layering rules -- the harness included by the code build, the loop by the resolver, tree-sitter by the extractor and by a surface -- each failing `harness.layering`. The mutations: a prose upsert, or the record pass's `ensure_edge`, stamping extracted; the migration reading old edges as extracted; a changed code description keeping its vector; an edge nothing states kept; a sync retiring prose nodes; an inferred edge never promoted; code identity folding case; `find_nodes` listing folded code nodes beside the exact one; a prose plan, or a reconcile, reading or pruning code state rows; community edges, or expansion seeds, including unresolved names; dedupe considering code nodes; a fold demoting an extracted edge, or leaving its sites behind; the scope counting names as entities, or not saying the prose skip; an unsummarised community writing a pseudo-chunk or waiting for a vector; salience ignoring code mentions; stats' split wrong; the content hash or the extractor id ignored; a damaged cache failing the build; a gone file never forgotten; vendored directories, binary or oversized files parsed; a dry run recording state; cancellation ignored; an unowned member forgotten anyway; `--lang` ignored, or an alias selecting nothing; an unsupported file skipped silently; a partial parse not named; a MISSING token counted as an error; the text predicates ignored; a `_` capture reaching the extractor; a host JSX element a call; a `require` call also a call; a C `static` or an anonymous namespace not internal; a signature never clipped; `__init__` its own module; a relative import in `__init__` one level up; an ambiguous module or include picking one; recursion recording a self edge; an out-of-line member not its class's; the files' order not normalised; a member never found through a base; an unresolved member call keeping its variable's name; a `.h` always C; `String` a reference; no summariser calling a null function; a parsed relation not marked, or a code entity without its line, in the injected section; `communities` building providers with nothing to build; a relative `--source` recorded relative; a tree building into a collection's name; a dry run writing the entry; the HTTP `update` flag ignored; `"summaries": false` still needing a backend; an HTTP tree recorded unnormalised; a relative tree, or two trees under one name, accepted; the doctor passing a missing tree.

**Real weights.** Not run, and none was asked for: the code graph makes no model call by construction (the layering rule holds it), and the one model-facing path it touches -- the injected section -- is verified on a scripted mock.

**Not verified.** Windows and Linux at run time: MinGW cross-compiles every tree-sitter source and every new C++ file warning-free, and CI's unit-test runners build them, but the e2e is POSIX and no graph was built on either. Each grammar beyond its fixture: one mini-repo per language exercises the common constructs, and what the queries do not capture -- C preprocessor macros, C++ template specializations and calls through `auto`, Python decorators and dynamic attributes, Ruby's dynamic dispatch, a C++ `using` declaration inside a namespace (bound as written, not looked up from its namespace) -- stays an unresolved name, counted. A tree outside any repository that holds a `build/` directory (walked; not on the excluded list). A very large tree: every file's facts are held at once while linking (this repository's 871 files, easily).

**Left for the owner.** **The binary cost of the broad roster**, the user's call: about 17.6 MB of grammar code and parse tables in the executable (the stripped macOS binary 21.4 → 39.1 MB), +1.4 MB compressed; C# (5.1 MB), C++ (3.3) and Ruby (2.0) the heaviest. A grammar dropped is one pin, one roster entry and one fixture. Readings this item chose, each in the table and each a one-place change if vetoed: a source tree's label as its directory name; `build/` not on the excluded list (inside a repository git already leaves it out); a local's type resolving calls but not a `references` edge; and over HTTP, `"summaries": false` as a flag beside the existing `501` rather than the `501` reinterpreted.

### 2026-10-05 — `graph-navigation` (backlog item 27l): path, explain, neighbors and query over one traversal core, and the graph toolset

**The shape it inherited.** A built graph could be shown a node at a time (`graph show`) and expanded into a turn's transient prefix, but nobody -- person or model -- could *walk* it: no "how does A reach B?", no "everything around X and why it is there". 27k had just made code graphs model-free, with every edge's origin and every code node's `file:line` in the store. This item adds the traversal Graphify proved people use, in Apogee's idiom: one core, every surface, read-only, bounded, and with no model.

**What was built**

- [x] **The navigation reads** (`embedstore/graph_search.cpp`, declared in `store.h`): `has_graph`; `relation_counts` -- a node's edges per (relation, direction), counted in SQL so a hub never loads its whole edge list to show twelve; a filtered, capped `node_neighbors` (relations, direction, peer type) ordered **structure before unresolved `name` nodes**, then heaviest first, then by name -- the deterministic order a walk and a card both rely on; `search_node_names`, the entity index over **names alone** (an FTS5 column filter: a question's words never match a description); `code_nodes_ending` (a code node by the last parts of its qualified name at a `::`, `.` or `/`, by GLOB so case-sensitive as code identity is, its metacharacters bracketed); `code_files` and `code_spans_at` (the definitions and declarations holding a line, innermost first); `node_communities`.
- [x] **The one traversal core** (`graph/navigate.h/.cpp`), pure over an injected store, read-only and model-free -- what the CLI verbs, the toolset and the admin twins all call, each payload serialised by its one `to_json`:
  - *Addressing* (`resolve_node`): `path:line` (the innermost definition or declaration holding the line; the path as recorded, under its member's label, or a unique tail at a `/`), `kind:name` (a code kind, one of the extractor's eight types, or `decision`; any other prefix is part of a name), the exact name, then a code node's **unqualified name** when exactly one qualified name ends in it -- every resolution saying how it matched. A name several nodes answer to is **never picked**: the `NavigationError` lists each candidate by the `type:name` that names it alone (with its `file:line` for code), ten at most then a count; a name that matches nothing names its near matches from the entity index.
  - *`shortest_path`*: breadth first from one node, undirected by default with each hop's direction shown, `directed` following edges the way they point, optionally over a few relations only; the edges at each node read in the store's fixed order, so the path is always the same one. **An unresolved `name` node may end a path and never carries one** -- walked through, `.push_back` would connect every one of its callers. The hop cap is 8, at most 32; a missing connection is `found: false` with "no path within N hops". Each hop carries its relation, origin (`extracted`/`inferred`), weight, a parsed edge's first site (`file:line`) and an asserted one's description.
  - *`neighborhood` and `node_card`* (the explain payload): degree (total, out, in), neighbours grouped by (relation, direction), each group counted in full and listed to the cap (12, at most 100); provenance -- a code node's definitions, declarations or references at their lines, a prose node's chunks resolved through its member's store (a member gone, the chunk named missing) -- the first 12 with the count said; communities with their summaries; the decision records one edge away with their status; descriptions clipped at 400 codepoints. 27m's report and HTML cards render these.
  - *`query_graph`*: retrieval-time expansion seeded by the question alone -- its exact name, else its words against entity names, at most half the entity cap as seeds so the neighbourhood has room, never an unresolved name -- walked by `graph_expand` (hops 1..2 and the entity cap, the graph's own knobs by default, at most 50) and cut whole lines at the **1,500-codepoint section budget** a turn injects, a cut entity ending it before any relation; the cut applied in the core, so the JSON and the human view carry the same facts.
  - *Which graph* (`resolve_graph_target`, `OpenGraph`): `--graph` graphs-first exactly as every `graph` subcommand resolves its name; `--collection` through the retrieval precedence rule (`agentloop::named_graph_covering`: a built named graph listing it, else its own graph); neither, the one graph built, else a refusal listing them. A database is never created by a read; an empty one says how to build it.
- [x] **The verbs** (`cli/graph_navigate.h/.cpp`, bound under `graph`): `graph path FROM TO [--directed] [--relation R]... [--max-hops N]`, `graph explain NODE [--max-neighbors N]`, `graph neighbors NODE [--relation R] [--direction in|out|both]` and `graph query QUESTION [--hops N] [--max-entities N]`, each with `--graph`/`--collection` and `--output-format text|json` (27j's `ReadFormat` and `write_document`). Hops render as `a -[calls·extracted]-> b  at file:line` (backwards `a <-[calls·extracted]- b`); the query renders as the section a turn would inject. A node that resolves to nothing or to several, a cap out of range, or a selection that names nothing is a user error (exit 1) on stderr naming the candidates or the near matches, with nothing on stdout.
- [x] **The `graph` toolset** (`tools/graph_nav.h/.cpp`): `graph_query`, `graph_path`, `graph_explain`, `graph_neighbors` -- registered by `register_native_toolsets` as a sixth toolset (`graph` joins `tools.disabled`'s and a suite member's `toolset:` words, the template saying so), each returning **the CLI's `--output-format json` document byte for byte**, every failure an error result with the CLI's message. None `writes` or is `outbound`, so the gate never asks about one on any surface -- and `apogee __mcp-tools`, which serves exactly the tools that do not write, serves all four with no code of its own (asserted, not assumed: by unit test over `read_only_tools` and by an external MCP client on the real binary). Arguments are tolerant of a local template's habits -- `"True"`, `"8"`, `"['calls']"` read as what they mean, anything else refused by name. `GraphToolsOptions::scope` builds the set over one injected `GraphTarget` -- a store path, no `graph`/`collection` arguments -- the seam 27o hands a chat's attachment graph to. `tools/` now links `graph/` (`cmake/modules.cmake`).
- [x] **The read twins** (`httpserver/admin_graph_navigate.h/.cpp`): `GET /v1/admin/graph/{id}/path|explain|neighbors|query`, `{id}` graphs-first, each `200` body the CLI's JSON document byte for byte; a failure the CLI's message in the error envelope -- `404` for nothing by that name, a graph not built or a node matching nothing (its near matches as `error.candidates`), `400` for a cap, a missing or non-integer parameter, or a name several nodes answer to (`error.candidates`). Eighty admin rows; the parity table classes the four verbs as reads served. [http-api.md](../reference/http-api.md) and [machine-mode.md](../reference/machine-mode.md) document the shapes.
- [x] **39 new Catch2 cases** over **one committed fixture graph** (`tests/support/graph_fixture`: a code layer with a ten-hop call chain, fifteen callers past the cap, two `helper`s and an `add`/`Add` pair to be ambiguous, an island reachable only through an unresolved name; a prose layer with `Atlas` as two types, a shipped decision, a bridge into the code, a summarised community, a node concerned by thirteen records and one mentioned by fourteen chunks), and **`cli.graph_navigation_lifecycle`** on the real binary.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | **`graph/navigate`** (the core, the target resolution and every payload's `to_json`); seven reads in `embedstore/graph_search.cpp` rather than two or three; **`tools/graph_nav`**; the verbs in **`cli/graph_navigate`** beside `cli/graph.cpp`; **`httpserver/admin_graph_navigate`**; `tools` linking `graph` *(2026-10-05)* | One serialisation per payload is what makes "the same bytes" structural; a hub's card and a walk both needed counts and caps in SQL, and `path:line` and unqualified names needed their own lookups. `cli/graph.cpp` was already 1,600 lines. |
| A fourth verb | **`graph neighbors`** beside `path`, `explain`, `query` *(2026-10-05)* | The spec names four tools and requires an MCP client to get "the same payloads the CLI prints as JSON"; `graph_neighbors` had no CLI twin to print one. |
| The selection | `--graph` **graphs-first** (a named graph, else a collection's own -- as every `graph` subcommand's NAME); `--collection` through **`named_graph_covering`**, else the collection's own graph **whether or not `graph.enabled`**; neither, **the one graph built**, else refused listing them *(2026-10-05)* | The spec (and 27m's) presume a `--graph`/`--collection` convention the CLI did not have; `enabled` gates retrieval-time expansion, not reading a built graph. |
| `query`'s match | **Lexical on every install** -- exact, then FTS over **names only** (a column filter), never descriptions; no entity-vector match even with an embedder *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed model-free path, and nothing in the store searches entity vectors yet; one deterministic match keeps the CLI, the tools and the twins trivially identical. A vector match is an additive upgrade behind the same function. |
| `query`'s budget | **At most half the entity cap as seeds**; the 1,500-codepoint section budget **applied in the core**, a cut entity ending the section *(2026-10-05)* | Expansion's own seeding would fill every slot with name hits; the budget in the core keeps JSON and text the same facts. |
| Addressing beyond the three forms | **A code node's unqualified name**, only when exactly one qualified name ends in it, said as `matched: unqualified` *(2026-10-05)* | People and models say `build_source`, not `apogee::graph::build_source`; ambiguity still lists, so nothing is silently picked. |
| `path:line` | **The innermost definition or declaration holding the line**; the path as recorded, member-prefixed, or a unique `/` tail; a tail never inside a file's name *(2026-10-05)* | "The function I am looking at", whichever line of it is named. |
| Unresolved names on a path | **An endpoint, never a hop** *(2026-10-05)* | 27k's "a name is not structure", carried into traversal. |
| A relation filter on `path` | **`--relation` (repeatable), the tools' `relations`** *(2026-10-05)* | Undirected over every relation (the confirmed default) finds shared files and imports; "how does X reach Y" as a call chain is `--directed --relation calls`, which the tool's description says. |
| Neighbour order | **Structure before unresolved names**, then heaviest, then by name *(2026-10-05)* | A capped `calls ->` group showed nine `.push_back`-like names before the first parsed callee. |
| The ceilings | path 8 / **32**; neighbours 12 / **100** per relation; query hops 1..2, entities the graph's / **50**; provenance and decisions **12**; descriptions **400**, summaries **300**, relation descriptions **200** codepoints; candidates **10**, near matches **5** *(2026-10-05)* | "Flag-overridable, never unbounded" needs a number past the flag. |
| No path, and a failure | **No path is an answer** (exit 0, "No path within N hops", `found: false`); a resolution failure is a user error on stderr with **nothing on stdout** in JSON mode, the same message the tool returns and the twin serves *(2026-10-05)* | 27j's read convention: one document on stdout or none, diagnostics on stderr. |
| The toolset's presence | **Always registered** (like `rag`), switched off with `tools.disabled: [graph]`; with no graph built a call says how to build one *(2026-10-05)* | The `rag` precedent; registration happens at startup, before a graph built later in the session could be known; 26g keeps the four off the menu for questions they do not fit. |
| Tolerant tool arguments | Booleans and numbers as text, an array written as text *(2026-10-05)* | Found on real weights: Llama 3.1 8B's template sent `"directed": "True"` and `"relations": "['calls']"` -- refused, it retried the same call three times. |
| The twins' selection | **`{id}` only, graphs-first** -- no `?collection=` *(2026-10-05)* | The existing graph routes' pattern, which the spec asked the twins to follow. |
| Read-only, made checkable | Navigation adds no write; **a read never creates a database**; the e2e holds a digest of the graph's rows unchanged *(2026-10-05)* | The store's own open-time schema bookkeeping is every reader's, `graph show`'s included; "never writes" is about what navigation does. |
| The fixture | **Built in code** (`tests/support/graph_fixture`), the same graph every time, for every layer's tests *(2026-10-05)* | "A committed fixture graph" as committed source, deterministic and readable, rather than a binary database. |

**The acceptance run over this repository.** In a sandboxed `APOGEE_HOME` with no backend, `graph build --source lib/src/cli --graph apogee-code` (10,060 nodes, 65,471 edges, every one extracted), then: `graph path run_graph_build build_source --directed --relation calls` -- `run_graph_build -[calls·extracted]-> build_named -[calls·extracted]-> build_code -[calls·extracted]-> build_graph_sources -[calls·extracted]-> build_source`, each hop at its call site, both endpoints matched by their unqualified names -- in 0.02 s; undirected, the same two in 3 hops through `graph.cpp`'s include of `code_build.h`; a walk with no path at the 32-hop ceiling, the whole graph searched, 0.31 s; `graph explain build_source` (its declaration and definition, 32 callees with the parsed ones first, 4 callers) in 0.01 s and 6.5 KB of JSON; `graph explain parse` refused, naming its 8 candidates; `graph explain code_build.cpp:210` resolving to `build_source` by the line.

**Verified on the real binary.** `cli.graph_navigation_lifecycle`, with zero backends, no key and the network at a closed port: a code graph built from the Python fixture with no model; `graph path` with each hop's relation, origin and site, and "No path within 8 hops" where there is none; `explain`, `neighbors`, `query` and a refusal naming the node; an external MCP client (`tests/scripts/py/mcp_graph_client.py`, raw JSON-RPC over `apogee __mcp-tools`'s stdio) listing the four graph tools marked `readOnlyHint: true`, no writer among them, and getting back for each **exactly the document the CLI printed** with `--output-format json`; a `complete --tools` turn on a pipe -- where nobody can answer the gate, so a gated tool is denied -- calling `graph_path` from a scripted mock and relaying the route; and a digest of the graph's rows unchanged by all of it. In-process, `cli/graph_navigate_test` holds the one core for eight questions: the CLI's JSON, the tool's result and the served twin's body the same bytes. The full suite through `make test` (llama.cpp on): 100% passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before; `make format-check` clean; `clang-tidy` over every new translation unit reports no error (the ownership gate) -- the warnings left are kinds the tree already carries, all in the tests (designated-initializer suggestions, stream const-correctness, and the cognitive complexity of a table-driven case).

**Guardrails, each mutation-tested.** 46 mutants against the final code, each applied in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared checkout), rebuilt, and run against the navigation, toolset and twin suites -- **45 caught outright, 1 after its test was strengthened**: a query that skipped past an entity the budget cut, rather than ending the section, survived a fixture whose cut fell at the last entity -- a store whose second neighbour alone overruns the budget, with a third that would fit, now holds the rule. Three bounds were given fixture data before the run, since nothing in the first fixture exceeded them: fourteen chunks mentioning one node, fourteen references to one name, thirteen records concerning one node. The mutations: each ceiling dropped (hops, neighbours, query hops, query entities); a group, a card's code or chunk provenance, or its decisions uncapped; the clip never clipping; the budget ignored, or a cut entity skipped past; seeds taking the whole cap; a name carrying a path; `directed` or the relation filter ignored; the hop cap off by one; ambiguity picking the first; any prefix a kind; the kind filter ignored; `path:line` not innermost; a path tail inside a file's name; no unqualified lookup; a collection ignoring its covering graph; a graph and a collection both taken; several built graphs, the first taken; an empty store opened; an unresolved name seeding a query, by its exact name or by its words; a missing chunk dropped; the no-path note dropped; degree directions swapped; a hop's direction inverted; a node's file dropped from its JSON; decisions not filtered by type; counts merging directions; structure not first; the names index reading descriptions; unresolved names always included; GLOB metacharacters live; a tail without its separator; communities not by node; a served ambiguity a `404`; served candidates dropped; `--output-format json` ignored; a backward hop drawn forward; a graph tool that writes.

**Real weights** (a sandboxed chat over the `apogee-code` graph built with `graph build --source`, zero model calls to build; `chat --tools --no-recall` driven in machine mode, one family at a time, each model loaded once; two questions in one chat: "In this codebase, how does run_graph_build reach build_source?" then "How does run_graph_update reach sync_code_graph?" -- the tools offered and selection left to the model and 26g, never forced):
- **Meta** `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M`: called `graph_path` unprompted on the first question, ungated. Its template sent every argument as text (`"directed": "True"`, `"relations": "['calls']"`), which the first cut refused -- the tolerant parsing above came from this run. Re-run: it passed `graph: "default"`, read the refusal listing the built graphs, retried with `apogee-code` and got the 4-hop call chain -- then its final answer did not match its template's format and was kept as text ("The function call that best answers the prompt is"). On the second question it reached for `run_command` (grep), which the gate stopped on the pipe.
- **Qwen** `Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M`: called `graph_path` unprompted on **both** questions, ungated, and answered each from the path it returned, every node with its `file:line` (the undirected default: through `graph.cpp`'s include of `code_build.h`, and through `build_code`'s reference to `Store`).
- **Google** `gemma-4-12B-it-Q4_K_M`: called `graph_path` on the first question with `directed: true, relations: ["calls"]` -- as the tool's description suggests -- and answered with the exact 4-hop call chain, each function at its line. On the second it reached for `search_files` and then `run_command`, which the gate stopped.
- **OpenAI** `gpt-oss-20b-F16` (no Q4_K_M exists): explored with `list_directory` and then asked for `run_command`, which the gate stopped; it did not call a graph tool.
Three of four families called `graph_path` unprompted, none was asked about it by the gate, and two answered "how does X reach Y" from the path itself.

**Not verified.** Windows and Linux at run time (the e2e is POSIX). A served twin over a live `serve` (the handlers are held in-process and their routes, gated, by the parity table). Navigation of a **prose** graph on real weights (the fixture's prose layer is held by every suite; the real-weights run used a code graph). Entity-vector matching for `query` (not built; see the decisions).

**Left for the owner.** Readings this item chose, each in the table and each a one-place change if vetoed: a code node addressable by its unqualified name; `--relation` on `path`; structure before unresolved names in a capped list; a collection's own graph read whether or not `graph.enabled`; the `graph` toolset registered on every tool-using surface whether or not a graph is built; and the tools' tolerance of stringly-typed arguments.

### 2026-10-05 — `graph-artifacts` (backlog item 27m): the report, the page, the exports -- each a file, none a model call

**The shape it inherited.** After 27k and 27l a graph could be built with no model and walked from every surface, but everything it knew came out one question at a time. A graph's highest-leverage output is often an *artifact* instead: the one-page architecture read a newcomer starts from, the picture a team argues over, the file another tool imports. Graphify ships three and people use all of them; this item is their Apogee equivalents over the existing store -- each assembled from what is already there, and each a file, never a port.

**What was built**

- [x] **The one ranking** (`graph/navigate`): `node_degree`, the summation a card's `Degree` already was (`relation_counts` added up, one `degree_of` the card and the ranking share), and `rank_by_degree` -- every node but the unresolved `name` nodes, by degree, then mentions, then name and type, so the order is the store's to decide. It is **what a hub means everywhere**: the report's hubs and orphans, the HTML's cap and the Mermaid selection all read it, and no artifact computes "hub" a second way. Beside it `to_json` for a `Degree` and a `NeighborGroup` (the serialisations 27l's payloads already used, made public) and `clip_text`.
- [x] **The report model** (`graph/report.h/.cpp`): `build_report`, pure over a store and read-only -- the overview and the extracted/inferred mix from `graph_stats`; the **hubs**, the ranking's top ten, each with 27l's `neighborhood` groups (every relation counted, three neighbours named); the **communities** as `graph communities` stored them, the ten largest with five most-mentioned members each and the summary exactly as written -- **one clustered with no model has none and says so, one by one; nothing is generated**; for a named graph of two or more members the **cross-collection links** (relations whose endpoints share no member, the member pairs they join, entities stated in several -- members being collections and source trees alike, read from both mention tables by the new `node_members`); the **decisions**, most connected first, each with what it concerns (its outgoing relations); the **orphans**, degree zero, the ten most mentioned; every list capped and counted; and a `human_summary` paragraph of the same facts. `to_json` is the one document, `{"object":"graph.report",…}`.
- [x] **The renderer** (`render/graph_report.h/.cpp`): `render_graph_report`, the document as Markdown in reading order -- overview, origin (in `graph stats`' own words: `N extracted (parsed from source), M inferred (asserted by a model)`), hubs (`calls <- 17: a, b, c, and 14 more`), communities (`_No summary -- clustered with no model._` per community, the command that writes them named), cross-collection links (a table and the relations across; a named graph of one member says it has nothing to link; a collection's own graph has no section), decisions, orphans -- and `human_summary` **last**. Every name a code span whatever backticks it holds (`code_span`), every prose field one line, a table cell's pipes escaped.
- [x] **The HTML page** (`graph/export_html.h/.cpp`, `graph/html_template.h/.cpp`, `assets/graph/graph.html`): `export_html` takes the ranking's top 2,000 (the recorded cap; `--max-nodes` lowers it), gives each entity **27l's `node_card`**, serialised by its own `to_json` -- byte for byte `graph explain <it> --output-format json --max-neighbors 6`, less the `matched` word a typed address adds -- plus the edges among them by index (a model's flagged), the communities for the legend and the cap sentence, as **one JSON block** written by `embeddable_json` (`<`, `>`, `&` as `\u` escapes and `/` as `\/`, so it can neither close its element nor open a comment nor hold a `//`), filled into the compiled-in page by `fill_template` in one pass. The page is hand-written: a Barnes-Hut force simulation on a canvas, seeded by community; community colours with a legend that focuses one; full-text search over names, files, kinds and descriptions (`/` to focus, arrows and Enter); a click on an entity -- or a neighbour in a card -- opening its card (relations with "and N more", where it is stated, its community and summary, its decisions); pan, zoom, drag, fit; the busiest dozen always labelled. 33 KB of inline CSS and script, no library, a `Content-Security-Policy` of `default-src 'none'` so the browser itself refuses any fetch, and the cap printed in the page: `Showing the 2000 highest-degree of 8374 entities -- capped at 2000 by degree rank; the 1928 unresolved names are left out. apogee graph export graphml carries every one.` The page is an asset compiled in like the clerks' prompts, emitted by `scripts/generate_graph_assets.py` as raw-string chunks under MSVC's literal limit and held byte-equal to the file by a test.
- [x] **GraphML** (`graph/export_graphml.h/.cpp`): every node and edge, **uncapped** -- the unresolved names marked `unresolved` -- each node with its name, kind, description, mentions, degree, largest community, members and, for code, the `file:line` of its definition; each edge its relation, origin, weight, confidence when recorded and description; ids the store's, so two exports of one graph are the same bytes. `xml_escape` writes what XML 1.0 cannot carry, and any invalid UTF-8, as U+FFFD. The GraphML namespace is declared (readers need it; it is a name, not a fetch) and no `schemaLocation` is.
- [x] **Mermaid** (`graph/export_mermaid.h/.cpp`): a code graph's **call flow** -- functions calling functions, the ranking's top 40 by default (150 at most), grouped in a subgraph per defining file, short names unless two in a file share one -- or, with no parsed calls, the busiest entities and their labelled relations, a model's dotted; at most 500 edges (Mermaid's own `maxEdges`, past which a diagram does not draw), what was drawn of what said in its opening `%%` comment, every label in Mermaid's numeric entity codes.
- [x] **The artifact reads** (`embedstore/graph_search.cpp`): `graph_nodes` and `graph_edges` (every row, the names' included) and `node_members`; `GraphEdge` gains `origin` and `confidence`, which `all_edges` now fills too.
- [x] **The verbs** (`cli/graph_artifacts.h/.cpp`, bound under `graph`): `graph report [--out FILE] [--output-format text|json]` prints the Markdown (or the one document) and `--out` writes **the same bytes** to a file; `graph export html|graphml|mermaid [--out FILE|-]` (and `--max-nodes` for html and mermaid) lands in the **working directory** as `<graph>.html`, `<graph>.graphml` or `<graph>.mmd`, at `--out`, or on stdout for `-`, written atomically -- never into the data directory. Each takes `--graph`/`--collection` exactly as 27l's verbs do and needs no backend; a graph that is not built, a cap past its ceiling or an unknown name is a user error on stderr. The parity table classes the four as read-only (the `knowledge export` precedent).
- [x] **31 new Catch2 cases** -- `graph/report_test` (the facts), `graph/export_test` (the page, GraphML through **an XML reader written in the test**, Mermaid through **a grammar check of its own**, the privacy of chunk text), `render/graph_report_test` (**two golden pages**, `tests/fixtures/graph_report/work.md` and `work_no_summaries.md`), `cli/graph_artifacts_test` (the verbs and **the privacy sweep**) -- over 27l's fixture graph with twelve orphans added (`add_report_orphans`), and **`cli.graph_artifacts_lifecycle`** on the real binary, which drives the page's own script under node (`tests/scripts/js/graph_html_check.js`) and reads the GraphML back with Python's `xml.etree` and networkx.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | The report **model** in `graph/report`, its **renderer** in `render/graph_report`; the verbs in **`cli/graph_artifacts`** beside `cli/graph_navigate`; the page generated into `graph/html_template` by `scripts/generate_graph_assets.py`; the tests split by layer (`business/graph/{report,export}_test`, `presentation/render/graph_report_test`, `presentation/cli/graph_artifacts_test`) *(2026-10-05)* | The spec predates the four layers: `render/` is Presentation and `graph/` Business, so the model cannot include the renderer -- it hands it a document. `cli/graph.cpp` is past 1,600 lines. A 33 KB page would be hand-chunked error-prone, so it has a generator like the training assets'. |
| The report's Markdown | **A renderer of its own**, sections in reading order, `human_summary` last -- not `render_markdown` *(2026-10-05)* | The generic renderer alphabetises sections and titles each list item by its longest string: right for a model's free-form report, wrong for an architecture page whose order is the point. The `human_summary`-last discipline is kept. |
| What a hub is | **`rank_by_degree`**: 27l's `Degree` (every relation either way, the card's own summation) over **every node but the unresolved names**, ties by mentions, name, type; the one ranking the report, the HTML cap and Mermaid all read *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed plain-degree first cut, labelled. A name is not structure (27k: "never ranked"); ranked, `.push_back` would top any C++ tree. |
| Files and classes as hubs | **Ranked like any entity** -- a header's `defined_in`/`imports` fan-in puts it first in a C++ tree (this repository's top hub is `config.h`) *(2026-10-05)* | Plain degree, as confirmed; the report says what the metric counts, so the reader can discount it. A per-kind ranking is a later refinement, not a second definition. |
| Orphans | **Degree zero, the ten most mentioned**, with the count *(2026-10-05)* | "Sampled top-10" made deterministic: the entities the sources talk about most and the graph connects to nothing are the ones worth asking about. |
| Cross-collection links | Relations whose endpoints are **stated in no common member**, the member pairs they join, and entities stated in several; members are collections and source trees alike; none for a collection's own graph, "one member" said for a named graph of one *(2026-10-05)* | An entity in two members is one node (Milestone Y), so a "link" is either a relation across or a shared entity; both are counted, the top ten of each listed. |
| Decisions | **Most connected first**, each with its outgoing relations (`concerns`, `supersedes`), three named per relation, ten listed with the count *(2026-10-05)* | "The decision nodes with what they concern"; top-N with counts, never the whole enumeration. |
| Community summaries in the report | **Whole**, as `graph communities` wrote them; the page's legend and cards carry 27l's 300-codepoint `CommunityRef` *(2026-10-05)* | The report is where the paid-for prose is read; a clipped summary would be a worse report of the same facts. |
| The page's layout | **Hand-rolled** -- a Barnes-Hut force simulation on a canvas, 33 KB of inline CSS and script, no library *(2026-10-05)* | The recorded default (hand-rolled or a pinned MIT library under ~200 KB): hand-rolled is smaller, needs no pin, licence or `third_party/` entry, and nothing in it can reach a network. |
| Neighbours per card in the page | **6** per relation (27l's default is 12), the card saying so and that `graph explain` lists up to 100 *(2026-10-05)* | Over this repository the cards are nine tenths of the page: 8.8 MB at 8 per relation, 7.9 MB at 6 (0.7 MB gzipped). Still 27l's payload, at a cap 27l's own argument takes. |
| The data block's escaping | `<`, `>`, `&` as `<`/`>`/`&` **and `/` as `\/`** *(2026-10-05)* | Valid JSON that parses to the same value; the block can never end its element or open a comment, and the file can never hold `//` -- so the mechanical "no `http:`, no `//`, no `src=`" grep holds even over a graph whose names are URLs. |
| A Content-Security-Policy | **`default-src 'none'`**, inline script and style allowed *(2026-10-05)* | Beyond the spec: the browser itself refuses any fetch, so "zero fetches" is enforced at run time as well as grepped at build time. |
| What the page leaves out | **The unresolved names**, counted in the cap note *(2026-10-05)* | Not structure, never ranked; GraphML carries them. |
| `graph report --output-format json` | **Added**, 27j's one-document read; invalid UTF-8 in a stored description replaced, never thrown on *(2026-10-05)* | The renderer's input is a document anyway, and a GUI renders reads from documents (machine-mode.md). |
| Where an artifact lands | `report` **prints** (the acceptance) and writes only with `--out`; an export lands **in the working directory** as `<graph>.html`/`.graphml`/`.mmd` or at `--out`, `-` for stdout; an existing file is **overwritten**, atomically *(2026-10-05)* | The confirmed default names in the working directory; overwriting is `knowledge export -o`'s precedent and what re-exporting needs. |
| Mermaid's selection | **Functions calling functions**, the ranking's top 40 (150 at most), grouped by file, at most 500 edges; with no parsed calls, the top entities and their labelled relations *(2026-10-05)* | "A call-flow diagram for a code graph's docs-friendly view" that Mermaid will actually draw: its default `maxEdges` is 500, and a diagram past a few dozen boxes is not read. |
| GraphML's form | The GraphML namespace declared, **no `schemaLocation`**; typed keys; ids the store's *(2026-10-05)* | Readers need the namespace (networkx matches on it); a schema location is a URL some validators fetch. Stable ids make two exports diffable. |
| The parity table | The four verbs **read-only**, no admin route *(2026-10-05)* | Serving the visualization is out of scope (the never-listens invariant); files a CLI writes are `knowledge export`'s class. Machine mode reaches the report through `--output-format json`; HTTP is the skipped mode, named here (ADR 0002). |
| Testing the page's script | Under **node, optional** in the e2e (said when skipped): the page's own script against a stand-in DOM and a recording canvas *(2026-10-05)* | No browser runs in the suite; this is the only check that the script works at all -- two of the mutants (search, click-to-explain) are caught by it alone. |

**The sanity run over this repository.** In a sandboxed `APOGEE_HOME` with **no backend**, from the repository root: `graph build --source lib/src/cli --graph apogee-code` (909 files, **10,302 nodes and 67,022 edges, every one extracted**, 3.1 s) and `graph communities --no-summaries` (477 clusters, 0.13 s). Then: `graph report` in **0.11 s** -- 11.6 KB of Markdown (34 KB as JSON); the hubs `source/data/contracts/config.h` (257 relations: 174 files include it, 69 entities defined in it), `apogee::harness::Config` (238), `apogee::httpserver::HttpResponse` (228), `apogee::testing::TempDir::path` (216 callers); every community "no summary -- clustered with no model". `graph export html` in **1.5 s**: **2,000 of 8,374 entities and the 10,566 relations among them**, the cap printed, **7.9 MB** (0.7 MB gzipped; the cards 95% of it); its script under node settled the layout in 162 frames and opened cards by click, by neighbour and by search. `graph export graphml` in **1.6 s**: every node and edge, 19.6 MB (0.79 MB gzipped), read back whole by networkx (10,302 nodes, 67,022 edges) in 1.6 s. `graph export mermaid` in **0.1 s**: the call flow of the 40 highest-degree of 4,835 calling functions, 39 calls among them, every line one the grammar reads. Nothing under the sandbox's data directory changed.

### 2026-10-06 — `attachment-code-graph` (backlog item 27n): a folder of code, graphed in the chat's own index

**The shape it inherited.** 27k left a build entry over an injected file list (`graph::build_source`) precisely so an attachment could hand it the files its attach had already found. A chat's attachment index (`attachments/<chat id>.db`, 26d) is an ordinary embedstore database, so the code layer's tables were already in it; what was missing was the wiring -- the worker running the build, the store holding one graph per chat, and a word to the user. The attachment-representation spike (2026-10-03) had measured it interactive: a 429-file C++ tree chunk-indexed inside a 1.7 s run, a tree-sitter pass the same order of work.

**What was built**

- [x] **The pass** (`cli/attachment_graph.h/.cpp`): `build_attachment_graph` builds one attached folder (`AttachmentGraphJob` -- its label, its folder, the files its attach found, the other attached folders' members) into the chat's index with 27k's `build_source` over the injected files and `operations/graph_sources`' one disk reader. The chat's graph is one graph: each graphed folder a source member, linked to the others (a call in one folder resolving into another is structure), the others linked from their cache and never re-read (`prune_other_members` off), and any member no attachment owns -- a folder detached, a build a crash cut short -- forgotten before the build so nothing outlives its attachment. Cancelled between files it syncs nothing, the parsed files cached; a storage error is `Failed`, said, never a throw. `forget_attachment_graph` drops a folder's member and re-links the rest from their cache -- parsing nothing -- so the graph holds exactly the kept attachments' code. **Zero model calls**: nothing in it takes a closure, and 27k's include rule already keeps every model out of the build.
- [x] **The one line** (`attachment_graph_line`, `skipped_kinds`): `graph: 7160 nodes, 45054 edges (supported: cpp 545; skipped: .txt 5, .md 4)` -- the folder's own part of the graph (the code nodes it mentions, the edges it states: `embedstore`'s new `code_member_counts`, which with one folder are the graph's totals), the files used by language, and what was left out by extension, by why (`binary`, `too large`, `unreadable`, `unparseable`) or by vendored directory, largest first, eight named and the rest counted. Absent, it says so: `graph: not built -- cancelled; attach it again to build it`.
- [x] **On the worker** (`cli/chat_attachments`): `attach` gives a folder -- never one file, never a glob -- whose files include a language a vendored grammar parses (`offers_code`) a graph job over the very list its walk produced (before media nothing reads is left out, so the build counts what a direct build would), labelled by the folder's name as `graph build --source` labels the same tree, `-2`, `-3` for a second folder of one name; the worker runs it after the folder's chunks, saying how far it has got on the status line, and `settle` waits for it as for the chunks. `record` says the line after the attach line -- a warning when absent -- and keeps the folder's part on the session; `/attachments` (`describe`) ends that folder's line with it, counted from the index as it stands. **Re-attached**, the same member is updated by content hash, only changed files parsed; a re-attach that indexes nothing leaves the folder and its graph standing (26d's "nothing attached" keeps the old record). **One forgetting path, `reconcile_graph`**: after every settle's records and every detach, any member of the index's code graph that no recorded attachment owns is forgotten and the rest re-linked from their cache -- so a folder **detached**, one **re-attached with the graph off or no code left**, one whose build **failed**, and one **interrupted by Ctrl-C** at the turn that waits (its ready chunks kept, its graph recorded absent and said, so `/attachments` says it too) all leave no graph behind, and the index's graph is, after every settle, exactly the session's graphed folders'. **A quit mid-attach** reaches no settle, so the graph stays as the saved session knows it, the files parsed so far cached for the next attach. **Deleting the chat** takes the graph with the index file (`remove_index`, unchanged). `Hooks::code_graph` is off in both of `complete`'s one-shot hooks (at a terminal and in machine mode), which 27p's flag will override.
- [x] **The bridge, shared** (`operations/graph_sources`): `source_files_under` (a walk's files relative to their folder), `source_member` (the one reader every source build is handed -- `graph build --source`, the admin build, an attached folder) and `offers_code` (the supported-language test: by extension against 27k's roster, outside a vendored directory, the build's own selection), with `open_graph_sources` rebuilt on the first two, so "shared verbatim with `graph build --source`" is one function, not a copy.
- [x] **Kept with the session** (`logger/session`): `Attachment::graph` (`AttachmentGraph`) -- the folder's member label and its notice's supported and skipped counts, or why it is absent -- written as `graph` only when set, additive to schema 2 (26q's `map_at` precedent); one that cannot be read costs the graph's line, never the attachment.
- [x] **23 new Catch2 cases** over the mini-repos 27k commits (six in `cli/attachment_graph_test`, thirteen in `cli/chat_attachments_test`, three in `operations/graph_sources_test`, one in `logger/session_test`), the 26q map test and `chat_test`'s map case updated for a folder of code now graphed (and `complete`, at a terminal and in machine mode, held to building none), and **`cli.code_graph_lifecycle` grown a section on the real binary**.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | The supported-language test and the walk-to-member bridge in **`operations/graph_sources`**, not `agentloop/attachments`; the pass and its line in a new **`cli/attachment_graph`** beside `cli/chat_attachments`; tests in `tests/presentation/{cli,operations}/` and `tests/data/logger/` *(2026-10-06)* | The spec predates the four layers: `graph` links `agentloop`, so `agentloop` including `graph/code_languages.h` would close a module cycle the build refuses. `operations/graph_sources` already turned a walk into a source member for both surfaces; extending it is what makes the attach's build and `graph build --source` one path. |
| What gets a graph | **A folder** -- never one file, never a glob -- whose files include a supported language outside a vendored directory *(2026-10-06)* | The spec's "folder attach". A glob has no folder to qualify names from (Python's module path, Go's package directory are paths under the root); one file is barely a graph. 27p's flag is where widening would go. |
| A folder's label | **Its directory name**, as `graph build --source` labels the tree; a second folder of one name `-2`, `-3`; a re-attach keeps its label, even after the name it collided with is gone *(2026-10-06)* | Byte-equivalence covers every mention's member label; `build_source` refuses two members of one label; a stable label keeps the incremental update incremental. |
| The file list | **Everything the attach's walk found**, relative to the folder, before media nothing reads is left out; the build skips and counts the rest *(2026-10-06)* | "One extractor, one file list": the same list a direct build walks, so the skipped counts match too; what is supported is 27k's rule, never a second filter. |
| Several folders | **One graph per chat, a member per folder**, linked to each other; a member no attachment owns forgotten before a build *(2026-10-06)* | "The store stays the chat's": the graph is exactly its attachments', and code spread over two folders resolves across them. |
| The line's numbers | **The folder's own part** (nodes it mentions, edges it states), counted from the index when said and when listed *(2026-10-06)* | A line per attachment; with one folder these are the graph's totals, which is what the acceptance compares with a direct build. |
| Forgetting | **One path, after the records: `reconcile_graph`** -- any member no recorded attachment owns forgotten, the rest re-linked -- run after every settle and every detach *(2026-10-06)* | The first cut forgot in the worker, case by case, and mutation testing found the settle-time check made those redundant; one rule ("the graph is exactly the recorded folders'") covers detach, Ctrl-C, failure, the graph turned off and a crash's leftover alike, and costs one `code_members` read when there is nothing to do. |
| Ctrl-C | **The folder's graph recorded absent, said as a warning, its member forgotten** with its parse cache *(2026-10-06)* | "Absent, never half-trusted": a build cancelled before its sync leaves the previous graph -- stale for a re-attach -- and 27k's cache cannot be kept without its half being linked by the next build. The cost is one full parse on the next attach: seconds. |
| A quit mid-attach | **Nothing forgotten**: the destructor's cancel reaches no settle, so the graph stays as the saved session knows it, the parsed files cached *(2026-10-06)* | Nothing is recorded after it, so forgetting would leave a resumed chat claiming a graph its index had lost; the next build reuses the cache, or the next settle prunes it as unowned. |
| Detach | **Its part forgotten, the rest re-linked** *(2026-10-06)* | The spec is silent; 27o's "absent after detach" and "the store stays the chat's" both need it. |
| A re-attach with the graph off, or no code left | **The earlier graph forgotten**, nothing said *(2026-10-06)* | The attach replaces the attachment, and its old graph would be stale; 27p's `--graph=off` is honest by construction. |
| `complete` | **No graph** -- `Hooks::code_graph` false in both of its hooks, at a terminal and in machine mode *(2026-10-06)* | The spec's default: a one-shot has no follow-up to walk a graph in; 27p's flag overrides it. |
| The session record | **`Attachment::graph`, additive**, no schema bump; a malformed one dropped with the attachment kept *(2026-10-06)* | 26q's `map_at` precedent; the label is what a resumed chat needs to update, detach and count its folder's part. |
| The e2e | **`cli.code_graph_lifecycle` grown**, not a new case: a machine-mode chat over the same tree, compared row for row with Python's `sqlite3` *(2026-10-06)* | The same sandbox and tree the 27k e2e already builds; the comparison is of content, not counts. |

**The acceptance run over this repository.** In sandboxed `APOGEE_HOME`s (and `HOME`) with a mock chat backend, no key and every proxy at a closed port, `apogee chat` under a pseudo-terminal in the repository root, `/attach lib/src/cli/source` -- 554 files, so the size guard asks, answered yes (on a pipe a folder over 500 files is refused, as 26d decided). **With no embedding model** the attach line said `searched by its words`, and the one notice followed: `graph: 7160 nodes, 45054 edges (supported: cpp 545; skipped: .txt 5, .md 4)` -- the walk through `git ls-files`, the five `CMakeLists.txt` and four layer `CLAUDE.md` cards counted out. The chunks (16,765) and the graph together settled within 3.5 s of the attach being confirmed. A direct `graph build --source lib/src/cli/source --graph direct` in the same sandbox took 1.7 s and reported the same 545 files, 7,160 nodes and 45,054 edges; read back row for row, the chat's index and the named graph hold **identical** nodes (7,160, descriptions and metadata included), edges (45,054, with weights and origins), mentions (45,185), edge sites (67,200) and file states (545). `/attachments` in the resumed chat repeated the line. **With a mock embedding model** the attach vectorised its chunks and the graph was the same, row for row. **Touched and re-attached** -- on a copy of the tree (543 files: the copy outside any repository), one function appended to `business/graph/code_build.cpp`, the chat resumed and the folder attached again: of 543 file states only that file's was rewritten (the rest kept their parse times), the line said `graph: 7154 nodes, 44961 edges` (from 7,153 and 44,958), the attach settled within 1.7 s, and the index matched a fresh `graph build --source` of the edited copy row for row. **`chats delete`** left the attachments folder empty.

**Verified on the real binary.** `cli.code_graph_lifecycle`, its new last section: in the 27k sandbox (zero backends until then, a plain mock added to answer, no embedder, no key, the network at a closed port), a machine-mode chat attaching the Python fixture copy gets the attach line and `graph: … (supported: python 4; skipped: .lua 1, third_party/ 1)`; Python's `sqlite3` finds the chat's index holding exactly the nodes, edges, mentions and sites a direct `graph build --source` of the tree holds; `chats delete` leaves nothing of it. In-process, every grammar's mini-repo attached as one folder holds byte for byte (`graph_dump`) what `build_graph_sources` builds; Ctrl-C, raised as `SIGINT` while the turn waits on an embedding held for it, keeps the ready chunk, says the absence and leaves no graph row, and the next attach completes it. The full suite through `make test` (llama.cpp on): 100% of 2,710 passed, the pdftotext case skipped as before; `make format-check` clean; `clang-tidy` over every file this item touched reports no error (the ownership gate) -- the warnings left are kinds the tree already carries (the cognitive complexity of `record`, the worker and Catch2's test bodies, unchecked-optional notes after a `REQUIRE`); `gcc-check.py` compiles all 512 first-party files with MinGW-w64 GCC's library.

**Guardrails, each mutation-tested.** 54 mutants against the final code, each applied in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared checkout) built with llama.cpp off, rebuilt and run against the attachment, session, graph and operations suites -- **53 caught outright, 1 equivalent and removed as dead code**: the worker's own check for a cancel before the graph pass, which the build makes itself before its first file. The rounds before it reshaped the code: a Ctrl-C test on a first attach could not tell whether a cancelled *re-attach* forgot its stale graph (a re-attach case was added); `complete`'s "no graph" was stated in three places, any one of which could go (it is stated where the hooks are built, both of them tested, machine mode added); a trailing-separator guard in `source_files_under` was equivalent -- `lexically_relative` ignores the empty element in both standard libraries (LWG 3070) -- and went, the no-backend case now attaching `app/`; five mutants of a name-to-label map's per-outcome bookkeeping survived, redundant or unreachable, and the session became the one record of a folder's label, in-flight labels kept only until the settle; and the worker's case-by-case forgetting turned out redundant once a settle-time reconcile existed, which became the one forgetting path. The mutations: leftover members kept, or no relink after a forget; other folders pruned by a build, the folder's own member forgotten before it, no forget of the unowned first; a cancel unsaid, or taken as built; the supported languages, the label or the vendored directories left out of the record; the kinds unparsed, `unparseable` dropped, sorted ascending, folded one late, `none` empty, a plural inverted, the absence ignored, nodes and edges swapped; a storage error thrown; `code_member_counts` counting mentions, other members' edges, or other members' files; a folder offering no code built, the graph off ignored, a re-attach's label recomputed, no numbering on a collision, an in-flight label unrecorded or never cleared, a pass run when nothing was indexed, a forget job building, the reconcile dropped after a settle or a detach, or keeping nothing, a recorded label ignored, the session's or the in-flight labels left out of what is kept; the line unsaid, not a warning, unrecorded, missing from `/attachments`, or uncounted there; the graph handed no files; `complete` building a graph at a terminal or in machine mode; vendored directories offering code; a file outside the folder kept; the reader's error unsaid; the session's graph unwritten, its absence unwritten, an empty one kept, a malformed one dropping the attachment, its skipped counts unread.

**Real weights.** None applies, and none was run: the attachment graph makes no model call -- built, updated and forgotten with zero backends, as the in-process suite and the e2e hold.

**Not verified.** Windows and Linux at run time (the e2e is POSIX; the code is portable and GCC compiles it). Ctrl-C landing *during* the graph's own parse at a real terminal: in-process the pass's cancellation between files is held by a token, and the chat's by a `SIGINT` while chunks are indexed -- the same forget either way. A folder over 500 files from machine mode or any pipe: refused by 26d's size guard before any graph is considered, so `lib/src/cli/source` (554 files) can be attached only where someone can answer. The graph's use on turns -- expansion and the scoped toolset are 27o's.

**Left for the owner.** Readings this item chose, each in the table and each a one-place change if vetoed: folders only (a glob or one file builds none); a folder's label its directory name, numbered on a collision; the line's numbers the folder's own part; Ctrl-C dropping the folder's parse cache with its graph; detach forgetting the folder's graph. Found on the way, out of this item's scope: machine mode's `json_reporter` serialises each answer delta with `nlohmann::json::dump()`, which throws on a delta that splits a multi-byte UTF-8 character -- seen with the mock, which streams a reply in fixed byte chunks, echoing a system prompt holding a `—`; a real backend whose stream can split a code point would end the turn the same way.

### 2026-10-06 — `attachment-graph-turns` (backlog item 27o): the chat's graph reaches its turns, and the model walks it

**The shape it inherited.** 27n built a graphed folder's code graph into the chat's own index and nothing ever read it: the 2026-10-03 spike had measured three walls -- the attachments retrieval path returned (`package_attachments`) before any graph section was built, the one graph-resolution decision (`resolve_turn_graph`) is keyed on config collections the chat's index is not, and no surface set `graph_enabled` on an attachment turn. Its central judgment set this item's shape: the stress test (a model attached this repository inventing `lib/src/core/` and cycling) failed on *passive injection*, so the graph's value had to arrive through tools the model calls. 27l had left the seam -- `GraphToolsOptions::scope`, the toolset over an injected store with no selection arguments.

**What was built**

- [x] **The scoped toolset** (`tools/graph_nav`, `cli/attachment_graph`, `cli/chat`): while a graphed folder is attached, a tool-using chat offers 27l's four read-only tools -- `graph_query`, `graph_path`, `graph_explain`, `graph_neighbors`, the same names and the same one traversal core -- **scoped to the chat's own code graph**. `with_graph_scope` returns the registry with the four swapped for the scoped set (every other tool as it was; a registry without the toolset, `tools.disabled: [graph]`, returned unchanged), and the chat's `attachment_graph_tools` calls it over `attachment_graph_target` -- the index as a `graph::GraphTarget` named `attachments`, made from the chat's state and never a `graphs:` entry -- with `attachment_graph_note` in each description: the folders as the user named them, each with its member label, each file named relative to its folder, so 26g ranks the tools against a question about that code. The scoped registry's environment note adds when to reach for them (`scoped_graph_policy`, 26p's mechanism, read off the registry asking, so a toolset pin without them says nothing). The chat compares `ChatAttachments::graph_scope()` before every turn, on a terminal and in machine mode, and re-offers when it changes: the scoped set in when the first graphed folder settles, the unscoped set back when the last is detached; a suite's toolset pin narrows the scoped registry, never the unscoped one. Read-only and never gated, as 27l's set is; `complete`, whose one-shot store builds no graph (27n), offers the unscoped set as before.
- [x] **The chat's graph state** (`ChatAttachments::graph_scope`, `AttachmentGraphScope`, `GraphedFolder`): the index and its graphed folders while a recorded folder carries a graph label *and* the index holds a graph -- nullopt for chunk-only attachments, for a folder whose graph is absent, after the last graphed folder is detached, and for a missing index, which asking never creates. Equal scopes offer the same tools.
- [x] **The attachment turn's expansion** (`agentloop/rag`, `agentloop/graph_context`, `agentloop/attachments`, `embedstore/graph_search`): `for_turn` sets `RagTurn::graph_enabled` from `graph_scope`, so Milestone Y's expansion runs on an attachment turn -- **seeded from the excerpt hits**: the same retrieval-ordered top-k, taken before the judge, named to the code graph by their chunks' content hash and line range (`code_excerpt_refs`) -- a file's chunks are keyed by the same SHA-256 of its bytes a code file's state records, so no path is mapped and every file of that content is found. `Store::code_nodes_in_excerpts` finds the functions and classes an excerpt states (those starting within its lines, and the innermost one holding its first line; files, modules and unresolved names never) and `graph_expand_excerpts` walks from them -- never re-listing them, as a chunk's mentions are never re-listed, their code being in front of the model -- with the question's words seeding through the entity index as on any lexical or hybrid turn; every expansion is now one private walk (`expand_from`). `build_graph_section_excerpts` renders it under the same 1,500-codepoint section budget and the graph knobs' defaults (one hop, eight entities). `package_attachments` renders the section **after the excerpts** in the same transient message and fits the pair to the retrieval share as the collection path does: the leading excerpts that fit beside it, else the section alone, framed on its own, else neither, both said.
- [x] **The line** (`operations/retrieval`): `describe_attachment_retrieval` ends with `+N graph entities` as a collection's line does -- `3 excerpts from the attachments, fair match (0.912 [lexical], 1 of 2 question words) +8 graph entities` -- and says nothing of a graph that injected none.
- [x] **The mock's `{{tool_names}}`** (`backends/mock`): the request's tool names, comma-separated -- what lets a scripted turn show which tools a chat offered.
- [x] **20 new Catch2 cases** (two in `embedstore/graph_code_test`, five in `agentloop/rag_test`, two in `agentloop/attachments_test`, one in `tools/graph_nav_test`, one in `cli/helpers_test`, five in `cli/chat_attachments_test`, three in `cli/chat_test`, one in `cli/graph_navigate_test`), and two extended: the mock's placeholders, and **27l's one-core golden extended to the scoped instance**.

**Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec's paths landed | The attachment turn's graph fields set in **`cli/chat_attachments::for_turn`**, where the attachment `RagTurn` is built (`cli/helpers.cpp` builds none; the collection's moved to `operations/retrieval` in A4); the excerpt-to-code read in **`embedstore`** beside 27l's reads; the scope's types, its target and the registry a chat offers with it (`attachment_graph_tools`) in **`cli/attachment_graph`** beside the pass; the swap in **`tools/graph_nav`** (`with_graph_scope`); tests in `tests/presentation/cli/` *(2026-10-06)* | The seams as the code stands, each package keeping what it owns. |
| How an excerpt seeds a code graph | **By content hash and lines** through the code file states (`kg_state.content_hash`), the functions and classes starting within it plus the innermost holding its first line -- never a file or a module -- walked from and never listed *(2026-10-06)* | A code mention is a line, not a chunk, so the chunk seeding Milestone Y uses finds nothing; the hash names the file with no path mapping (an excerpt's label is relative to where the chat was, a code file to its folder). A file or a namespace holds everything beside the excerpt, and a walk from one lists its contents rather than what the excerpt is about. |
| The scoped tools' names | **The same four names, replacing the unscoped set** in what the chat offers while a graphed folder is attached; restored when the last is detached *(2026-10-06)* | A registry's names are unique and 27l built the scope with no selection arguments, so the spec's "scoped `graph_*` tools" is a swap; two sets of near-identical tools would confuse a small model. The cost: in that chat the tools do not read named graphs (the CLI verbs and an `auto_rag` turn's expansion still do). |
| The scope's name | **`attachments`** -- the section header and every payload's `graph` *(2026-10-06)* | What the attachment turn's collection was already called (26d); one name for one graph. |
| The off switches | `tools.disabled: [graph]` **switches the scoped set off too**; a suite's toolset pin narrows the scoped registry *(2026-10-06)* | The scope is the same toolset under the same switch -- never a way round the user's. |
| When the tools are said to the model | A **tool-use policy paragraph** in the environment note of the scoped registry only: a question about where the attached code defines or implements something, or how its parts connect, looked up in the graph before answering, and no path the graph or the excerpts do not show *(2026-10-06)* | Measured: offered but never mentioned, the tools went uncalled -- Qwen3-VL-8B and Llama 3.1 8B answered "where is retrieval implemented?" from the excerpts alone (the spike's passive-injection failure). 26p's mechanism, a capability and why, never an order: the model still decides, so 27l's divergence from Graphify (never forcing the graph) stands. |

| What makes a scope | **Both** a recorded graphed folder **and** an index holding a graph -- asked of the chat's state, never of the index's tables alone, and never creating an index by asking *(2026-10-06)* | A scope over an empty store would offer tools that answer "no graph built"; and code the index holds that no recorded folder owns -- what a quit mid-attach leaves until the next settle forgets it -- is never walked by a turn. |
